<h1 id="api">API v0.0.1</h1>

> Scroll down for code samples, example requests and responses. Select a language for code samples from the tabs above or the mobile navigation menu.

<h1 id="api-operatorservice">OperatorService</h1>

OperatorService API defines how Temporal SDKs and other clients interact with the Temporal server
 to perform administrative functions like registering a search attribute or a namespace.
 APIs in this file could be not compatible with Temporal Cloud, hence it's usage in SDKs should be limited by
 designated APIs that clearly state that they shouldn't be used by the main Application (Workflows & Activities) framework.

## ListNexusEndpoints

<a id="opIdListNexusEndpoints"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/api/v1/nexus/endpoints \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /api/v1/nexus/endpoints`

List all Nexus endpoints for the cluster, sorted by ID in ascending order. Set page_token in the request to the
 next_page_token field of the previous response to get the next page of results. An empty next_page_token
 indicates that there are no more results. During pagination, a newly added service with an ID lexicographically
 earlier than the previous page's last endpoint's ID may be missed.

<h3 id="listnexusendpoints-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pageSize|query|integer(int32)|false|none|
|nextPageToken|query|string(bytes)|false|To get the next page, pass in `ListNexusEndpointsResponse.next_page_token` from the previous page's<br> response, the token will be empty if there's no other page.<br> Note: the last page may be empty if the total number of endpoints registered is a multiple of the page size.|
|name|query|string|false|Name of the incoming endpoint to filter on - optional. Specifying this will result in zero or one results.<br> (-- api-linter: core::203::field-behavior-required=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: Not following linter rules. --)|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "nextPageToken": "string",
  "endpoints": [
    {
      "version": "string",
      "id": "string",
      "spec": {
        "name": "string",
        "description": {},
        "target": {
          "worker": {
            "namespace": "string",
            "taskQueue": "string"
          },
          "external": {
            "url": "string"
          }
        }
      },
      "createdTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "lastModifiedTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "urlPrefix": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "details": [
    {
      "@type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="listnexusendpoints-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[ListNexusEndpointsResponse](#schemalistnexusendpointsresponse)|
|default|Default|Default error response|[Status](#schemastatus)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## CreateNexusEndpoint

<a id="opIdCreateNexusEndpoint"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/api/v1/nexus/endpoints \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "spec": {
      "name": "string",
      "description": {},
      "target": {
        "worker": {
          "namespace": "string",
          "taskQueue": "string"
        },
        "external": {
          "url": "string"
        }
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/nexus/endpoints`

Create a Nexus endpoint. This will fail if an endpoint with the same name is already registered with a status of
 ALREADY_EXISTS.
 Returns the created endpoint with its initial version. You may use this version for subsequent updates.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "spec": {
    "name": "string",
    "description": {},
    "target": {
      "worker": {
        "namespace": "string",
        "taskQueue": "string"
      },
      "external": {
        "url": "string"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="createnexusendpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[CreateNexusEndpointRequest](#schemacreatenexusendpointrequest)|true|none|
|» spec|body|object|false|Endpoint definition to create.|
|» » name|body|string|false|Endpoint name, unique for this cluster. Must match `[a-zA-Z_][a-zA-Z0-9_]*`.<br> Renaming an endpoint breaks all workflow callers that reference this endpoint, causing operations to fail.|
|» » description|body|object|false|Markdown description serialized as a single JSON string.<br> If the Payload is encrypted, the UI and CLI may decrypt with the configured codec server endpoint.<br> By default, the server enforces a limit of 20,000 bytes for this entire payload.|
|» » target|body|object|false|Target to route requests to.|
|» » » worker|body|[EndpointTarget_Worker](#schemaendpointtarget_worker)|false|Target a worker polling on a Nexus task queue in a specific namespace.|
|» » » external|body|[EndpointTarget_External](#schemaendpointtarget_external)|false|Target an external server by URL.<br> At a later point, this will support providing credentials, in the meantime, an http.RoundTripper can be injected<br> into the server to modify the request.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "endpoint": {
    "version": "string",
    "id": "string",
    "spec": {
      "name": "string",
      "description": {},
      "target": {
        "worker": {
          "namespace": "string",
          "taskQueue": "string"
        },
        "external": {
          "url": "string"
        }
      }
    },
    "createdTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "lastModifiedTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "urlPrefix": "string"
  }
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "details": [
    {
      "@type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="createnexusendpoint-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[CreateNexusEndpointResponse](#schemacreatenexusendpointresponse)|
|default|Default|Default error response|[Status](#schemastatus)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## UpdateNexusEndpoint

<a id="opIdUpdateNexusEndpoint"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/api/v1/nexus/endpoints/string/update \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "id": "string",
    "version": "string",
    "spec": {
      "name": "string",
      "description": {},
      "target": {
        "worker": {
          "namespace": "string",
          "taskQueue": "string"
        },
        "external": {
          "url": "string"
        }
      }
    }
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/nexus/endpoints/{id}/update`

Optimistically update a Nexus endpoint based on provided version as obtained via the `GetNexusEndpoint` or
 `ListNexusEndpointResponse` APIs. This will fail with a status of FAILED_PRECONDITION if the version does not
 match.
 Returns the updated endpoint with its updated version. You may use this version for subsequent updates. You don't
 need to increment the version yourself. The server will increment the version for you after each update.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "version": "string",
  "spec": {
    "name": "string",
    "description": {},
    "target": {
      "worker": {
        "namespace": "string",
        "taskQueue": "string"
      },
      "external": {
        "url": "string"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

<h3 id="updatenexusendpoint-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|path|string|true|Server-generated unique endpoint ID.|
|body|body|[UpdateNexusEndpointRequest](#schemaupdatenexusendpointrequest)|true|none|
|» id|body|string|false|Server-generated unique endpoint ID.|
|» version|body|string|false|Data version for this endpoint. Must match current version.|
|» spec|body|[EndpointSpec](#schemaendpointspec)|false|Contains mutable fields for an Endpoint.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "endpoint": {
    "version": "string",
    "id": "string",
    "spec": {
      "name": "string",
      "description": {},
      "target": {
        "worker": {
          "namespace": "string",
          "taskQueue": "string"
        },
        "external": {
          "url": "string"
        }
      }
    },
    "createdTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "lastModifiedTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "urlPrefix": "string"
  }
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "details": [
    {
      "@type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="updatenexusendpoint-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[UpdateNexusEndpointResponse](#schemaupdatenexusendpointresponse)|
|default|Default|Default error response|[Status](#schemastatus)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

<h1 id="api-workflowservice">WorkflowService</h1>

WorkflowService API defines how Temporal SDKs and other clients interact with the Temporal server
 to create and interact with workflows and activities.

 Users are expected to call `StartWorkflowExecution` to create a new workflow execution.

 To drive workflows, a worker using a Temporal SDK must exist which regularly polls for workflow
 and activity tasks from the service. For each workflow task, the sdk must process the
 (incremental or complete) event history and respond back with any newly generated commands.

 For each activity task, the worker is expected to execute the user's code which implements that
 activity, responding with completion or failure.

`POST /api/v1/namespaces`

RegisterNamespace creates a new namespace which can be used as a container for all resources.

 A Namespace is a top level entity within Temporal, and is used as a container for resources

## PauseActivity

<a id="opIdPauseActivity"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/api/v1/namespaces/string/activities-deprecated/pause \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "namespace": "string",
    "execution": {
      "workflowId": "string",
      "runId": "string"
    },
    "identity": "string",
    "id": "string",
    "type": "string",
    "reason": "string",
    "requestId": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/activities-deprecated/pause`

PauseActivity pauses the execution of an activity specified by its ID or type.
 If there are multiple pending activities of the provided type - all of them will be paused

 Pausing an activity means:
 - If the activity is currently waiting for a retry or is running and subsequently fails,
   it will not be rescheduled until it is unpaused.
 - If the activity is already paused, calling this method will have no effect.
 - If the activity is running and finishes successfully, the activity will be completed.
 - If the activity is running and finishes with failure:
   * if there is no retry left - the activity will be completed.
   * if there are more retries left - the activity will be paused.
 For long-running activities:
 - activities in paused state will send a cancellation with "activity_paused" set to 'true' in response to 'RecordActivityTaskHeartbeat'.
 - The activity should respond to the cancellation accordingly.

 Returns a `NotFound` error if there is no pending activity with the provided ID or type
 This API will be deprecated soon and replaced with a newer PauseActivityExecution that is better named and
 structured to work well for standalone activities.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "execution": {
    "workflowId": "string",
    "runId": "string"
  },
  "identity": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "type": "string",
  "reason": "string",
  "requestId": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="pauseactivity-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace of the workflow which scheduled this activity.|
|body|body|[PauseActivityRequest](#schemapauseactivityrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|Namespace of the workflow which scheduled this activity.|
|» execution|body|object|false|Execution info of the workflow which scheduled this activity|
|» » workflowId|body|string|false|none|
|» » runId|body|string|false|none|
|» identity|body|string|false|The identity of the client who initiated this request.|
|» id|body|string|false|Only the activity with this ID will be paused.|
|» type|body|string|false|Pause all running activities of this type.<br> Note: Experimental - the behavior of pause by activity type might change in a future release.|
|» reason|body|string|false|Reason to pause the activity.|
|» requestId|body|string|false|Used to de-dupe pause requests.|

> Example responses

```json
{}
```

```json
  "message": "string",

    {
      "@type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

## ResetActivity

<a id="opIdResetActivity"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/api/v1/namespaces/string/activities-deprecated/reset \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "namespace": "string",
    "execution": {
      "workflowId": "string",
      "runId": "string"
    },
    "identity": "string",
    "id": "string",
    "type": "string",
    "matchAll": true,
    "resetHeartbeat": true,
    "keepPaused": true,
    "jitter": "string",
    "restoreOriginalOptions": true
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/activities-deprecated/reset`

ResetActivity resets the execution of an activity specified by its ID or type.
 If there are multiple pending activities of the provided type - all of them will be reset.

 Resetting an activity means:
 * number of attempts will be reset to 0.
 * activity timeouts will be reset.
 * if the activity is waiting for retry, and it is not paused or 'keep_paused' is not provided:
    it will be scheduled immediately (* see 'jitter' flag),

 Flags:

 'jitter': the activity will be scheduled at a random time within the jitter duration.
 If the activity currently paused it will be unpaused, unless 'keep_paused' flag is provided.
 'reset_heartbeats': the activity heartbeat timer and heartbeats will be reset.
 'keep_paused': if the activity is paused, it will remain paused.

 Returns a `NotFound` error if there is no pending activity with the provided ID or type.
 This API will be deprecated soon and replaced with a newer ResetActivityExecution that is better named and
 structured to work well for standalone activities.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "execution": {
    "workflowId": "string",
    "runId": "string"
  },
  "identity": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "type": "string",
  "matchAll": true,
  "resetHeartbeat": true,
  "keepPaused": true,
  "jitter": "string",
  "restoreOriginalOptions": true
}
```

<h3 id="resetactivity-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace of the workflow which scheduled this activity.|
|body|body|[ResetActivityRequest](#schemaresetactivityrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|Namespace of the workflow which scheduled this activity.|
|» execution|body|object|false|Execution info of the workflow which scheduled this activity|
|» » workflowId|body|string|false|none|
|» » runId|body|string|false|none|
|» identity|body|string|false|The identity of the client who initiated this request.|
|» id|body|string|false|Only activity with this ID will be reset.|
|» type|body|string|false|Reset all running activities with of this type.|
|» matchAll|body|boolean|false|Reset all running activities.|
|» resetHeartbeat|body|boolean|false|Indicates that activity should reset heartbeat details.<br> This flag will be applied only to the new instance of the activity.|
|» keepPaused|body|boolean|false|If activity is paused, it will remain paused after reset|
|» jitter|body|string|false|If set, and activity is in backoff, the activity will start at a random time within the specified jitter duration.<br> (unless it is paused and keep_paused is set)|
|» restoreOriginalOptions|body|boolean|false|If set, the activity options will be restored to the defaults.<br> Default options are then options activity was created with.<br> They are part of the first schedule event.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

```json
  "message": "string",
  "details": [
    {
      "@type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

## UnpauseActivity

<a id="opIdUnpauseActivity"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/api/v1/namespaces/string/activities-deprecated/unpause \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "namespace": "string",
    "execution": {
      "workflowId": "string",
      "runId": "string"
    },
    "identity": "string",
    "id": "string",
    "type": "string",
    "unpauseAll": true,
    "resetAttempts": true,
    "resetHeartbeat": true,
    "jitter": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/activities-deprecated/unpause`

UnpauseActivity unpauses the execution of an activity specified by its ID or type.
 If there are multiple pending activities of the provided type - all of them will be unpaused.

 If activity is not paused, this call will have no effect.
 If the activity was paused while waiting for retry, it will be scheduled immediately (* see 'jitter' flag).
 Once the activity is unpaused, all timeout timers will be regenerated.

 Flags:
 'jitter': the activity will be scheduled at a random time within the jitter duration.
 'reset_attempts': the number of attempts will be reset.
 'reset_heartbeat': the activity heartbeat timer and heartbeats will be reset.

 Returns a `NotFound` error if there is no pending activity with the provided ID or type
 This API will be deprecated soon and replaced with a newer UnpauseActivityExecution that is better named and
 structured to work well for standalone activities.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "execution": {
    "workflowId": "string",
    "runId": "string"
  },
  "identity": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "type": "string",
  "unpauseAll": true,
```

`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/activities-deprecated/update-options`

UpdateActivityOptions is called by the client to update the options of an activity by its ID or type.
 If there are multiple pending activities of the provided type - all of them will be updated.
 This API will be deprecated soon and replaced with a newer UpdateActivityExecutionOptions that is better named and
 structured to work well for standalone activities.

> Body parameter

```json
  "execution": {

    "runId": "string"
  },
  "identity": "string",
  "activityOptions": {

        "string"
      ]
    },

    }
  },

  "matchAll": true,

}
```

<h3 id="updateactivityoptions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace of the workflow which scheduled this activity|
|body|body|[UpdateActivityOptionsRequest](#schemaupdateactivityoptionsrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|Namespace of the workflow which scheduled this activity|
|» execution|body|object|false|Execution info of the workflow which scheduled this activity|
|» » workflowId|body|string|false|none|
|» » runId|body|string|false|none|
|» identity|body|string|false|The identity of the client who initiated this request|
|» activityOptions|body|object|false|Activity options. Partial updates are accepted and controlled by update_mask|
|» » taskQueue|body|[TaskQueue](#schemataskqueue)|false|See https://docs.temporal.io/docs/concepts/task-queues/|
|» » scheduleToCloseTimeout|body|string|false|Indicates how long the caller is willing to wait for an activity completion. Limits how long<br> retries will be attempted. Either this or `start_to_close_timeout` must be specified.<br><br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "to" is used to indicate interval. --)|
|» » scheduleToStartTimeout|body|string|false|Limits time an activity task can stay in a task queue before a worker picks it up. This<br> timeout is always non retryable, as all a retry would achieve is to put it back into the same<br> queue. Defaults to `schedule_to_close_timeout` or workflow execution timeout if not<br> specified.<br><br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "to" is used to indicate interval. --)|
|» » startToCloseTimeout|body|string|false|Maximum time an activity is allowed to execute after being picked up by a worker. This<br> timeout is always retryable. Either this or `schedule_to_close_timeout` must be<br> specified.<br><br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "to" is used to indicate interval. --)|
|» » heartbeatTimeout|body|string|false|Maximum permitted time between successful worker heartbeats.|
|» » retryPolicy|body|object|false|The retry policy for the activity. Will never exceed `schedule_to_close_timeout`.|
|» » » initialInterval|body|string|false|Interval of the first retry. If retryBackoffCoefficient is 1.0 then it is used for all retries.|
|» » » backoffCoefficient|body|number(double)|false|Coefficient used to calculate the next retry interval.<br> The next retry interval is previous interval multiplied by the coefficient.<br> Must be 1 or larger.|
|» » » maximumInterval|body|string|false|Maximum interval between retries. Exponential backoff leads to interval increase.<br> This value is the cap of the increase. Default is 100x of the initial interval.|
|» » » maximumAttempts|body|integer(int32)|false|Maximum number of attempts. When exceeded the retries stop even if not expired yet.<br> 1 disables retries. 0 means unlimited (up to the timeouts)|
|» » » nonRetryableErrorTypes|body|[string]|false|Non-Retryable errors types. Will stop retrying if the error type matches this list. Note that<br> this is not a substring match, the error *type* (not message) must match exactly.|
|» » priority|body|object|false|Priority metadata. If this message is not present, or any fields are not<br> present, they inherit the values from the workflow.|
|» » » priorityKey|body|integer(int32)|false|Priority key is a positive integer from 1 to n, where smaller integers<br> correspond to higher priorities (tasks run sooner). In general, tasks in<br> a queue should be processed in close to priority order, although small<br> deviations are possible.<br><br> The maximum priority value (minimum priority) is determined by server<br> configuration, and defaults to 5.<br><br> If priority is not present (or zero), then the effective priority will be<br> the default priority, which is calculated by (min+max)/2. With the<br> default max of 5, and min of 1, that comes out to 3.|
|» » » fairnessKey|body|string|false|Fairness key is a short string that's used as a key for a fairness<br> balancing mechanism. It may correspond to a tenant id, or to a fixed<br> string like "high" or "low". The default is the empty string.<br><br> The fairness mechanism attempts to dispatch tasks for a given key in<br> proportion to its weight. For example, using a thousand distinct tenant<br> ids, each with a weight of 1.0 (the default) will result in each tenant<br> getting a roughly equal share of task dispatch throughput.<br><br> (Note: this does not imply equal share of worker capacity! Fairness<br> decisions are made based on queue statistics, not<br> current worker load.)<br><br> As another example, using keys "high" and "low" with weight 9.0 and 1.0<br> respectively will prefer dispatching "high" tasks over "low" tasks at a<br> 9:1 ratio, while allowing either key to use all worker capacity if the<br> other is not present.<br><br> All fairness mechanisms, including rate limits, are best-effort and<br> probabilistic. The results may not match what a "perfect" algorithm with<br> infinite resources would produce. The more unique keys are used, the less<br> accurate the results will be.<br><br> Fairness keys are limited to 64 bytes.|
|» » » fairnessWeight|body|number(float)|false|Fairness weight for a task can come from multiple sources for<br> flexibility. From highest to lowest precedence:<br> 1. Weights for a small set of keys can be overridden in task queue<br>    configuration with an API.<br> 2. It can be attached to the workflow/activity in this field.<br> 3. The default weight of 1.0 will be used.<br><br> Weight values are clamped to the range [0.001, 1000].|
|» updateMask|body|string(field-mask)|false|Controls which fields from `activity_options` will be applied|
|» id|body|string|false|Only activity with this ID will be updated.|
|» type|body|string|false|Update all running activities of this type.|
|» matchAll|body|boolean|false|Update all running activities.|
|» restoreOriginal|body|boolean|false|If set, the activity options will be restored to the default.<br> Default options are then options activity was created with.<br> They are part of the first schedule event.<br> This flag cannot be combined with any other option; if you supply<br> restore_original together with other options, the request will be rejected.|

## DescribeActivityExecution

<a id="opIdDescribeActivityExecution"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/api/v1/namespaces/string/activities/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/activities/{activityId}`

DescribeActivityExecution returns information about an activity execution.
 It can be used to:
 - Get current activity info without waiting
 - Long-poll for next state change and return new activity info
 Response can optionally include activity input or outcome (if the activity has completed).

<h3 id="describeactivityexecution-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|activityId|path|string|true|none|
|runId|query|string|false|Activity run ID. If empty the request targets the latest run.|
|includeInput|query|boolean|false|Include the input field in the response.|
|includeOutcome|query|boolean|false|Include the outcome (result/failure) in the response if the activity has completed.|
|longPollToken|query|string(bytes)|false|Token from a previous DescribeActivityExecutionResponse. If present, long-poll until activity<br> state changes from the state encoded in this token. If absent, return current state immediately.<br> If present, run_id must also be present.<br> Note that activity state may change multiple times between requests, therefore it is not<br> guaranteed that a client making a sequence of long-poll requests will see a complete<br> sequence of state changes.|

|» activityType|body|object|false|The type of the activity, a string that corresponds to a registered activity on a worker.|
|» » name|body|string|false|none|

|» » name|body|string|false|none|

|» » normalName|body|string|false|Iff kind == TASK_QUEUE_KIND_STICKY, then this field contains the name of<br> the normal task queue that the sticky worker is running on.|
|» scheduleToCloseTimeout|body|string|false|Indicates how long the caller is willing to wait for an activity completion. Limits how long<br> retries will be attempted. Either this or `start_to_close_timeout` must be specified.<br><br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "to" is used to indicate interval. --)|
|» scheduleToStartTimeout|body|string|false|Limits time an activity task can stay in a task queue before a worker picks it up. This<br> timeout is always non retryable, as all a retry would achieve is to put it back into the same<br> queue. Defaults to `schedule_to_close_timeout` if not specified.<br><br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "to" is used to indicate interval. --)|
|» startToCloseTimeout|body|string|false|Maximum time an activity is allowed to execute after being picked up by a worker. This<br> timeout is always retryable. Either this or `schedule_to_close_timeout` must be<br> specified.<br><br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "to" is used to indicate interval. --)|
|» heartbeatTimeout|body|string|false|Maximum permitted time between successful worker heartbeats.|
|» retryPolicy|body|object|false|The retry policy for the activity. Will never exceed `schedule_to_close_timeout`.|
|» » initialInterval|body|string|false|Interval of the first retry. If retryBackoffCoefficient is 1.0 then it is used for all retries.|
|» » backoffCoefficient|body|number(double)|false|Coefficient used to calculate the next retry interval.<br> The next retry interval is previous interval multiplied by the coefficient.<br> Must be 1 or larger.|
|» » maximumInterval|body|string|false|Maximum interval between retries. Exponential backoff leads to interval increase.<br> This value is the cap of the increase. Default is 100x of the initial interval.|
|» » maximumAttempts|body|integer(int32)|false|Maximum number of attempts. When exceeded the retries stop even if not expired yet.<br> 1 disables retries. 0 means unlimited (up to the timeouts)|
|» » nonRetryableErrorTypes|body|[string]|false|Non-Retryable errors types. Will stop retrying if the error type matches this list. Note that<br> this is not a substring match, the error *type* (not message) must match exactly.|
|» input|body|object|false|Serialized arguments to the activity. These are passed as arguments to the activity function.|
|» » payloads|body|[[Payload](#schemapayload)]|false|none|
|» idReusePolicy|body|string(enum)|false|Defines whether to allow re-using the activity id from a previously *closed* activity.<br> The default policy is ACTIVITY_ID_REUSE_POLICY_ALLOW_DUPLICATE.|
|» idConflictPolicy|body|string(enum)|false|Defines how to resolve an activity id conflict with a *running* activity.<br> The default policy is ACTIVITY_ID_CONFLICT_POLICY_FAIL.|
|» searchAttributes|body|object|false|Search attributes for indexing.|
|» » indexedFields|body|object|false|none|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|[Payload](#schemapayload)|false|Represents some binary (byte array) data (ex: activity input parameters or workflow result) with<br> metadata which describes this binary data (format, encoding, encryption, etc). Serialization<br> of the data may be user-defined.|
|» header|body|object|false|Header for context propagation and tracing purposes.|
|» » fields|body|object|false|none|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|[Payload](#schemapayload)|false|Represents some binary (byte array) data (ex: activity input parameters or workflow result) with<br> metadata which describes this binary data (format, encoding, encryption, etc). Serialization<br> of the data may be user-defined.|
|» userMetadata|body|object|false|Metadata for use by user interfaces to display the fixed as-of-start summary and details of the activity.|
|» » summary|body|object|false|Short-form text that provides a summary. This payload should be a "json/plain"-encoded payload<br> that is a single JSON string for use in user interfaces. User interface formatting may not<br> apply to this text when used in "title" situations. The payload data section is limited to 400<br> bytes by default.|
|» » details|body|object|false|Long-form text that provides details. This payload should be a "json/plain"-encoded payload<br> that is a single JSON string for use in user interfaces. User interface formatting may apply to<br> this text in common use. The payload data section is limited to 20000 bytes by default.|
|» priority|body|object|false|Priority metadata.|
|» » priorityKey|body|integer(int32)|false|Priority key is a positive integer from 1 to n, where smaller integers<br> correspond to higher priorities (tasks run sooner). In general, tasks in<br> a queue should be processed in close to priority order, although small<br> deviations are possible.<br><br> The maximum priority value (minimum priority) is determined by server<br> configuration, and defaults to 5.<br><br> If priority is not present (or zero), then the effective priority will be<br> the default priority, which is calculated by (min+max)/2. With the<br> default max of 5, and min of 1, that comes out to 3.|
|» » fairnessKey|body|string|false|Fairness key is a short string that's used as a key for a fairness<br> balancing mechanism. It may correspond to a tenant id, or to a fixed<br> string like "high" or "low". The default is the empty string.<br><br> The fairness mechanism attempts to dispatch tasks for a given key in<br> proportion to its weight. For example, using a thousand distinct tenant<br> ids, each with a weight of 1.0 (the default) will result in each tenant<br> getting a roughly equal share of task dispatch throughput.<br><br> (Note: this does not imply equal share of worker capacity! Fairness<br> decisions are made based on queue statistics, not<br> current worker load.)<br><br> As another example, using keys "high" and "low" with weight 9.0 and 1.0<br> respectively will prefer dispatching "high" tasks over "low" tasks at a<br> 9:1 ratio, while allowing either key to use all worker capacity if the<br> other is not present.<br><br> All fairness mechanisms, including rate limits, are best-effort and<br> probabilistic. The results may not match what a "perfect" algorithm with<br> infinite resources would produce. The more unique keys are used, the less<br> accurate the results will be.<br><br> Fairness keys are limited to 64 bytes.|
|» » fairnessWeight|body|number(float)|false|Fairness weight for a task can come from multiple sources for<br> flexibility. From highest to lowest precedence:<br> 1. Weights for a small set of keys can be overridden in task queue<br>    configuration with an API.<br> 2. It can be attached to the workflow/activity in this field.<br> 3. The default weight of 1.0 will be used.<br><br> Weight values are clamped to the range [0.001, 1000].|
|» completionCallbacks|body|[[Callback](#schemacallback)]|false|Callbacks to be called by the server when this activity reaches a terminal state.<br> Callback addresses must be whitelisted in the server's dynamic configuration.|
|» links|body|[[Link](#schemalink)]|false|Links to be associated with the activity. Callbacks may also have associated links;<br> links already included with a callback should not be duplicated here.|
|» onConflictOptions|body|object|false|Options for handling conflicts when using ACTIVITY_ID_CONFLICT_POLICY_USE_EXISTING.|
|» » attachRequestId|body|boolean|false|Attaches the request ID to the running execution.|
|» » attachCompletionCallbacks|body|boolean|false|Attaches the completion callbacks to the running execution.|
|» » attachLinks|body|boolean|false|Attaches the links to the running execution.|
|» startDelay|body|string|false|Time to wait before dispatching the first activity task. This delay is not applied to retry attempts.|

## RequestCancelActivityExecution

<a id="opIdRequestCancelActivityExecution"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/api/v1/namespaces/string/activities/string/cancel \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "namespace": "string",
    "activityId": "string",
    "runId": "string",
    "identity": "string",
    "requestId": "string",
    "reason": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/activities/{activityId}/cancel`

RequestCancelActivityExecution requests cancellation of an activity execution.

 Cancellation is cooperative: this call records the request, but the activity must detect and
 acknowledge it for the activity to reach CANCELED status. The cancellation signal is
 delivered via `cancel_requested` in the heartbeat response; SDKs surface this via
 language-idiomatic mechanisms (context cancellation, exceptions, abort signals).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "activityId": "string",
  "runId": "string",
  "identity": "string",
  "requestId": "string",
  "reason": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="requestcancelactivityexecution-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|activityId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[RequestCancelActivityExecutionRequest](#schemarequestcancelactivityexecutionrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|none|
|» activityId|body|string|false|none|
|» runId|body|string|false|Activity run ID, targets the latest run if run_id is empty.|
|» identity|body|string|false|The identity of the worker/client.|
|» requestId|body|string|false|Used to de-dupe cancellation requests.|
|» reason|body|string|false|Reason for requesting the cancellation, recorded and available via the PollActivityExecution API.<br> Not propagated to a worker if an activity attempt is currently running.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "details": [
    {
      "@type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="requestcancelactivityexecution-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[RequestCancelActivityExecutionResponse](#schemarequestcancelactivityexecutionresponse)|
|default|Default|Default error response|[Status](#schemastatus)|

This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## PauseActivityExecution

<a id="opIdPauseActivityExecution"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/api/v1/namespaces/string/activities/string/pause \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "namespace": "string",
    "workflowId": "string",
    "activityId": "string",
    "runId": "string",
    "identity": "string",
    "reason": "string",
    "resourceId": "string",
    "requestId": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/activities/{activityId}/pause`

PauseActivityExecution pauses the execution of an activity specified by its ID.
 This API can be used to target a workflow activity or a standalone activity

 Pausing an activity means:
 - If the activity is currently waiting for a retry or is running and subsequently fails,
   it will not be rescheduled until it is unpaused.
 - If the activity is already paused, calling this method will have no effect.
 - If the activity is running and finishes successfully, the activity will be completed.
 - If the activity is running and finishes with failure:
   * if there is no retry left - the activity will be completed.
   * if there are more retries left - the activity will be paused.
 For long-running activities:
 - activities in paused state will send a cancellation with "activity_paused" set to 'true' in response to 'RecordActivityTaskHeartbeat'.

 Returns a `NotFound` error if there is no pending activity with the provided ID

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "workflowId": "string",
  "activityId": "string",
  "runId": "string",
  "identity": "string",
  "reason": "string",
  "resourceId": "string",
  "requestId": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="pauseactivityexecution-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace of the workflow which scheduled this activity.|
|activityId|path|string|true|The ID of the activity to target.|
|body|body|[PauseActivityExecutionRequest](#schemapauseactivityexecutionrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|Namespace of the workflow which scheduled this activity.|
|» workflowId|body|string|false|If provided, pause a workflow activity (or activities) for the given workflow ID.<br> If empty, targets a standalone activity.|
|» activityId|body|string|false|The ID of the activity to target.|
|» runId|body|string|false|Run ID of the workflow or standalone activity.|
|» identity|body|string|false|The identity of the client who initiated this request.|
|» reason|body|string|false|Reason to pause the activity.|
|» resourceId|body|string|false|Resource ID for routing. Contains "workflow:{workflow_id}" for workflow activities or "activity:{activity_id}" for standalone activities.|
|» requestId|body|string|false|Used to de-dupe pause requests.|

> Example responses

```json
{}
```

```json
  "message": "string",

    }
  ]
}
```

## ResetActivityExecution

<a id="opIdResetActivityExecution"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/api/v1/namespaces/string/activities/string/reset \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "namespace": "string",
    "workflowId": "string",
    "activityId": "string",
    "runId": "string",
    "identity": "string",
    "resetHeartbeat": true,
    "keepPaused": true,
    "jitter": "string",
    "restoreOriginalOptions": true,
    "resourceId": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/activities/{activityId}/reset`

ResetActivityExecution resets the execution of an activity specified by its ID.
 This API can be used to target a workflow activity or a standalone activity.

 Resetting an activity means:
 * number of attempts will be reset to 0.
 * activity timeouts will be reset.
 * if the activity is waiting for retry, and it is not paused or 'keep_paused' is not provided:
    it will be scheduled immediately (* see 'jitter' flag)

 Returns a `NotFound` error if there is no pending activity with the provided ID or type.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "workflowId": "string",
  "activityId": "string",
  "runId": "string",
  "identity": "string",
  "resetHeartbeat": true,
  "keepPaused": true,
  "jitter": "string",
  "restoreOriginalOptions": true,
  "resourceId": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="resetactivityexecution-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace of the workflow which scheduled this activity.|
|activityId|path|string|true|The ID of the activity to target.|
|body|body|[ResetActivityExecutionRequest](#schemaresetactivityexecutionrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|Namespace of the workflow which scheduled this activity.|
|» workflowId|body|string|false|If provided, targets a workflow activity for the given workflow ID.<br> If empty, targets a standalone activity.|
|» activityId|body|string|false|The ID of the activity to target.|
|» runId|body|string|false|Run ID of the workflow or standalone activity.|
|» identity|body|string|false|The identity of the client who initiated this request.|
|» resetHeartbeat|body|boolean|false|Indicates that activity should reset heartbeat details.<br> This flag will be applied only to the new instance of the activity.|
|» keepPaused|body|boolean|false|If activity is paused, it will remain paused after reset|
|» jitter|body|string|false|If set, and activity is in backoff, the activity will start at a random time within the specified jitter duration.<br> (unless it is paused and keep_paused is set)|
|» restoreOriginalOptions|body|boolean|false|If set, the activity options will be restored to the defaults.<br> Default options are then options activity was created with.<br> They are part of the first schedule event.|
|» resourceId|body|string|false|Resource ID for routing. Contains "workflow:{workflow_id}" for workflow activities or "activity:{activity_id}" for standalone activities.|

> Example responses

```json
{}
```

```json
  "message": "string",
  "details": [
    {
      "@type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

```bash
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "namespace": "string",
    "activityId": "string",
    "runId": "string",
    "identity": "string",
    "requestId": "string",
    "reason": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/activities/{activityId}/terminate`

TerminateActivityExecution terminates an existing activity execution immediately.

 Termination does not reach the worker and the activity code cannot react to it. A terminated activity may have a
 running attempt.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "activityId": "string",
  "runId": "string",
  "identity": "string",
  "requestId": "string",
  "reason": "string"
}
```

|body|body|[TerminateActivityExecutionRequest](#schematerminateactivityexecutionrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|none|
|» activityId|body|string|false|none|
|» runId|body|string|false|Activity run ID, targets the latest run if run_id is empty.|
|» identity|body|string|false|The identity of the worker/client.|
|» requestId|body|string|false|Used to de-dupe termination requests.|
|» reason|body|string|false|Reason for requesting the termination, recorded in in the activity's result failure outcome.|

## UnpauseActivityExecution

<a id="opIdUnpauseActivityExecution"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/api/v1/namespaces/string/activities/string/unpause \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "namespace": "string",
    "workflowId": "string",
    "activityId": "string",
    "runId": "string",
    "identity": "string",
    "resetAttempts": true,
    "resetHeartbeat": true,
    "reason": "string",
    "jitter": "string",
    "resourceId": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/activities/{activityId}/unpause`

UnpauseActivityExecution unpauses the execution of an activity specified by its ID.
 This API can be used to target a workflow activity or a standalone activity.

 If activity is not paused, this call will have no effect.
 If the activity was paused while waiting for retry, it will be scheduled immediately (* see 'jitter' flag).
 Once the activity is unpaused, all timeout timers will be regenerated.

 Returns a `NotFound` error if there is no pending activity with the provided ID

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "workflowId": "string",
  "activityId": "string",
  "runId": "string",
  "identity": "string",
  "resetAttempts": true,
  "resetHeartbeat": true,
  "reason": "string",
  "jitter": "string",
  "resourceId": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="unpauseactivityexecution-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace of the workflow which scheduled this activity.|
|activityId|path|string|true|The ID of the activity to target.|
|body|body|[UnpauseActivityExecutionRequest](#schemaunpauseactivityexecutionrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|Namespace of the workflow which scheduled this activity.|
|» workflowId|body|string|false|If provided, targets a workflow activity for the given workflow ID.<br> If empty, targets a standalone activity.|
|» activityId|body|string|false|The ID of the activity to target.|
|» runId|body|string|false|Run ID of the workflow or standalone activity.|
|» identity|body|string|false|The identity of the client who initiated this request.|
|» resetAttempts|body|boolean|false|Providing this flag will also reset the number of attempts.|
|» resetHeartbeat|body|boolean|false|Providing this flag will also reset the heartbeat details.|
|» reason|body|string|false|Reason to unpause the activity.|
|» jitter|body|string|false|If set, the activity will start at a random time within the specified jitter duration.|
|» resourceId|body|string|false|Resource ID for routing. Contains "workflow:{workflow_id}" for workflow activities or "activity:{activity_id}" for standalone activities.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "details": [
    {
      "@type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="unpauseactivityexecution-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[UnpauseActivityExecutionResponse](#schemaunpauseactivityexecutionresponse)|
|default|Default|Default error response|[Status](#schemastatus)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication

```bash
      ]
    },

    }
  },

  "restoreOriginal": true,
```

```json
}
```

<h3 id="updateactivityexecutionoptions-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace of the workflow which scheduled this activity|
|activityId|path|string|true|The ID of the activity to target.|
|body|body|[UpdateActivityExecutionOptionsRequest](#schemaupdateactivityexecutionoptionsrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|Namespace of the workflow which scheduled this activity|
|» workflowId|body|string|false|If provided, targets a workflow activity for the given workflow ID.<br> If empty, targets a standalone activity.|
|» activityId|body|string|false|The ID of the activity to target.|
|» runId|body|string|false|Run ID of the workflow or standalone activity.|
|» identity|body|string|false|The identity of the client who initiated this request|
|» activityOptions|body|object|false|Activity options. Partial updates are accepted and controlled by update_mask|
|» » taskQueue|body|[TaskQueue](#schemataskqueue)|false|See https://docs.temporal.io/docs/concepts/task-queues/|
|» » scheduleToCloseTimeout|body|string|false|Indicates how long the caller is willing to wait for an activity completion. Limits how long<br> retries will be attempted. Either this or `start_to_close_timeout` must be specified.<br><br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "to" is used to indicate interval. --)|
|» » scheduleToStartTimeout|body|string|false|Limits time an activity task can stay in a task queue before a worker picks it up. This<br> timeout is always non retryable, as all a retry would achieve is to put it back into the same<br> queue. Defaults to `schedule_to_close_timeout` or workflow execution timeout if not<br> specified.<br><br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "to" is used to indicate interval. --)|
|» » startToCloseTimeout|body|string|false|Maximum time an activity is allowed to execute after being picked up by a worker. This<br> timeout is always retryable. Either this or `schedule_to_close_timeout` must be<br> specified.<br><br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "to" is used to indicate interval. --)|
|» » heartbeatTimeout|body|string|false|Maximum permitted time between successful worker heartbeats.|
|» » retryPolicy|body|object|false|The retry policy for the activity. Will never exceed `schedule_to_close_timeout`.|
|» » » initialInterval|body|string|false|Interval of the first retry. If retryBackoffCoefficient is 1.0 then it is used for all retries.|
|» » » backoffCoefficient|body|number(double)|false|Coefficient used to calculate the next retry interval.<br> The next retry interval is previous interval multiplied by the coefficient.<br> Must be 1 or larger.|
|» » » maximumInterval|body|string|false|Maximum interval between retries. Exponential backoff leads to interval increase.<br> This value is the cap of the increase. Default is 100x of the initial interval.|
|» » » maximumAttempts|body|integer(int32)|false|Maximum number of attempts. When exceeded the retries stop even if not expired yet.<br> 1 disables retries. 0 means unlimited (up to the timeouts)|
|» » » nonRetryableErrorTypes|body|[string]|false|Non-Retryable errors types. Will stop retrying if the error type matches this list. Note that<br> this is not a substring match, the error *type* (not message) must match exactly.|
|» » priority|body|object|false|Priority metadata. If this message is not present, or any fields are not<br> present, they inherit the values from the workflow.|
|» » » priorityKey|body|integer(int32)|false|Priority key is a positive integer from 1 to n, where smaller integers<br> correspond to higher priorities (tasks run sooner). In general, tasks in<br> a queue should be processed in close to priority order, although small<br> deviations are possible.<br><br> The maximum priority value (minimum priority) is determined by server<br> configuration, and defaults to 5.<br><br> If priority is not present (or zero), then the effective priority will be<br> the default priority, which is calculated by (min+max)/2. With the<br> default max of 5, and min of 1, that comes out to 3.|
|» » » fairnessKey|body|string|false|Fairness key is a short string that's used as a key for a fairness<br> balancing mechanism. It may correspond to a tenant id, or to a fixed<br> string like "high" or "low". The default is the empty string.<br><br> The fairness mechanism attempts to dispatch tasks for a given key in<br> proportion to its weight. For example, using a thousand distinct tenant<br> ids, each with a weight of 1.0 (the default) will result in each tenant<br> getting a roughly equal share of task dispatch throughput.<br><br> (Note: this does not imply equal share of worker capacity! Fairness<br> decisions are made based on queue statistics, not<br> current worker load.)<br><br> As another example, using keys "high" and "low" with weight 9.0 and 1.0<br> respectively will prefer dispatching "high" tasks over "low" tasks at a<br> 9:1 ratio, while allowing either key to use all worker capacity if the<br> other is not present.<br><br> All fairness mechanisms, including rate limits, are best-effort and<br> probabilistic. The results may not match what a "perfect" algorithm with<br> infinite resources would produce. The more unique keys are used, the less<br> accurate the results will be.<br><br> Fairness keys are limited to 64 bytes.|
|» » » fairnessWeight|body|number(float)|false|Fairness weight for a task can come from multiple sources for<br> flexibility. From highest to lowest precedence:<br> 1. Weights for a small set of keys can be overridden in task queue<br>    configuration with an API.<br> 2. It can be attached to the workflow/activity in this field.<br> 3. The default weight of 1.0 will be used.<br><br> Weight values are clamped to the range [0.001, 1000].|
|» updateMask|body|string(field-mask)|false|Controls which fields from `activity_options` will be applied|
|» restoreOriginal|body|boolean|false|If set, the activity options will be restored to the default.<br> Default options are then options activity was created with.<br> They are part of the first schedule event.<br> This flag cannot be combined with any other option; if you supply<br> restore_original together with other options, the request will be rejected.|
|» resourceId|body|string|false|Resource ID for routing. Contains "workflow:{workflow_id}" for workflow activities or "activity:{activity_id}" for standalone activities.|

`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/activity-complete`

RespondActivityTaskCompleted is called by workers when they successfully complete an activity
 task.

 For workflow activities, this results in a new `ACTIVITY_TASK_COMPLETED` event being written to the workflow history
 and a new workflow task created for the workflow. Fails with `NotFound` if the task token is
 no longer valid due to activity timeout, already being completed, or never having existed.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "taskToken": "string",
  "result": {
    "payloads": [
      null
    ]
  },
  "identity": "string",
  "namespace": "string",
  "resourceId": "string",
  "workerVersion": {
    "buildId": "string",
    "useVersioning": true
  },
  "deployment": {
    "seriesName": "string",
    "buildId": "string"
  },
  "deploymentOptions": {
    "deploymentName": "string",
    "buildId": "string",
    "workerVersioningMode": "WORKER_VERSIONING_MODE_UNSPECIFIED"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="respondactivitytaskcompleted-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[RespondActivityTaskCompletedRequest](#schemarespondactivitytaskcompletedrequest)|true|none|
|» taskToken|body|string(bytes)|false|The task token as received in `PollActivityTaskQueueResponse`|
|» result|body|object|false|The result of successfully executing the activity|
|» » payloads|body|[[Payload](#schemapayload)]|false|none|
|» identity|body|string|false|The identity of the worker/client|
|» namespace|body|string|false|none|
|» resourceId|body|string|false|Resource ID for routing. Contains the workflow ID or activity ID for standalone activities.|
|» workerVersion|body|object|false|Version info of the worker who processed this task. This message's `build_id` field should<br> always be set by SDKs. Workers opting into versioning will also set the `use_versioning`<br> field to true. See message docstrings for more.<br> Deprecated. Use `deployment_options` instead.|
|» » buildId|body|string|false|An opaque whole-worker identifier. Replaces the deprecated `binary_checksum` field when this<br> message is included in requests which previously used that.|
|» » useVersioning|body|boolean|false|If set, the worker is opting in to worker versioning. Otherwise, this is used only as a<br> marker for workflow reset points and the BuildIDs search attribute.|
|» deployment|body|object|false|Deployment info of the worker that completed this task. Must be present if user has set<br> `WorkerDeploymentOptions` regardless of versioning being enabled or not.<br> Deprecated. Replaced with `deployment_options`.|
|» » seriesName|body|string|false|Different versions of the same worker service/application are related together by having a<br> shared series name.<br> Out of all deployments of a series, one can be designated as the current deployment, which<br> receives new workflow executions and new tasks of workflows with<br> `VERSIONING_BEHAVIOR_AUTO_UPGRADE` versioning behavior.|
|» » buildId|body|string|false|Build ID changes with each version of the worker when the worker program code and/or config<br> changes.|
|» deploymentOptions|body|object|false|Worker deployment options that user has set in the worker.|
|» » deploymentName|body|string|false|Required when `worker_versioning_mode==VERSIONED`.|
|» » buildId|body|string|false|The Build ID of the worker. Required when `worker_versioning_mode==VERSIONED`, in which case,<br> the worker will be part of a Deployment Version.|
|» » workerVersioningMode|body|string(enum)|false|Required. Versioning Mode for this worker. Must be the same for all workers with the<br> same `deployment_name` and `build_id` combination, across all Task Queues.<br> When `worker_versioning_mode==VERSIONED`, the worker will be part of a Deployment Version.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » workerVersioningMode|WORKER_VERSIONING_MODE_UNSPECIFIED|
|» » workerVersioningMode|WORKER_VERSIONING_MODE_UNVERSIONED|
|» » workerVersioningMode|WORKER_VERSIONING_MODE_VERSIONED|

## RecordActivityTaskHeartbeat

<a id="opIdRecordActivityTaskHeartbeat"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/api/v1/namespaces/string/activity-heartbeat \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "taskToken": "string",
    "details": {
      "payloads": [
        null
      ]
    },
    "identity": "string",
    "namespace": "string",
    "resourceId": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/activity-heartbeat`

RecordActivityTaskHeartbeat is optionally called by workers while they execute activities.

 If a worker fails to heartbeat within the `heartbeat_timeout` interval for the activity task,
 then the current attempt times out. Depending on RetryPolicy, this may trigger a retry or
 time out the activity.

 For workflow activities, an `ACTIVITY_TASK_TIMED_OUT` event will be written to the workflow
 history. Calling `RecordActivityTaskHeartbeat` will fail with `NotFound` in such situations,
 in that event, the SDK should request cancellation of the activity.

 The request may contain response `details` which will be persisted by the server and may be
 used by the activity to checkpoint progress. The `cancel_requested` field in the response
 indicates whether cancellation has been requested for the activity.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "taskToken": "string",
  "details": {
    "payloads": [
      null
    ]
  },
  "identity": "string",
  "namespace": "string",
  "resourceId": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="recordactivitytaskheartbeat-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[RecordActivityTaskHeartbeatRequest](#schemarecordactivitytaskheartbeatrequest)|true|none|
|» taskToken|body|string(bytes)|false|The task token as received in `PollActivityTaskQueueResponse`|
|» details|body|object|false|Arbitrary data, of which the most recent call is kept, to store for this activity|
|» » payloads|body|[[Payload](#schemapayload)]|false|none|
|» identity|body|string|false|The identity of the worker/client|
|» namespace|body|string|false|none|
|» resourceId|body|string|false|Resource ID for routing. Contains the workflow ID or activity ID for standalone activities.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "cancelRequested": true,
  "activityPaused": true,
  "activityReset": true
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "details": [
    {
      "@type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="recordactivitytaskheartbeat-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[RecordActivityTaskHeartbeatResponse](#schemarecordactivitytaskheartbeatresponse)|
|default|Default|Default error response|[Status](#schemastatus)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/activity-resolve-as-canceled`

RespondActivityTaskFailed is called by workers when processing an activity task fails.

 For workflow activities, this results in a new `ACTIVITY_TASK_CANCELED` event being written to the workflow history
 and a new workflow task created for the workflow. Fails with `NotFound` if the task token is
 no longer valid due to activity timeout, already being completed, or never having existed.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "taskToken": "string",
  "details": {
    "payloads": [
      null
    ]
  },
  "identity": "string",
  "namespace": "string",
  "resourceId": "string",
  "workerVersion": {
    "buildId": "string",
    "useVersioning": true
  },
  "deployment": {
    "seriesName": "string",
    "buildId": "string"
  },
  "deploymentOptions": {
    "deploymentName": "string",
    "buildId": "string",
    "workerVersioningMode": "WORKER_VERSIONING_MODE_UNSPECIFIED"
  }
}
```

<h3 id="startbatchoperation-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace that contains the batch operation|
|jobId|path|string|true|Job ID defines the unique ID for the batch job|
|body|body|[StartBatchOperationRequest](#schemastartbatchoperationrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|Namespace that contains the batch operation|
|» visibilityQuery|body|string|false|Visibility query defines the the group of workflow to apply the batch operation<br> This field and `executions` are mutually exclusive|
|» jobId|body|string|false|Job ID defines the unique ID for the batch job|
|» reason|body|string|false|Reason to perform the batch operation|
|» executions|body|[[WorkflowExecution](#schemaworkflowexecution)]|false|Executions to apply the batch operation<br> This field and `visibility_query` are mutually exclusive|
|» maxOperationsPerSecond|body|number(float)|false|Limit for the number of operations processed per second within this batch.<br> Its purpose is to reduce the stress on the system caused by batch operations, which helps to prevent system<br> overload and minimize potential delays in executing ongoing tasks for user workers.<br> Note that when no explicit limit is provided, the server will operate according to its limit defined by the<br> dynamic configuration key `worker.batcherRPS`. This also applies if the value in this field exceeds the<br> server's configured limit.|
|» terminationOperation|body|[BatchOperationTermination](#schemabatchoperationtermination)|false|BatchOperationTermination sends terminate requests to batch workflows.<br> Keep the parameter in sync with temporal.api.workflowservice.v1.TerminateWorkflowExecutionRequest.<br> Ignore first_execution_run_id because this is used for single workflow operation.|
|» signalOperation|body|[BatchOperationSignal](#schemabatchoperationsignal)|false|BatchOperationSignal sends signals to batch workflows.<br> Keep the parameter in sync with temporal.api.workflowservice.v1.SignalWorkflowExecutionRequest.|
|» cancellationOperation|body|[BatchOperationCancellation](#schemabatchoperationcancellation)|false|BatchOperationCancellation sends cancel requests to batch workflows.<br> Keep the parameter in sync with temporal.api.workflowservice.v1.RequestCancelWorkflowExecutionRequest.<br> Ignore first_execution_run_id because this is used for single workflow operation.|
|» deletionOperation|body|[BatchOperationDeletion](#schemabatchoperationdeletion)|false|BatchOperationDeletion sends deletion requests to batch workflows.<br> Keep the parameter in sync with temporal.api.workflowservice.v1.DeleteWorkflowExecutionRequest.|
|» resetOperation|body|[BatchOperationReset](#schemabatchoperationreset)|false|BatchOperationReset sends reset requests to batch workflows.<br> Keep the parameter in sync with temporal.api.workflowservice.v1.ResetWorkflowExecutionRequest.|
|» updateWorkflowOptionsOperation|body|[BatchOperationUpdateWorkflowExecutionOptions](#schemabatchoperationupdateworkflowexecutionoptions)|false|BatchOperationUpdateWorkflowExecutionOptions sends UpdateWorkflowExecutionOptions requests to batch workflows.<br> Keep the parameters in sync with temporal.api.workflowservice.v1.UpdateWorkflowExecutionOptionsRequest.|
|» unpauseActivitiesOperation|body|[BatchOperationUnpauseActivities](#schemabatchoperationunpauseactivities)|false|BatchOperationUnpauseActivities sends unpause requests to batch workflows.|
|» resetActivitiesOperation|body|[BatchOperationResetActivities](#schemabatchoperationresetactivities)|false|BatchOperationResetActivities sends activity reset requests in a batch.<br> NOTE: keep in sync with temporal.api.workflowservice.v1.ResetActivityRequest|
|» updateActivityOptionsOperation|body|[BatchOperationUpdateActivityOptions](#schemabatchoperationupdateactivityoptions)|false|BatchOperationUpdateActivityOptions sends an update-activity-options requests in a batch.<br> NOTE: keep in sync with temporal.api.workflowservice.v1.UpdateActivityRequest|

`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/current-deployment/{deployment.series_name}`

Sets a deployment as the current deployment for its deployment series. Can optionally update
 the metadata of the deployment as well.
 Experimental. This API might significantly change or be removed in a future release.
 Deprecated. Replaced by `SetWorkerDeploymentCurrentVersion`.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "deployment": {
    "seriesName": "string",
    "buildId": "string"
  },
  "identity": "string",
  "updateMetadata": {
    "upsertEntries": {
      "property1": null,
      "property2": null
    },
    "removeEntries": [
      "string"
    ]
  }
}
```

<h3 id="setcurrentdeployment-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|deployment.series_name|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[SetCurrentDeploymentRequest](#schemasetcurrentdeploymentrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|none|
|» deployment|body|[Deployment](#schemadeployment)|false|`Deployment` identifies a deployment of Temporal workers. The combination of deployment series<br> name + build ID serves as the identifier. User can use `WorkerDeploymentOptions` in their worker<br> programs to specify these values.<br> Deprecated.|
|» identity|body|string|false|Optional. The identity of the client who initiated this request.|
|» updateMetadata|body|object|false|Optional. Use to add or remove user-defined metadata entries. Metadata entries are exposed<br> when describing a deployment. It is a good place for information such as operator name,<br> links to internal deployment pipelines, etc.|
|» » upsertEntries|body|object|false|none|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|[Payload](#schemapayload)|false|Represents some binary (byte array) data (ex: activity input parameters or workflow result) with<br> metadata which describes this binary data (format, encoding, encryption, etc). Serialization<br> of the data may be user-defined.|
|» » removeEntries|body|[string]|false|List of keys to remove from the metadata.|

 Deprecated. Replaced with `DescribeWorkerDeploymentVersion`.

## GetDeploymentReachability

<a id="opIdGetDeploymentReachability"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/api/v1/namespaces/string/deployments/string/string/reachability \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/deployments/{deployment.series_name}/{deployment.build_id}/reachability`

Returns the reachability level of a worker deployment to help users decide when it is time
 to decommission a deployment. Reachability level is calculated based on the deployment's
 `status` and existing workflows that depend on the given deployment for their execution.
 Calculating reachability is relatively expensive. Therefore, server might return a recently
 cached value. In such a case, the `last_update_time` will inform you about the actual
 reachability calculation time.
 Experimental. This API might significantly change or be removed in a future release.
 Deprecated. Replaced with `DrainageInfo` returned by `DescribeWorkerDeploymentVersion`.

<h3 id="getdeploymentreachability-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|deployment.series_name|path|string|true|none|
|deployment.build_id|path|string|true|none|
|deployment.seriesName|query|string|false|Different versions of the same worker service/application are related together by having a<br> shared series name.<br> Out of all deployments of a series, one can be designated as the current deployment, which<br> receives new workflow executions and new tasks of workflows with<br> `VERSIONING_BEHAVIOR_AUTO_UPGRADE` versioning behavior.|
|deployment.buildId|query|string|false|Build ID changes with each version of the worker when the worker program code and/or config<br> changes.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "deploymentInfo": {
    "deployment": {
      "seriesName": "string",
      "buildId": "string"
    },
    "createTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "taskQueueInfos": [
      {
        "name": "string",
        "type": "TASK_QUEUE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED",
        "firstPollerTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
      }
    ],
    "metadata": {
      "property1": null,
      "property2": null
    },
    "isCurrent": true
  },
  "reachability": "DEPLOYMENT_REACHABILITY_UNSPECIFIED",
  "lastUpdateTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
}
```

## DescribeNexusOperationExecution

<a id="opIdDescribeNexusOperationExecution"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/api/v1/namespaces/string/nexus-operations/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/nexus-operations/{operationId}`

DescribeNexusOperationExecution returns information about a Nexus operation.
 Supported use cases include:
 - Get current operation info without waiting
 - Long-poll for next state change and return new operation info
 Response can optionally include operation input or outcome (if the operation has completed).

<h3 id="describenexusoperationexecution-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|operationId|path|string|true|none|
|runId|query|string|false|Operation run ID. If empty the request targets the latest run.|
|includeInput|query|boolean|false|Include the input field in the response.|
|includeOutcome|query|boolean|false|Include the outcome (result/failure) in the response if the operation has completed.|
|longPollToken|query|string(bytes)|false|Token from a previous DescribeNexusOperationExecutionResponse. If present, this RPC will long-poll until operation<br> state changes from the state encoded in this token. If absent, return current state immediately.<br> If present, run_id must also be present.<br> Note that operation state may change multiple times between requests, therefore it is not<br> guaranteed that a client making a sequence of long-poll requests will see a complete<br> sequence of state changes.|

`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/nexus-operations/{operationId}`

StartNexusOperationExecution starts a new Nexus operation.

 Returns a `NexusOperationExecutionAlreadyStarted` error if an instance already exists with same operation ID in this
 namespace unless permitted by the specified ID conflict policy.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "identity": "string",
  "requestId": "string",
  "operationId": "string",
  "endpoint": "string",
  "service": "string",
  "operation": "string",
  "scheduleToCloseTimeout": "string",
  "scheduleToStartTimeout": "string",
  "startToCloseTimeout": "string",
  "input": {},
  "idReusePolicy": "NEXUS_OPERATION_ID_REUSE_POLICY_UNSPECIFIED",
  "idConflictPolicy": "NEXUS_OPERATION_ID_CONFLICT_POLICY_UNSPECIFIED",
  "searchAttributes": {
    "indexedFields": {
      "property1": null,
      "property2": null
    }
  },
  "nexusHeader": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "userMetadata": {
    "summary": {},
    "details": {}
  }
}
```

<h3 id="startnexusoperationexecution-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|operationId|path|string|true|Identifier for this operation. This is a caller-side ID, distinct from any internal<br> operation identifiers generated by the handler. Must be unique among operations in the<br> same namespace, subject to the rules imposed by id_reuse_policy and id_conflict_policy.|
|body|body|[StartNexusOperationExecutionRequest](#schemastartnexusoperationexecutionrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|none|
|» identity|body|string|false|The identity of the client who initiated this request.|
|» requestId|body|string|false|A unique identifier for this caller-side start request. Typically UUIDv4.<br> StartOperation requests sent to the handler will use a server-generated request ID.|
|» operationId|body|string|false|Identifier for this operation. This is a caller-side ID, distinct from any internal<br> operation identifiers generated by the handler. Must be unique among operations in the<br> same namespace, subject to the rules imposed by id_reuse_policy and id_conflict_policy.|
|» endpoint|body|string|false|Endpoint name, resolved to a URL via the cluster's endpoint registry.|
|» service|body|string|false|Service name.|
|» operation|body|string|false|Operation name.|
|» scheduleToCloseTimeout|body|string|false|Schedule-to-close timeout for this operation.<br> Indicates how long the caller is willing to wait for operation completion.<br> Calls are retried internally by the server.<br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "to" is used to indicate interval. --)|
|» scheduleToStartTimeout|body|string|false|Schedule-to-start timeout for this operation.<br> Indicates how long the caller is willing to wait for the operation to be started (or completed if synchronous)<br> by the handler.<br> If not set or zero, no schedule-to-start timeout is enforced.<br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "to" is used to indicate interval. --)|
|» startToCloseTimeout|body|string|false|Start-to-close timeout for this operation.<br> Indicates how long the caller is willing to wait for an asynchronous operation to complete after it has been<br> started. Synchronous operations ignore this timeout.<br> If not set or zero, no start-to-close timeout is enforced.<br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "to" is used to indicate interval. --)|
|» input|body|object|false|Serialized input to the operation. Passed as the request payload.|
|» idReusePolicy|body|string(enum)|false|Defines whether to allow re-using the operation id from a previously *closed* operation.<br> The default policy is NEXUS_OPERATION_ID_REUSE_POLICY_ALLOW_DUPLICATE.|
|» idConflictPolicy|body|string(enum)|false|Defines how to resolve an operation id conflict with a *running* operation.<br> The default policy is NEXUS_OPERATION_ID_CONFLICT_POLICY_FAIL.|
|» searchAttributes|body|object|false|Search attributes for indexing.|
|» » indexedFields|body|object|false|none|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|[Payload](#schemapayload)|false|Represents some binary (byte array) data (ex: activity input parameters or workflow result) with<br> metadata which describes this binary data (format, encoding, encryption, etc). Serialization<br> of the data may be user-defined.|
|» nexusHeader|body|object|false|Header to attach to the Nexus request.<br> Users are responsible for encrypting sensitive data in this header as it is stored in workflow history and<br> transmitted to external services as-is.<br> This is useful for propagating tracing information.<br> Note these headers are not the same as Temporal headers on internal activities and child workflows, these are<br> transmitted to Nexus operations that may be external and are not traditional payloads.|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|string|false|none|
|» userMetadata|body|object|false|Metadata for use by user interfaces to display the fixed as-of-start summary and details of the operation.|
|» » summary|body|object|false|Short-form text that provides a summary. This payload should be a "json/plain"-encoded payload<br> that is a single JSON string for use in user interfaces. User interface formatting may not<br> apply to this text when used in "title" situations. The payload data section is limited to 400<br> bytes by default.|
|» » details|body|object|false|Long-form text that provides details. This payload should be a "json/plain"-encoded payload<br> that is a single JSON string for use in user interfaces. User interface formatting may apply to<br> this text in common use. The payload data section is limited to 20000 bytes by default.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» idReusePolicy|NEXUS_OPERATION_ID_REUSE_POLICY_UNSPECIFIED|
|» idReusePolicy|NEXUS_OPERATION_ID_REUSE_POLICY_ALLOW_DUPLICATE|
|» idReusePolicy|NEXUS_OPERATION_ID_REUSE_POLICY_ALLOW_DUPLICATE_FAILED_ONLY|
|» idReusePolicy|NEXUS_OPERATION_ID_REUSE_POLICY_REJECT_DUPLICATE|
|» idConflictPolicy|NEXUS_OPERATION_ID_CONFLICT_POLICY_UNSPECIFIED|
|» idConflictPolicy|NEXUS_OPERATION_ID_CONFLICT_POLICY_FAIL|
|» idConflictPolicy|NEXUS_OPERATION_ID_CONFLICT_POLICY_USE_EXISTING|

```json
}
```
