## RequestCancelNexusOperationExecution

<a id="opIdRequestCancelNexusOperationExecution"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/api/v1/namespaces/string/nexus-operations/string/cancel \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "namespace": "string",
    "operationId": "string",
    "runId": "string",
    "identity": "string",
    "requestId": "string",
    "reason": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/nexus-operations/{operationId}/cancel`

RequestCancelNexusOperationExecution requests cancellation of a Nexus operation.

 Requesting to cancel an operation does not automatically transition the operation to canceled status.
 The operation will only transition to canceled status if it supports cancellation and the handler
 processes the cancellation request.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "operationId": "string",
  "runId": "string",
  "identity": "string",
  "requestId": "string",
  "reason": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="requestcancelnexusoperationexecution-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|operationId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[RequestCancelNexusOperationExecutionRequest](#schemarequestcancelnexusoperationexecutionrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|none|
|» operationId|body|string|false|none|
|» runId|body|string|false|Operation run ID, targets the latest run if empty.|
|» identity|body|string|false|The identity of the client who initiated this request.|
|» requestId|body|string|false|Used to de-dupe cancellation requests.|
|» reason|body|string|false|Reason for requesting the cancellation, recorded and available via the DescribeNexusOperationExecution API.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

PollNexusOperationExecution long-polls for a Nexus operation for a given wait stage to complete and returns
 the outcome (result or failure).

|waitStage|query|string(enum)|false|Stage to wait for. The operation may be in a more advanced stage when the poll is unblocked.|

## TerminateNexusOperationExecution

<a id="opIdTerminateNexusOperationExecution"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/api/v1/namespaces/string/nexus-operations/string/terminate \
  -X POST \

    "namespace": "string",
    "operationId": "string",

    "requestId": "string",
    "reason": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/nexus-operations/{operationId}/terminate`

TerminateNexusOperationExecution terminates an existing Nexus operation immediately.

 Termination happens immediately and the operation handler cannot react to it. A terminated operation will have
 its outcome set to a failure with a termination reason.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "operationId": "string",
  "runId": "string",
  "identity": "string",
  "requestId": "string",
  "reason": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="terminatenexusoperationexecution-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|operationId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[TerminateNexusOperationExecutionRequest](#schematerminatenexusoperationexecutionrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|none|
|» operationId|body|string|false|none|
|» runId|body|string|false|Operation run ID, targets the latest run if empty.|
|» identity|body|string|false|The identity of the client who initiated this request.|
|» requestId|body|string|false|Used to de-dupe termination requests.|
|» reason|body|string|false|Reason for requesting the termination, recorded in the operation's result failure outcome.|

> Example responses

<h3 id="createschedule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|The namespace the schedule should be created in.|
|scheduleId|path|string|true|The id of the new schedule.|
|body|body|[CreateScheduleRequest](#schemacreateschedulerequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|The namespace the schedule should be created in.|
|» scheduleId|body|string|false|The id of the new schedule.|
|» schedule|body|object|false|The schedule spec, policies, action, and initial state.|
|» » spec|body|[ScheduleSpec](#schemaschedulespec)|false|ScheduleSpec is a complete description of a set of absolute timestamps<br> (possibly infinite) that an action should occur at. The meaning of a<br> ScheduleSpec depends only on its contents and never changes, except that the<br> definition of a time zone can change over time (most commonly, when daylight<br> saving time policy changes for an area). To create a totally self-contained<br> ScheduleSpec, use UTC or include timezone_data.<br><br> For input, you can provide zero or more of: structured_calendar, calendar,<br> cron_string, interval, and exclude_structured_calendar, and all of them will<br> be used (the schedule will take action at the union of all of their times,<br> minus the ones that match exclude_structured_calendar).<br><br> On input, calendar and cron_string fields will be compiled into<br> structured_calendar (and maybe interval and timezone_name), so if you<br> Describe a schedule, you'll see only structured_calendar, interval, etc.<br><br> If a spec has no matching times after the current time, then the schedule<br> will be subject to automatic deletion (after several days).|
|» » action|body|[ScheduleAction](#schemascheduleaction)|false|none|
|» » policies|body|[SchedulePolicies](#schemaschedulepolicies)|false|none|
|» » state|body|[ScheduleState](#schemaschedulestate)|false|none|
|» initialPatch|body|object|false|Optional initial patch (e.g. to run the action once immediately).|
|» » triggerImmediately|body|object|false|If set, trigger one action immediately.|
|» » » overlapPolicy|body|string(enum)|false|If set, override overlap policy for this one request.|
|» » » scheduledTime|body|string(date-time)|false|Timestamp used for the identity of the target workflow.<br> If not set the default value is the current time.|
|» » backfillRequest|body|[[BackfillRequest](#schemabackfillrequest)]|false|If set, runs though the specified time period(s) and takes actions as if that time<br> passed by right now, all at once. The overlap policy can be overridden for the<br> scope of the backfill.|
|» » pause|body|string|false|If set, change the state to paused or unpaused (respectively) and set the<br> notes field to the value of the string.|
|» » unpause|body|string|false|none|
|» identity|body|string|false|The identity of the client who initiated this request.|
|» requestId|body|string|false|A unique identifier for this create request for idempotence. Typically UUIDv4.|
|» memo|body|object|false|Memo and search attributes to attach to the schedule itself.|
|» » fields|body|object|false|none|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|[Payload](#schemapayload)|false|Represents some binary (byte array) data (ex: activity input parameters or workflow result) with<br> metadata which describes this binary data (format, encoding, encryption, etc). Serialization<br> of the data may be user-defined.|
|» searchAttributes|body|[SearchAttributes](#schemasearchattributes)|false|A user-defined set of *indexed* fields that are used/exposed when listing/searching workflows.<br> The payload is not serialized in a user-defined way.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» » » overlapPolicy|SCHEDULE_OVERLAP_POLICY_UNSPECIFIED|
|» » » overlapPolicy|SCHEDULE_OVERLAP_POLICY_SKIP|
|» » » overlapPolicy|SCHEDULE_OVERLAP_POLICY_BUFFER_ONE|
|» » » overlapPolicy|SCHEDULE_OVERLAP_POLICY_BUFFER_ALL|
|» » » overlapPolicy|SCHEDULE_OVERLAP_POLICY_CANCEL_OTHER|
|» » » overlapPolicy|SCHEDULE_OVERLAP_POLICY_TERMINATE_OTHER|
|» » » overlapPolicy|SCHEDULE_OVERLAP_POLICY_ALLOW_ALL|

<h3 id="updateschedule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|The namespace of the schedule to update.|
|scheduleId|path|string|true|The id of the schedule to update.|
|body|body|[UpdateScheduleRequest](#schemaupdateschedulerequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|The namespace of the schedule to update.|
|» scheduleId|body|string|false|The id of the schedule to update.|
|» schedule|body|object|false|The new schedule. The four main fields of the schedule (spec, action,<br> policies, state) are replaced completely by the values in this message.|
|» » spec|body|[ScheduleSpec](#schemaschedulespec)|false|ScheduleSpec is a complete description of a set of absolute timestamps<br> (possibly infinite) that an action should occur at. The meaning of a<br> ScheduleSpec depends only on its contents and never changes, except that the<br> definition of a time zone can change over time (most commonly, when daylight<br> saving time policy changes for an area). To create a totally self-contained<br> ScheduleSpec, use UTC or include timezone_data.<br><br> For input, you can provide zero or more of: structured_calendar, calendar,<br> cron_string, interval, and exclude_structured_calendar, and all of them will<br> be used (the schedule will take action at the union of all of their times,<br> minus the ones that match exclude_structured_calendar).<br><br> On input, calendar and cron_string fields will be compiled into<br> structured_calendar (and maybe interval and timezone_name), so if you<br> Describe a schedule, you'll see only structured_calendar, interval, etc.<br><br> If a spec has no matching times after the current time, then the schedule<br> will be subject to automatic deletion (after several days).|
|» » action|body|[ScheduleAction](#schemascheduleaction)|false|none|
|» » policies|body|[SchedulePolicies](#schemaschedulepolicies)|false|none|
|» » state|body|[ScheduleState](#schemaschedulestate)|false|none|
|» conflictToken|body|string(bytes)|false|This can be the value of conflict_token from a DescribeScheduleResponse,<br> which will cause this request to fail if the schedule has been modified<br> between the Describe and this Update.<br> If missing, the schedule will be updated unconditionally.|
|» identity|body|string|false|The identity of the client who initiated this request.|
|» requestId|body|string|false|A unique identifier for this update request for idempotence. Typically UUIDv4.|
|» searchAttributes|body|object|false|Schedule search attributes to be updated.<br> Do not set this field if you do not want to update the search attributes.<br> A non-null empty object will set the search attributes to an empty map.<br> Note: you cannot only update the search attributes with `UpdateScheduleRequest`,<br> you must also set the `schedule` field; otherwise, it will unset the schedule.|
|» » indexedFields|body|object|false|none|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|[Payload](#schemapayload)|false|Represents some binary (byte array) data (ex: activity input parameters or workflow result) with<br> metadata which describes this binary data (format, encoding, encryption, etc). Serialization<br> of the data may be user-defined.|
|» memo|body|object|false|Schedule memo to replace. If set, replaces the entire memo.<br> Do not set this field if you do not want to update the memo.<br> A non-null empty object will clear the memo.|
|» » fields|body|object|false|none|
|» » » **additionalProperties**|body|[Payload](#schemapayload)|false|Represents some binary (byte array) data (ex: activity input parameters or workflow result) with<br> metadata which describes this binary data (format, encoding, encryption, etc). Serialization<br> of the data may be user-defined.|

`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/task-queues/{taskQueue}/update-config`

Updates task queue configuration.
 For the overall queue rate limit: the rate limit set by this api overrides the worker-set rate limit,
 which uncouples the rate limit from the worker lifecycle.
 If the overall queue rate limit is unset, the worker-set rate limit takes effect.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "identity": "string",
  "taskQueue": "string",
  "taskQueueType": "TASK_QUEUE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED",
  "updateQueueRateLimit": {
    "rateLimit": {
      "requestsPerSecond": 0
    },
    "reason": "string"
  },
  "updateFairnessKeyRateLimitDefault": {
    "rateLimit": {
      "requestsPerSecond": 0
    },
    "reason": "string"
  },
  "setFairnessWeightOverrides": {
    "property1": 0,
    "property2": 0
  },
  "unsetFairnessWeightOverrides": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="updatetaskqueueconfig-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|taskQueue|path|string|true|Selects the task queue to update.|
|body|body|[UpdateTaskQueueConfigRequest](#schemaupdatetaskqueueconfigrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|none|
|» identity|body|string|false|none|
|» taskQueue|body|string|false|Selects the task queue to update.|
|» taskQueueType|body|string(enum)|false|none|
|» updateQueueRateLimit|body|object|false|Update to queue-wide rate limit.<br> If not set, this configuration is unchanged.<br> NOTE: A limit set by the worker is overriden; and restored again when reset.<br> If the `rate_limit` field in the `RateLimitUpdate` is missing, remove the existing rate limit.|
|» » rateLimit|body|object|false|Rate Limit to be updated|
|» » » requestsPerSecond|body|number(float)|false|Zero is a valid rate limit.|
|» » reason|body|string|false|Reason for why the rate limit was set.|
|» updateFairnessKeyRateLimitDefault|body|object|false|Update to the default fairness key rate limit.<br> If not set, this configuration is unchanged.<br> If the `rate_limit` field in the `RateLimitUpdate` is missing, remove the existing rate limit.|
|» » rateLimit|body|object|false|Rate Limit to be updated|
|» » » requestsPerSecond|body|number(float)|false|Zero is a valid rate limit.|
|» » reason|body|string|false|Reason for why the rate limit was set.|
|» setFairnessWeightOverrides|body|object|false|If set, overrides the fairness weight for each specified fairness key.<br> Fairness keys not listed in this map will keep their existing overrides (if any).|
|» » **additionalProperties**|body|number(float)|false|none|
|» unsetFairnessWeightOverrides|body|[string]|false|If set, removes any existing fairness weight overrides for each specified fairness key.<br> Fairness weights for corresponding keys fall back to the values set during task creation (if any),<br> or to the default weight of 1.0.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» taskQueueType|TASK_QUEUE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED|
|» taskQueueType|TASK_QUEUE_TYPE_WORKFLOW|
|» taskQueueType|TASK_QUEUE_TYPE_ACTIVITY|
|» taskQueueType|TASK_QUEUE_TYPE_NEXUS|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "config": {
    "queueRateLimit": {
      "rateLimit": {
        "requestsPerSecond": 0
      },
      "metadata": {
        "reason": "string",
        "updateIdentity": "string",
        "updateTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
      }
    },
    "fairnessKeysRateLimitDefault": {
      "rateLimit": {
        "requestsPerSecond": 0
      },
      "metadata": {
        "reason": "string",
        "updateIdentity": "string",
        "updateTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
      }
    },
    "fairnessWeightOverrides": {
      "property1": 0,
      "property2": 0
    }
  }
}
```

```json
  "details": [
    {
      "@type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

## DescribeTaskQueue

<a id="opIdDescribeTaskQueue"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/api/v1/namespaces/string/task-queues/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/task-queues/{task_queue.name}`

DescribeTaskQueue returns the following information about the target task queue, broken down by Build ID:
   - List of pollers
   - Workflow Reachability status
   - Backlog info for Workflow and/or Activity tasks

<h3 id="describetaskqueue-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|task_queue.name|path|string|true|none|
|taskQueue.name|query|string|false|none|
|taskQueue.kind|query|string(enum)|false|Default: TASK_QUEUE_KIND_NORMAL.|
|taskQueue.normalName|query|string|false|Iff kind == TASK_QUEUE_KIND_STICKY, then this field contains the name of<br> the normal task queue that the sticky worker is running on.|
|taskQueueType|query|string(enum)|false|If unspecified (TASK_QUEUE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED), then default value (TASK_QUEUE_TYPE_WORKFLOW) will be used.<br> Only supported in default mode (use `task_queue_types` in ENHANCED mode instead).|
|reportStats|query|boolean|false|Report stats for the requested task queue type(s).|
|reportConfig|query|boolean|false|Report Task Queue Config|
|includeTaskQueueStatus|query|boolean|false|Deprecated, use `report_stats` instead.<br> If true, the task queue status will be included in the response.|
|apiMode|query|string(enum)|false|Deprecated. ENHANCED mode is also being deprecated.<br> Select the API mode to use for this request: DEFAULT mode (if unset) or ENHANCED mode.<br> Consult the documentation for each field to understand which mode it is supported in.|
|versions.buildIds|query|[string]|false|Include specific Build IDs.|
|versions.unversioned|query|boolean|false|Include the unversioned queue.|
|versions.allActive|query|boolean|false|Include all active versions. A version is considered active if, in the last few minutes,<br> it has had new tasks or polls, or it has been the subject of certain task queue API calls.|
|taskQueueTypes|query|[string(enum)]|false|Deprecated (as part of the ENHANCED mode deprecation).<br> Task queue types to report info about. If not specified, all types are considered.|
|reportPollers|query|boolean|false|Deprecated (as part of the ENHANCED mode deprecation).<br> Report list of pollers for requested task queue types and versions.|

## DeleteWorkerDeploymentVersion

<a id="opIdDeleteWorkerDeploymentVersion"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/api/v1/namespaces/string/worker-deployment-versions/string/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`DELETE /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/worker-deployment-versions/{deployment_version.deployment_name}/{deployment_version.build_id}`

Used for manual deletion of Versions. User can delete a Version only when all the
 following conditions are met:
  - It is not the Current or Ramping Version of its Deployment.
  - It has no active pollers (none of the task queues in the Version have pollers)
  - It is not draining (see WorkerDeploymentVersionInfo.drainage_info). This condition
    can be skipped by passing `skip-drainage=true`.
 Experimental. This API might significantly change or be removed in a future release.

<h3 id="deleteworkerdeploymentversion-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|deployment_version.deployment_name|path|string|true|none|
|deployment_version.build_id|path|string|true|none|
|version|query|string|false|Deprecated. Use `deployment_version`.|
|deploymentVersion.buildId|query|string|false|A unique identifier for this Version within the Deployment it is a part of.<br> Not necessarily unique within the namespace.<br> The combination of `deployment_name` and `build_id` uniquely identifies this<br> Version within the namespace, because Deployment names are unique within a namespace.|
|deploymentVersion.deploymentName|query|string|false|Identifies the Worker Deployment this Version is part of.|
|skipDrainage|query|boolean|false|Pass to force deletion even if the Version is draining. In this case the open pinned<br> workflows will be stuck until manually moved to another version by UpdateWorkflowExecutionOptions.|
|identity|query|string|false|Optional. The identity of the client who initiated this request.|

> Example responses

<a id="opIdSetWorkerDeploymentCurrentVersion"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/api/v1/namespaces/string/worker-deployments/string/set-current-version \

    "namespace": "string",
    "deploymentName": "string",
    "version": "string",
    "buildId": "string",
    "conflictToken": "string",
    "identity": "string",
    "ignoreMissingTaskQueues": true,
    "allowNoPollers": true
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/worker-deployments/{deploymentName}/set-current-version`

Set/unset the Current Version of a Worker Deployment. Automatically unsets the Ramping
 Version if it is the Version being set as Current.
 Experimental. This API might significantly change or be removed in a future release.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "deploymentName": "string",
  "version": "string",
  "buildId": "string",
  "conflictToken": "string",
  "identity": "string",
  "ignoreMissingTaskQueues": true,
  "allowNoPollers": true
}
```

<h3 id="setworkerdeploymentcurrentversion-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|deploymentName|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[SetWorkerDeploymentCurrentVersionRequest](#schemasetworkerdeploymentcurrentversionrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|none|
|» deploymentName|body|string|false|none|
|» version|body|string|false|Deprecated. Use `build_id`.|
|» buildId|body|string|false|The build id of the Version that you want to set as Current.<br> Pass an empty value to set the Current Version to nil.<br> A nil Current Version represents all the unversioned workers (those with `UNVERSIONED` (or unspecified) `WorkerVersioningMode`.)|
|» conflictToken|body|string(bytes)|false|Optional. This can be the value of conflict_token from a Describe, or another Worker<br> Deployment API. Passing a non-nil conflict token will cause this request to fail if the<br> Deployment's configuration has been modified between the API call that generated the<br> token and this one.|
|» identity|body|string|false|Optional. The identity of the client who initiated this request.|
|» ignoreMissingTaskQueues|body|boolean|false|Optional. By default this request would be rejected if not all the expected Task Queues are<br> being polled by the new Version, to protect against accidental removal of Task Queues, or<br> worker health issues. Pass `true` here to bypass this protection.<br> The set of expected Task Queues is the set of all the Task Queues that were ever poller by<br> the existing Current Version of the Deployment, with the following exclusions:<br>   - Task Queues that are not used anymore (inferred by having empty backlog and a task<br>     add_rate of 0.)<br>   - Task Queues that are moved to another Worker Deployment (inferred by the Task Queue<br>     having a different Current Version than the Current Version of this deployment.)<br> WARNING: Do not set this flag unless you are sure that the missing task queue pollers are not<br> needed. If the request is unexpectedly rejected due to missing pollers, then that means the<br> pollers have not reached to the server yet. Only set this if you expect those pollers to<br> never arrive.|
|» allowNoPollers|body|boolean|false|Optional. By default this request will be rejected if no pollers have been seen for the proposed<br> Current Version, in order to protect users from routing tasks to pollers that do not exist, leading<br> to possible timeouts. Pass `true` here to bypass this protection.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "conflictToken": "string",
  "previousVersion": "string",
  "previousDeploymentVersion": {
    "buildId": "string",
    "deploymentName": "string"
  }
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "details": [
    {
      "@type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="setworkerdeploymentcurrentversion-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|200|OK|OK|[SetWorkerDeploymentCurrentVersionResponse](#schemasetworkerdeploymentcurrentversionresponse)|
|default|Default|Default error response|[Status](#schemastatus)|

`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/worker-deployments/{deploymentName}/set-ramping-version`

Set/unset the Ramping Version of a Worker Deployment and its ramp percentage. Can be used for
 gradual ramp to unversioned workers too.
 Experimental. This API might significantly change or be removed in a future release.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "deploymentName": "string",
  "version": "string",
  "buildId": "string",
  "percentage": 0,
  "conflictToken": "string",
  "identity": "string",
  "ignoreMissingTaskQueues": true,
  "allowNoPollers": true
}
```

<h3 id="setworkerdeploymentrampingversion-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|deploymentName|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[SetWorkerDeploymentRampingVersionRequest](#schemasetworkerdeploymentrampingversionrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|none|
|» deploymentName|body|string|false|none|
|» version|body|string|false|Deprecated. Use `build_id`.|
|» buildId|body|string|false|The build id of the Version that you want to ramp traffic to.<br> Pass an empty value to set the Ramping Version to nil.<br> A nil Ramping Version represents all the unversioned workers (those with `UNVERSIONED` (or unspecified) `WorkerVersioningMode`.)|
|» percentage|body|number(float)|false|Ramp percentage to set. Valid range: [0,100].|
|» conflictToken|body|string(bytes)|false|Optional. This can be the value of conflict_token from a Describe, or another Worker<br> Deployment API. Passing a non-nil conflict token will cause this request to fail if the<br> Deployment's configuration has been modified between the API call that generated the<br> token and this one.|
|» identity|body|string|false|Optional. The identity of the client who initiated this request.|
|» ignoreMissingTaskQueues|body|boolean|false|Optional. By default this request would be rejected if not all the expected Task Queues are<br> being polled by the new Version, to protect against accidental removal of Task Queues, or<br> worker health issues. Pass `true` here to bypass this protection.<br> The set of expected Task Queues equals to all the Task Queues ever polled from the existing<br> Current Version of the Deployment, with the following exclusions:<br>   - Task Queues that are not used anymore (inferred by having empty backlog and a task<br>     add_rate of 0.)<br>   - Task Queues that are moved to another Worker Deployment (inferred by the Task Queue<br>     having a different Current Version than the Current Version of this deployment.)<br> WARNING: Do not set this flag unless you are sure that the missing task queue poller are not<br> needed. If the request is unexpectedly rejected due to missing pollers, then that means the<br> pollers have not reached to the server yet. Only set this if you expect those pollers to<br> never arrive.<br> Note: this check only happens when the ramping version is about to change, not every time<br> that the percentage changes. Also note that the check is against the deployment's Current<br> Version, not the previous Ramping Version.|
|» allowNoPollers|body|boolean|false|Optional. By default this request will be rejected if no pollers have been seen for the proposed<br> Current Version, in order to protect users from routing tasks to pollers that do not exist, leading<br> to possible timeouts. Pass `true` here to bypass this protection.|

```json
}
```

## GetWorkerTaskReachability

<a id="opIdGetWorkerTaskReachability"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/api/v1/namespaces/string/worker-task-reachability \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/worker-task-reachability`

Deprecated. Use `DescribeTaskQueue`.

 Fetches task reachability to determine whether a worker may be retired.
 The request may specify task queues to query for or let the server fetch all task queues mapped to the given
 build IDs.

 When requesting a large number of task queues or all task queues associated with the given build ids in a
 namespace, all task queues will be listed in the response but some of them may not contain reachability
 information due to a server enforced limit. When reaching the limit, task queues that reachability information
 could not be retrieved for will be marked with a single TASK_REACHABILITY_UNSPECIFIED entry. The caller may issue
 another call to get the reachability for those task queues.

 Open source users can adjust this limit by setting the server's dynamic config value for
 `limit.reachabilityTaskQueueScan` with the caveat that this call can strain the visibility store.

<h3 id="getworkertaskreachability-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|buildIds|query|[string]|false|Build ids to retrieve reachability for. An empty string will be interpreted as an unversioned worker.<br> The number of build ids that can be queried in a single API call is limited.<br> Open source users can adjust this limit by setting the server's dynamic config value for<br> `limit.reachabilityQueryBuildIds` with the caveat that this call can strain the visibility store.|
|taskQueues|query|[string]|false|Task queues to retrieve reachability for. Leave this empty to query for all task queues associated with given<br> build ids in the namespace.<br> Must specify at least one task queue if querying for an unversioned worker.<br> The number of task queues that the server will fetch reachability information for is limited.<br> See the `GetWorkerTaskReachabilityResponse` documentation for more information.|
|reachability|query|string(enum)|false|Type of reachability to query for.<br> `TASK_REACHABILITY_NEW_WORKFLOWS` is always returned in the response.<br> Use `TASK_REACHABILITY_EXISTING_WORKFLOWS` if your application needs to respond to queries on closed workflows.<br> Otherwise, use `TASK_REACHABILITY_OPEN_WORKFLOWS`. Default is `TASK_REACHABILITY_EXISTING_WORKFLOWS` if left<br> unspecified.<br> See the TaskReachability docstring for information about each enum variant.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|reachability|TASK_REACHABILITY_UNSPECIFIED|
|reachability|TASK_REACHABILITY_NEW_WORKFLOWS|
|reachability|TASK_REACHABILITY_EXISTING_WORKFLOWS|
|reachability|TASK_REACHABILITY_OPEN_WORKFLOWS|
|reachability|TASK_REACHABILITY_CLOSED_WORKFLOWS|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "buildIdReachability": [
    {
      "buildId": "string",
      "taskQueueReachability": [
        {
          "taskQueue": "string",
          "reachability": [
            "TASK_REACHABILITY_UNSPECIFIED"
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "details": [
    {
      "@type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="getworkertaskreachability-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[GetWorkerTaskReachabilityResponse](#schemagetworkertaskreachabilityresponse)|
|default|Default|Default error response|[Status](#schemastatus)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

```json
        }
      ],

    },
```

```bash
    "requestId": "string",
    "identity": "string",
    "description": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/workflow-rules`

Create a new workflow rule. The rules are used to control the workflow execution.
 The rule will be applied to all running and new workflows in the namespace.
 If the rule with such ID already exist this call will fail
 Note: the rules are part of namespace configuration and will be stored in the namespace config.
 Namespace config is eventually consistent.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "spec": {
    "id": "string",
    "activityStart": {
      "predicate": "string"
    },
    "visibilityQuery": "string",
    "actions": [
      {
        "activityPause": {}
      }
    ],
    "expirationTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  },
  "forceScan": true,
  "requestId": "string",
  "identity": "string",
  "description": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="createworkflowrule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[CreateWorkflowRuleRequest](#schemacreateworkflowrulerequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|none|
|» spec|body|object|false|The rule specification .|
|» » id|body|string|false|The id of the new workflow rule. Must be unique within the namespace.<br> Can be set by the user, and can have business meaning.|
|» » activityStart|body|[WorkflowRuleSpec_ActivityStartingTrigger](#schemaworkflowrulespec_activitystartingtrigger)|false|Activity trigger will be triggered when an activity is about to start.|
|» » visibilityQuery|body|string|false|Restricted Visibility query.<br> This query is used to filter workflows in this namespace to which this rule should apply.<br> It is applied to any running workflow each time a triggering event occurs, before the trigger predicate is evaluated.<br> The following workflow attributes are supported:<br> - WorkflowType<br> - WorkflowId<br> - StartTime<br> - ExecutionStatus|
|» » actions|body|[[WorkflowRuleAction](#schemaworkflowruleaction)]|false|WorkflowRuleAction to be taken when the rule is triggered and predicate is matched.|
|» » expirationTime|body|string(date-time)|false|Expiration time of the rule. After this time, the rule will be deleted.<br> Can be empty if the rule should never expire.|
|» forceScan|body|boolean|false|If true, the rule will be applied to the currently running workflows via batch job.<br> If not set , the rule will only be applied when triggering condition is satisfied.<br> visibility_query in the rule will be used to select the workflows to apply the rule to.|
|» requestId|body|string|false|Used to de-dupe requests. Typically should be UUID.|
|» identity|body|string|false|Identity of the actor who created the rule. Will be stored with the rule.|
|» description|body|string|false|Rule description.Will be stored with the rule.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "rule": {
    "createTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
    "spec": {
      "id": "string",
      "activityStart": {
        "predicate": "string"
      },
      "visibilityQuery": "string",
      "actions": [
        {
          "activityPause": {}
        }
      ],
      "expirationTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    },
    "createdByIdentity": "string",
    "description": "string"
  },
  "jobId": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "details": [
    {
      "@type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="createworkflowrule-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[CreateWorkflowRuleResponse](#schemacreateworkflowruleresponse)|
|default|Default|Default error response|[Status](#schemastatus)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## GetWorkflowExecutionHistory

<a id="opIdGetWorkflowExecutionHistory"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/api/v1/namespaces/string/workflows/string/history \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/workflows/{execution.workflow_id}/history`

GetWorkflowExecutionHistory returns the history of specified workflow execution. Fails with
 `NotFound` if the specified workflow execution is unknown to the service.

<h3 id="getworkflowexecutionhistory-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|execution.workflow_id|path|string|true|none|
|execution.workflowId|query|string|false|none|
|execution.runId|query|string|false|none|
|maximumPageSize|query|integer(int32)|false|none|
|nextPageToken|query|string(bytes)|false|If a `GetWorkflowExecutionHistoryResponse` or a `PollWorkflowTaskQueueResponse` had one of<br> these, it should be passed here to fetch the next page.|
|waitNewEvent|query|boolean|false|If set to true, the RPC call will not resolve until there is a new event which matches<br> the `history_event_filter_type`, or a timeout is hit.|
|historyEventFilterType|query|string(enum)|false|Filter returned events such that they match the specified filter type.<br> Default: HISTORY_EVENT_FILTER_TYPE_ALL_EVENT.|
|skipArchival|query|boolean|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

## GetWorkflowExecutionHistoryReverse

<a id="opIdGetWorkflowExecutionHistoryReverse"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/api/v1/namespaces/string/workflows/string/history-reverse \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/workflows/{execution.workflow_id}/history-reverse`

GetWorkflowExecutionHistoryReverse returns the history of specified workflow execution in reverse
 order (starting from last event). Fails with`NotFound` if the specified workflow execution is
 unknown to the service.

<h3 id="getworkflowexecutionhistoryreverse-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|execution.workflow_id|path|string|true|none|
|execution.workflowId|query|string|false|none|
|execution.runId|query|string|false|none|
|maximumPageSize|query|integer(int32)|false|none|
|nextPageToken|query|string(bytes)|false|none|

|body|body|[QueryWorkflowRequest](#schemaqueryworkflowrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|none|
|» execution|body|[WorkflowExecution](#schemaworkflowexecution)|false|Identifies a specific workflow within a namespace. Practically speaking, because run_id is a<br> uuid, a workflow execution is globally unique. `POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/workflows/{execution.workflow_id}/trigger-rule`

TriggerWorkflowRule allows to:
  * trigger existing rule for a specific workflow execution;
  * trigger rule for a specific workflow execution without creating a rule;
 This is useful for one-off operations.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "execution": {
    "workflowId": "string",
    "runId": "string"
  },
  "id": "string",
  "spec": {
    "id": "string",
    "activityStart": {
      "predicate": "string"
    },
    "visibilityQuery": "string",
    "actions": [
      {
        "activityPause": {}
      }
    ],
    "expirationTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  },
  "identity": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="triggerworkflowrule-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|execution.workflow_id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[TriggerWorkflowRuleRequest](#schematriggerworkflowrulerequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|none|
|» execution|body|object|false|Execution info of the workflow which scheduled this activity|
|» » workflowId|body|string|false|none|
|» » runId|body|string|false|none|
|» id|body|string|false|none|
|» spec|body|object|false|Note: Rule ID and expiration date are not used in the trigger request.|
|» » id|body|string|false|The id of the new workflow rule. Must be unique within the namespace.<br> Can be set by the user, and can have business meaning.|
|» » activityStart|body|[WorkflowRuleSpec_ActivityStartingTrigger](#schemaworkflowrulespec_activitystartingtrigger)|false|Activity trigger will be triggered when an activity is about to start.|
|» » visibilityQuery|body|string|false|Restricted Visibility query.<br> This query is used to filter workflows in this namespace to which this rule should apply.<br> It is applied to any running workflow each time a triggering event occurs, before the trigger predicate is evaluated.<br> The following workflow attributes are supported:<br> - WorkflowType<br> - WorkflowId<br> - StartTime<br> - ExecutionStatus|
|» » actions|body|[[WorkflowRuleAction](#schemaworkflowruleaction)]|false|WorkflowRuleAction to be taken when the rule is triggered and predicate is matched.|
|» » expirationTime|body|string(date-time)|false|Expiration time of the rule. After this time, the rule will be deleted.<br> Can be empty if the rule should never expire.|
|» identity|body|string|false|The identity of the client who initiated this request|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "applied": true
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "details": [
    {
      "@type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

<h3 id="triggerworkflowrule-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[TriggerWorkflowRuleResponse](#schematriggerworkflowruleresponse)|
|default|Default|Default error response|[Status](#schemastatus)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication
</aside>

<h3 id="startworkflowexecution-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|workflowId|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[StartWorkflowExecutionRequest](#schemastartworkflowexecutionrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|none|
|» workflowId|body|string|false|none|
|» workflowType|body|[WorkflowType](#schemaworkflowtype)|false|Represents the identifier used by a workflow author to define the workflow. Typically, the<br> name of a function. This is sometimes referred to as the workflow's "name"|
|» taskQueue|body|[TaskQueue](#schemataskqueue)|false|See https://docs.temporal.io/docs/concepts/task-queues/|
|» input|body|object|false|Serialized arguments to the workflow. These are passed as arguments to the workflow function.|
|» » payloads|body|[[Payload](#schemapayload)]|false|none|
|» workflowExecutionTimeout|body|string|false|Total workflow execution timeout including retries and continue as new.|
|» workflowRunTimeout|body|string|false|Timeout of a single workflow run.|
|» workflowTaskTimeout|body|string|false|Timeout of a single workflow task.|
|» identity|body|string|false|The identity of the client who initiated this request|
|» requestId|body|string|false|A unique identifier for this start request. Typically UUIDv4.|
|» workflowIdReusePolicy|body|string(enum)|false|Defines whether to allow re-using the workflow id from a previously *closed* workflow.<br> The default policy is WORKFLOW_ID_REUSE_POLICY_ALLOW_DUPLICATE.<br><br> See `workflow_id_conflict_policy` for handling a workflow id duplication with a *running* workflow.|
|» workflowIdConflictPolicy|body|string(enum)|false|Defines how to resolve a workflow id conflict with a *running* workflow.<br> The default policy is WORKFLOW_ID_CONFLICT_POLICY_FAIL.<br><br> See `workflow_id_reuse_policy` for handling a workflow id duplication with a *closed* workflow.|
|» retryPolicy|body|object|false|The retry policy for the workflow. Will never exceed `workflow_execution_timeout`.|
|» » initialInterval|body|string|false|Interval of the first retry. If retryBackoffCoefficient is 1.0 then it is used for all retries.|
|» » backoffCoefficient|body|number(double)|false|Coefficient used to calculate the next retry interval.<br> The next retry interval is previous interval multiplied by the coefficient.<br> Must be 1 or larger.|
|» » maximumInterval|body|string|false|Maximum interval between retries. Exponential backoff leads to interval increase.<br> This value is the cap of the increase. Default is 100x of the initial interval.|
|» » maximumAttempts|body|integer(int32)|false|Maximum number of attempts. When exceeded the retries stop even if not expired yet.<br> 1 disables retries. 0 means unlimited (up to the timeouts)|
|» » nonRetryableErrorTypes|body|[string]|false|Non-Retryable errors types. Will stop retrying if the error type matches this list. Note that<br> this is not a substring match, the error *type* (not message) must match exactly.|
|» cronSchedule|body|string|false|See https://docs.temporal.io/docs/content/what-is-a-temporal-cron-job/|
|» memo|body|[Memo](#schemamemo)|false|A user-defined set of *unindexed* fields that are exposed when listing/searching workflows|
|» searchAttributes|body|[SearchAttributes](#schemasearchattributes)|false|A user-defined set of *indexed* fields that are used/exposed when listing/searching workflows.<br> The payload is not serialized in a user-defined way.|
|» header|body|[Header](#schemaheader)|false|Contains metadata that can be attached to a variety of requests, like starting a workflow, and<br> can be propagated between, for example, workflows and activities.|
|» requestEagerExecution|body|boolean|false|Request to get the first workflow task inline in the response bypassing matching service and worker polling.<br> If set to `true` the caller is expected to have a worker available and capable of processing the task.<br> The returned task will be marked as started and is expected to be completed by the specified<br> `workflow_task_timeout`.|
|» continuedFailure|body|object|false|These values will be available as ContinuedFailure and LastCompletionResult in the<br> WorkflowExecutionStarted event and through SDKs. If set, it will add a history event to the running workflow.|

|» priority|body|object|false|Priority metadata|
|» » priorityKey|body|integer(int32)|false|Priority key is a positive integer from 1 to n, where smaller integers<br> correspond to higher priorities (tasks run sooner). In general, tasks in<br> a queue should be processed in close to priority order, although small<br> deviations are possible.<br><br> The maximum priority value (minimum priority) is determined by server<br> configuration, and defaults to 5.<br><br> If priority is not present (or zero), then the effective priority will be<br> the default priority, which is calculated by (min+max)/2. With the<br> default max of 5, and min of 1, that comes out to 3.|
|» » fairnessKey|body|string|false|Fairness key is a short string that's used as a key for a fairness<br> balancing mechanism. It may correspond to a tenant id, or to a fixed<br> string like "high" or "low". The default is the empty string.<br><br> The fairness mechanism attempts to dispatch tasks for a given key in<br> proportion to its weight. For example, using a thousand distinct tenant<br> ids, each with a weight of 1.0 (the default) will result in each tenant<br> getting a roughly equal share of task dispatch throughput.<br><br> (Note: this does not imply equal share of worker capacity! Fairness<br> decisions are made based on queue statistics, not<br> current worker load.)<br><br> As another example, using keys "high" and "low" with weight 9.0 and 1.0<br> respectively will prefer dispatching "high" tasks over "low" tasks at a<br> 9:1 ratio, while allowing either key to use all worker capacity if the<br> other is not present.<br><br> All fairness mechanisms, including rate limits, are best-effort and<br> probabilistic. The results may not match what a "perfect" algorithm with<br> infinite resources would produce. The more unique keys are used, the less<br> accurate the results will be.<br><br> Fairness keys are limited to 64 bytes.|
|» » fairnessWeight|body|number(float)|false|Fairness weight for a task can come from multiple sources for<br> flexibility. From highest to lowest precedence:<br> 1. Weights for a small set of keys can be overridden in task queue<br>    configuration with an API.<br> 2. It can be attached to the workflow/activity in this field.<br> 3. The default weight of 1.0 will be used.<br><br> Weight values are clamped to the range [0.001, 1000].|
|» eagerWorkerDeploymentOptions|body|object|false|Deployment Options of the worker who will process the eager task. Passed when `request_eager_execution=true`.|
|» » deploymentName|body|string|false|Required when `worker_versioning_mode==VERSIONED`.|
|» » buildId|body|string|false|The Build ID of the worker. Required when `worker_versioning_mode==VERSIONED`, in which case,<br> the worker will be part of a Deployment Version.|
|» » workerVersioningMode|body|string(enum)|false|Required. Versioning Mode for this worker. Must be the same for all workers with the<br> same `deployment_name` and `build_id` combination, across all Task Queues.<br> When `worker_versioning_mode==VERSIONED`, the worker will be part of a Deployment Version.|
|» timeSkippingConfig|body|object|false|Time-skipping configuration. If not set, time skipping is disabled.|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|Enables or disables time skipping for this workflow execution.|
|» » maxSkippedDuration|body|string|false|Maximum total virtual time that can be skipped.|
|» » maxElapsedDuration|body|string|false|Maximum elapsed time since time skipping was enabled.<br> This includes both skipped time and real time elapsing.|

## PauseActivityExecution

<a id="opIdPauseActivityExecution"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/api/v1/namespaces/string/workflows/string/activities/string/pause \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "namespace": "string",
    "workflowId": "string",
    "activityId": "string",
    "runId": "string",
    "identity": "string",
    "reason": "string",
    "resourceId": "string",
    "requestId": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/workflows/{workflowId}/activities/{activityId}/pause`

PauseActivityExecution pauses the execution of an activity specified by its ID.
 This API can be used to target a workflow activity or a standalone activity

 Pausing an activity means:
 - If the activity is currently waiting for a retry or is running and subsequently fails,
   it will not be rescheduled until it is unpaused.
 - If the activity is already paused, calling this method will have no effect.
 - If the activity is running and finishes successfully, the activity will be completed.
 - If the activity is running and finishes with failure:
   * if there is no retry left - the activity will be completed.
   * if there are more retries left - the activity will be paused.
 For long-running activities:
 - activities in paused state will send a cancellation with "activity_paused" set to 'true' in response to 'RecordActivityTaskHeartbeat'.

 Returns a `NotFound` error if there is no pending activity with the provided ID

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "workflowId": "string",
  "activityId": "string",
  "runId": "string",
  "identity": "string",
  "reason": "string",
  "resourceId": "string",
  "requestId": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="pauseactivityexecution-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace of the workflow which scheduled this activity.|
|workflowId|path|string|true|If provided, pause a workflow activity (or activities) for the given workflow ID.<br> If empty, targets a standalone activity.|
|activityId|path|string|true|The ID of the activity to target.|
|body|body|[PauseActivityExecutionRequest](#schemapauseactivityexecutionrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|Namespace of the workflow which scheduled this activity.|
|» workflowId|body|string|false|If provided, pause a workflow activity (or activities) for the given workflow ID.<br> If empty, targets a standalone activity.|
|» activityId|body|string|false|The ID of the activity to target.|
|» runId|body|string|false|Run ID of the workflow or standalone activity.|
|» identity|body|string|false|The identity of the client who initiated this request.|
|» reason|body|string|false|Reason to pause the activity.|
|» resourceId|body|string|false|Resource ID for routing. Contains "workflow:{workflow_id}" for workflow activities or "activity:{activity_id}" for standalone activities.|
|» requestId|body|string|false|Used to de-dupe pause requests.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> default Response

```json
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "details": [
    {
      "@type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

## ResetActivityExecution

<a id="opIdResetActivityExecution"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/api/v1/namespaces/string/workflows/string/activities/string/reset \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "namespace": "string",
    "workflowId": "string",
    "activityId": "string",
    "runId": "string",

    "resetHeartbeat": true,
    "keepPaused": true,
    "jitter": "string",
    "restoreOriginalOptions": true,
    "resourceId": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/workflows/{workflowId}/activities/{activityId}/reset`

ResetActivityExecution resets the execution of an activity specified by its ID.
 This API can be used to target a workflow activity or a standalone activity.

 Resetting an activity means:
 * number of attempts will be reset to 0.
 * activity timeouts will be reset.
 * if the activity is waiting for retry, and it is not paused or 'keep_paused' is not provided:
    it will be scheduled immediately (* see 'jitter' flag)

 Returns a `NotFound` error if there is no pending activity with the provided ID or type.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "workflowId": "string",
  "activityId": "string",
  "runId": "string",
  "identity": "string",
  "resetHeartbeat": true,
  "keepPaused": true,
  "jitter": "string",
  "restoreOriginalOptions": true,
  "resourceId": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="resetactivityexecution-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace of the workflow which scheduled this activity.|
|workflowId|path|string|true|If provided, targets a workflow activity for the given workflow ID.<br> If empty, targets a standalone activity.|
|activityId|path|string|true|The ID of the activity to target.|
|body|body|[ResetActivityExecutionRequest](#schemaresetactivityexecutionrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|Namespace of the workflow which scheduled this activity.|
|» workflowId|body|string|false|If provided, targets a workflow activity for the given workflow ID.<br> If empty, targets a standalone activity.|
|» activityId|body|string|false|The ID of the activity to target.|
|» runId|body|string|false|Run ID of the workflow or standalone activity.|
|» identity|body|string|false|The identity of the client who initiated this request.|
|» resetHeartbeat|body|boolean|false|Indicates that activity should reset heartbeat details.<br> This flag will be applied only to the new instance of the activity.|
|» keepPaused|body|boolean|false|If activity is paused, it will remain paused after reset|
|» jitter|body|string|false|If set, and activity is in backoff, the activity will start at a random time within the specified jitter duration.<br> (unless it is paused and keep_paused is set)|
|» restoreOriginalOptions|body|boolean|false|If set, the activity options will be restored to the defaults.<br> Default options are then options activity was created with.<br> They are part of the first schedule event.|
|» resourceId|body|string|false|Resource ID for routing. Contains "workflow:{workflow_id}" for workflow activities or "activity:{activity_id}" for standalone activities.|

```json
{}
```

## UnpauseActivityExecution

<a id="opIdUnpauseActivityExecution"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/api/v1/namespaces/string/workflows/string/activities/string/unpause \
  -X POST \

    "namespace": "string",

    "activityId": "string",

    "resetAttempts": true,
    "resetHeartbeat": true,

    "jitter": "string",
    "resourceId": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/workflows/{workflowId}/activities/{activityId}/unpause`

UnpauseActivityExecution unpauses the execution of an activity specified by its ID.
 This API can be used to target a workflow activity or a standalone activity.

 If activity is not paused, this call will have no effect.
 If the activity was paused while waiting for retry, it will be scheduled immediately (* see 'jitter' flag).
 Once the activity is unpaused, all timeout timers will be regenerated.

 Returns a `NotFound` error if there is no pending activity with the provided ID

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "workflowId": "string",
  "activityId": "string",
  "runId": "string",
  "identity": "string",
  "resetAttempts": true,
  "resetHeartbeat": true,
  "reason": "string",
  "jitter": "string",
  "resourceId": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="unpauseactivityexecution-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace of the workflow which scheduled this activity.|
|workflowId|path|string|true|If provided, targets a workflow activity for the given workflow ID.<br> If empty, targets a standalone activity.|
|activityId|path|string|true|The ID of the activity to target.|
|body|body|[UnpauseActivityExecutionRequest](#schemaunpauseactivityexecutionrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|Namespace of the workflow which scheduled this activity.|
|» workflowId|body|string|false|If provided, targets a workflow activity for the given workflow ID.<br> If empty, targets a standalone activity.|
|» activityId|body|string|false|The ID of the activity to target.|
|» runId|body|string|false|Run ID of the workflow or standalone activity.|
|» identity|body|string|false|The identity of the client who initiated this request.|
|» resetAttempts|body|boolean|false|Providing this flag will also reset the number of attempts.|
|» resetHeartbeat|body|boolean|false|Providing this flag will also reset the heartbeat details.|
|» reason|body|string|false|Reason to unpause the activity.|
|» jitter|body|string|false|If set, the activity will start at a random time within the specified jitter duration.|
|» resourceId|body|string|false|Resource ID for routing. Contains "workflow:{workflow_id}" for workflow activities or "activity:{activity_id}" for standalone activities.|


|» » » maximumAttempts|body|integer(int32)|false|Maximum number of attempts. When exceeded the retries stop even if not expired yet.<br> 1 disables retries. 0 means unlimited (up to the timeouts)|
|» » » nonRetryableErrorTypes|body|[string]|false|Non-Retryable errors types. Will stop retrying if the error type matches this list. Note that<br> this is not a substring match, the error *type* (not message) must match exactly.|

In general, tasks in<br> a queue should be processed in close to priority order, although small<br> deviations are possible.<br><br> The maximum priority value (minimum priority) is determined by server<br> configuration, and defaults to 5.<br><br> If priority is not present (or zero), then the effective priority will be<br> the default priority, which is calculated by (min+max)/2. With the<br> default max of 5, and min of 1, that comes out to 3.|
|» » » fairnessKey|body|string|false|Fairness key is a short string that's used as a key for a fairness<br> balancing mechanism. It may correspond to a tenant id, or to a fixed<br> string like "high" or "low". The default is the empty string.<br><br> The fairness mechanism attempts to dispatch tasks for a given key in<br> proportion to its weight. For example, using a thousand distinct tenant<br> ids, each with a weight of 1.0 (the default) will result in each tenant<br> getting a roughly equal share of task dispatch throughput.<br><br> (Note: this does not imply equal share of worker capacity! Fairness<br> decisions are made based on queue statistics, not<br> current worker load.)<br><br> As another example, using keys "high" and "low" with weight 9.0 and 1.0<br> respectively will prefer dispatching "high" tasks over "low" tasks at a<br> 9:1 ratio, while allowing either key to use all worker capacity if the<br> other is not present.<br><br> All fairness mechanisms, including rate limits, are best-effort and<br> probabilistic. The results may not match what a "perfect" algorithm with<br> infinite resources would produce. The more unique keys are used, the less<br> accurate the results will be.<br><br> Fairness keys are limited to 64 bytes.|
|» » » fairnessWeight|body|number(float)|false|Fairness weight for a task can come from multiple sources for<br> flexibility. From highest to lowest precedence:<br> 1. Weights for a small set of keys can be overridden in task queue<br>    configuration with an API.<br> 2. It can be attached to the workflow/activity in this field.<br> 3. The default weight of 1.0 will be used.<br><br> Weight values are clamped to the range [0.001, 1000].|

## PauseWorkflowExecution

<a id="opIdPauseWorkflowExecution"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/api/v1/namespaces/string/workflows/string/pause \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "namespace": "string",
    "workflowId": "string",
    "runId": "string",
    "identity": "string",
    "reason": "string",
    "requestId": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/workflows/{workflowId}/pause`

Note: This is an experimental API and the behavior may change in a future release.
 PauseWorkflowExecution pauses the workflow execution specified in the request. Pausing a workflow execution results in
 - The workflow execution status changes to `PAUSED` and a new WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_PAUSED event is added to the history
 - No new workflow tasks or activity tasks are dispatched.
   - Any workflow task currently executing on the worker will be allowed to complete.
   - Any activity task currently executing will be paused.
 - All server-side events will continue to be processed by the server.
 - Queries & Updates on a paused workflow will be rejected.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "workflowId": "string",
  "runId": "string",
  "identity": "string",
  "reason": "string",
  "requestId": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="pauseworkflowexecution-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace of the workflow to pause.|
|workflowId|path|string|true|ID of the workflow execution to be paused. Required.|
|body|body|[PauseWorkflowExecutionRequest](#schemapauseworkflowexecutionrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|Namespace of the workflow to pause.|
|» workflowId|body|string|false|ID of the workflow execution to be paused. Required.|
|» runId|body|string|false|Run ID of the workflow execution to be paused. Optional. If not provided, the current run of the workflow will be paused.|
|» identity|body|string|false|The identity of the client who initiated this request.|
|» reason|body|string|false|Reason to pause the workflow execution.|
|» requestId|body|string|false|A unique identifier for this pause request for idempotence. Typically UUIDv4.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "details": [
    {
      "@type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

|default|Default|Default error response|[Status](#schemastatus)|

`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/workflows/{workflowId}/signal-with-start/{signalName}`

SignalWithStartWorkflowExecution is used to ensure a signal is sent to a workflow, even if
 it isn't yet started.

 If the workflow is running, a `WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_SIGNALED` event is recorded in the history
 and a workflow task is generated.

 If the workflow is not running or not found, then the workflow is created with
 `WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_STARTED` and `WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_SIGNALED` events in its history, and a
 workflow task is generated.

For example, using a thousand distinct tenant<br> ids, each with a weight of 1.0 (the default) will result in each tenant<br> getting a roughly equal share of task dispatch throughput.<br><br> (Note: this does not imply equal share of worker capacity! Fairness<br> decisions are made based on queue statistics, not<br> current worker load.)<br><br> As another example, using keys "high" and "low" with weight 9.0 and 1.0<br> respectively will prefer dispatching "high" tasks over "low" tasks at a<br> 9:1 ratio, while allowing either key to use all worker capacity if the<br> other is not present.<br><br> All fairness mechanisms, including rate limits, are best-effort and<br> probabilistic. The results may not match what a "perfect" algorithm with<br> infinite resources would produce. The more unique keys are used, the less<br> accurate the results will be.<br><br> Fairness keys are limited to 64 bytes.|

Weights for a small set of keys can be overridden in task queue<br>    configuration with an API.<br> 2. It can be attached to the workflow/activity in this field.<br> 3. The default weight of 1.0 will be used.<br><br> Weight values are clamped to the range [0.001, 1000].|


`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/workflows/{workflowId}/unpause`

Note: This is an experimental API and the behavior may change in a future release.
 UnpauseWorkflowExecution unpauses a previously paused workflow execution specified in the request.
 Unpausing a workflow execution results in
 - The workflow execution status changes to `RUNNING` and a new WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_UNPAUSED event is added to the history
 - Workflow tasks and activity tasks are resumed.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "workflowId": "string",
  "runId": "string",
  "identity": "string",
  "reason": "string",
  "requestId": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="unpauseworkflowexecution-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace of the workflow to unpause.|
|workflowId|path|string|true|ID of the workflow execution to be paused. Required.|
|body|body|[UnpauseWorkflowExecutionRequest](#schemaunpauseworkflowexecutionrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|Namespace of the workflow to unpause.|
|» workflowId|body|string|false|ID of the workflow execution to be paused. Required.|
|» runId|body|string|false|Run ID of the workflow execution to be paused. Optional. If not provided, the current run of the workflow will be paused.|
|» identity|body|string|false|The identity of the client who initiated this request.|
|» reason|body|string|false|Reason to unpause the workflow execution.|
|» requestId|body|string|false|A unique identifier for this unpause request for idempotence. Typically UUIDv4.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "details": [
    {
      "@type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/workflows/{workflow_execution.workflow_id}/cancel`

RequestCancelWorkflowExecution is called by workers when they want to request cancellation of
 a workflow execution.

 This results in a new `WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_CANCEL_REQUESTED` event being written to the
 workflow history and a new workflow task created for the workflow. It returns success if the requested
 workflow is already closed. It fails with 'NotFound' if the requested workflow doesn't exist.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "workflowExecution": {
    "workflowId": "string",
    "runId": "string"
  },
  "identity": "string",
  "requestId": "string",
  "firstExecutionRunId": "string",
  "reason": "string",
  "links": [
    {
      "workflowEvent": {
        "namespace": "string",
        "workflowId": "string",
        "runId": "string",
        "eventRef": {
          "eventId": "string",
          "eventType": "EVENT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED"
        },
        "requestIdRef": {
          "requestId": "string",
          "eventType": "EVENT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED"
        }
      },
      "batchJob": {
        "jobId": "string"
      },

        "runId": "string"
      },
      "nexusOperation": {

        "operationId": "string",
        "runId": "string"
      }
    }

}
```

`POST /api/v1/namespaces/{namespace}/workflows/{workflow_execution.workflow_id}/reset`

ResetWorkflowExecution will reset an existing workflow execution to a specified
 `WORKFLOW_TASK_COMPLETED` event (exclusive). It will immediately terminate the current
 execution instance. "Exclusive" means the identified completed event itself is not replayed
 in the reset history; the preceding `WORKFLOW_TASK_STARTED` event remains and will be marked as failed
 immediately, and a new workflow task will be scheduled to retry it.

> Body parameter

```json

  "namespace": "string",
  "workflowExecution": {
    "workflowId": "string",
    "runId": "string"
  },
  "reason": "string",
  "workflowTaskFinishEventId": "string",
  "requestId": "string",
  "resetReapplyType": "RESET_REAPPLY_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED",
  "resetReapplyExcludeTypes": [
    "RESET_REAPPLY_EXCLUDE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED"
  ],
  "postResetOperations": [
    {
      "signalWorkflow": {
        "signalName": "string",
        "input": {
          "payloads": [
            null
          ]
        },
        "header": {
          "fields": {
            "property1": null,
            "property2": null
          }
        },
        "links": [
          {
            "workflowEvent": {
              "namespace": "string",
              "workflowId": "string",
```

|» namespace|body|string|false|The namespace name of the target Workflow.|

|» » » pinned|body|object|false|Override the workflow to have Pinned behavior.|
|» » » » behavior|body|string(enum)|false|Defaults to PINNED_OVERRIDE_BEHAVIOR_UNSPECIFIED.<br> See `PinnedOverrideBehavior` for details.|
|» » » » version|body|object|false|Specifies the Worker Deployment Version to pin this workflow to.<br> Required if the target workflow is not already pinned to a version.<br><br> If omitted and the target workflow is already pinned, the effective<br> pinned version will be the existing pinned version.<br><br> If omitted and the target workflow is not pinned, the override request<br> will be rejected with a PreconditionFailed error.|
|» » » » » buildId|body|string|false|A unique identifier for this Version within the Deployment it is a part of.<br> Not necessarily unique within the namespace.<br> The combination of `deployment_name` and `build_id` uniquely identifies this<br> Version within the namespace, because Deployment names are unique within a namespace.|
|» » » » » deploymentName|body|string|false|Identifies the Worker Deployment this Version is part of.|
|» » » autoUpgrade|body|boolean|false|Override the workflow to have AutoUpgrade behavior.|
|» » » behavior|body|string(enum)|false|Required.<br> Deprecated. Use `override`.|
|» » » deployment|body|object|false|Required if behavior is `PINNED`. Must be null if behavior is `AUTO_UPGRADE`.<br> Identifies the worker deployment to pin the workflow to.<br> Deprecated. Use `override.pinned.version`.|
|» » » » seriesName|body|string|false|Different versions of the same worker service/application are related together by having a<br> shared series name.<br> Out of all deployments of a series, one can be designated as the current deployment, which<br> receives new workflow executions and new tasks of workflows with<br> `VERSIONING_BEHAVIOR_AUTO_UPGRADE` versioning behavior.|
|» » » » buildId|body|string|false|Build ID changes with each version of the worker when the worker program code and/or config<br> changes.|
|» » » pinnedVersion|body|string|false|Required if behavior is `PINNED`. Must be absent if behavior is not `PINNED`.<br> Identifies the worker deployment version to pin the workflow to, in the format<br> "<deployment_name>.<build_id>".<br> Deprecated. Use `override.pinned.version`.|
|» » priority|body|object|false|If set, overrides the workflow's priority sent by the SDK.|
|» » » priorityKey|body|integer(int32)|false|Priority key is a positive integer from 1 to n, where smaller integers<br> correspond to higher priorities (tasks run sooner). In general, tasks in<br> a queue should be processed in close to priority order, although small<br> deviations are possible.<br><br> The maximum priority value (minimum priority) is determined by server<br> configuration, and defaults to 5.<br><br> If priority is not present (or zero), then the effective priority will be<br> the default priority, which is calculated by (min+max)/2. With the<br> default max of 5, and min of 1, that comes out to 3.|
|» » » fairnessKey|body|string|false|Fairness key is a short string that's used as a key for a fairness<br> balancing mechanism. It may correspond to a tenant id, or to a fixed<br> string like "high" or "low". The default is the empty string.<br><br> The fairness mechanism attempts to dispatch tasks for a given key in<br> proportion to its weight. For example, using a thousand distinct tenant<br> ids, each with a weight of 1.0 (the default) will result in each tenant<br> getting a roughly equal share of task dispatch throughput.<br><br> (Note: this does not imply equal share of worker capacity! Fairness<br> decisions are made based on queue statistics, not<br> current worker load.)<br><br> As another example, using keys "high" and "low" with weight 9.0 and 1.0<br> respectively will prefer dispatching "high" tasks over "low" tasks at a<br> 9:1 ratio, while allowing either key to use all worker capacity if the<br> other is not present.<br><br> All fairness mechanisms, including rate limits, are best-effort and<br> probabilistic. The results may not match what a "perfect" algorithm with<br> infinite resources would produce. The more unique keys are used, the less<br> accurate the results will be.<br><br> Fairness keys are limited to 64 bytes.|
|» » » fairnessWeight|body|number(float)|false|Fairness weight for a task can come from multiple sources for<br> flexibility. From highest to lowest precedence:<br> 1. Weights for a small set of keys can be overridden in task queue<br>    configuration with an API.<br> 2. It can be attached to the workflow/activity in this field.<br> 3. The default weight of 1.0 will be used.<br><br> Weight values are clamped to the range [0.001, 1000].|
|» » timeSkippingConfig|body|object|false|Time-skipping configuration for this workflow execution.<br> If not set, the time-skipping configuration is not updated by this request;<br> the existing configuration is preserved.|
|» » » enabled|body|boolean|false|Enables or disables time skipping for this workflow execution.|
|» » » maxSkippedDuration|body|string|false|Maximum total virtual time that can be skipped.|
|» » » maxElapsedDuration|body|string|false|Maximum elapsed time since time skipping was enabled.<br> This includes both skipped time and real time elapsing.|
|» updateMask|body|string(field-mask)|false|Controls which fields from `workflow_execution_options` will be applied.<br> To unset a field, set it to null and use the update mask to indicate that it should be mutated.|

```bash
  }'
```

`POST /cluster/namespaces`

RegisterNamespace creates a new namespace which can be used as a container for all resources.

 A Namespace is a top level entity within Temporal, and is used as a container for resources
 like workflow executions, task queues, etc. A Namespace acts as a sandbox and provides
 isolation for all resources within the namespace. All resources belongs to exactly one
 namespace.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "description": "string",
  "ownerEmail": "string",
  "workflowExecutionRetentionPeriod": "string",
  "clusters": [
    {
      "clusterName": "string"
    }
  ],
  "activeClusterName": "string",
  "data": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "securityToken": "string",
  "isGlobalNamespace": true,
  "historyArchivalState": "ARCHIVAL_STATE_UNSPECIFIED",
  "historyArchivalUri": "string",
  "visibilityArchivalState": "ARCHIVAL_STATE_UNSPECIFIED",
  "visibilityArchivalUri": "string"
}
```

## PauseActivity

<a id="opIdPauseActivity"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/namespaces/string/activities-deprecated/pause \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "namespace": "string",
    "execution": {
      "workflowId": "string",
      "runId": "string"
    },
    "identity": "string",
    "id": "string",
    "type": "string",
    "reason": "string",
    "requestId": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /namespaces/{namespace}/activities-deprecated/pause`

PauseActivity pauses the execution of an activity specified by its ID or type.
 If there are multiple pending activities of the provided type - all of them will be paused

 Pausing an activity means:
 - If the activity is currently waiting for a retry or is running and subsequently fails,
   it will not be rescheduled until it is unpaused.
 - If the activity is already paused, calling this method will have no effect.
 - If the activity is running and finishes successfully, the activity will be completed.
 - If the activity is running and finishes with failure:
   * if there is no retry left - the activity will be completed.
   * if there are more retries left - the activity will be paused.
 For long-running activities:
 - activities in paused state will send a cancellation with "activity_paused" set to 'true' in response to 'RecordActivityTaskHeartbeat'.
 - The activity should respond to the cancellation accordingly.

 Returns a `NotFound` error if there is no pending activity with the provided ID or type
 This API will be deprecated soon and replaced with a newer PauseActivityExecution that is better named and
 structured to work well for standalone activities.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "execution": {
    "workflowId": "string",
    "runId": "string"
  },
  "identity": "string",
  "id": "string",
  "type": "string",
  "reason": "string",
  "requestId": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="pauseactivity-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace of the workflow which scheduled this activity.|
|body|body|[PauseActivityRequest](#schemapauseactivityrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|Namespace of the workflow which scheduled this activity.|
|» execution|body|object|false|Execution info of the workflow which scheduled this activity|
|» » workflowId|body|string|false|none|
|» » runId|body|string|false|none|
|» identity|body|string|false|The identity of the client who initiated this request.|
|» id|body|string|false|Only the activity with this ID will be paused.|
|» type|body|string|false|Pause all running activities of this type.<br> Note: Experimental - the behavior of pause by activity type might change in a future release.|
|» reason|body|string|false|Reason to pause the activity.|
|» requestId|body|string|false|Used to de-dupe pause requests.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> default Response

```json
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "details": [
    {
      "@type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```
