<a id="opIdCreateWorkflowRule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/namespaces/string/workflow-rules \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "namespace": "string",
    "spec": {
      "id": "string",
      "activityStart": {
        "predicate": "string"
      },
      "visibilityQuery": "string",
      "actions": [
        {
          "activityPause": {}
        }
      ],
      "expirationTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    },
    "forceScan": true,
    "requestId": "string",
    "identity": "string",
    "description": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /namespaces/{namespace}/workflow-rules`

Create a new workflow rule. The rules are used to control the workflow execution.
 The rule will be applied to all running and new workflows in the namespace.
 If the rule with such ID already exist this call will fail
 Note: the rules are part of namespace configuration and will be stored in the namespace config.
 Namespace config is eventually consistent.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "spec": {
    "id": "string",
    "activityStart": {
      "predicate": "string"
    },
    "visibilityQuery": "string",
    "actions": [
      {
        "activityPause": {}
      }
    ],
    "expirationTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  },
  "forceScan": true,
  "requestId": "string",
  "identity": "string",
  "description": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="createworkflowrule-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[CreateWorkflowRuleRequest](#schemacreateworkflowrulerequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|none|
|» spec|body|object|false|The rule specification .|
|» » id|body|string|false|The id of the new workflow rule. Must be unique within the namespace.<br> Can be set by the user, and can have business meaning.|
|» » activityStart|body|[WorkflowRuleSpec_ActivityStartingTrigger](#schemaworkflowrulespec_activitystartingtrigger)|false|Activity trigger will be triggered when an activity is about to start.|
|» » visibilityQuery|body|string|false|Restricted Visibility query.<br> This query is used to filter workflows in this namespace to which this rule should apply.<br> It is applied to any running workflow each time a triggering event occurs, before the trigger predicate is evaluated.<br> The following workflow attributes are supported:<br> - WorkflowType<br> - WorkflowId<br> - StartTime<br> - ExecutionStatus|
|» » actions|body|[[WorkflowRuleAction](#schemaworkflowruleaction)]|false|WorkflowRuleAction to be taken when the rule is triggered and predicate is matched.|
|» » expirationTime|body|string(date-time)|false|Expiration time of the rule. After this time, the rule will be deleted.<br> Can be empty if the rule should never expire.|
|» forceScan|body|boolean|false|If true, the rule will be applied to the currently running workflows via batch job.<br> If not set , the rule will only be applied when triggering condition is satisfied.<br> visibility_query in the rule will be used to select the workflows to apply the rule to.|
|» requestId|body|string|false|Used to de-dupe requests. Typically should be UUID.|
|» identity|body|string|false|Identity of the actor who created the rule. Will be stored with the rule.|
|» description|body|string|false|Rule description.Will be stored with the rule.|

## GetWorkflowExecutionHistory

<a id="opIdGetWorkflowExecutionHistory"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/namespaces/string/workflows/string/history \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /namespaces/{namespace}/workflows/{execution.workflow_id}/history`

GetWorkflowExecutionHistory returns the history of specified workflow execution. Fails with
 `NotFound` if the specified workflow execution is unknown to the service.

<h3 id="getworkflowexecutionhistory-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|execution.workflow_id|path|string|true|none|
|execution.workflowId|query|string|false|none|
|execution.runId|query|string|false|none|
|maximumPageSize|query|integer(int32)|false|none|
|nextPageToken|query|string(bytes)|false|If a `GetWorkflowExecutionHistoryResponse` or a `PollWorkflowTaskQueueResponse` had one of<br> these, it should be passed here to fetch the next page.|
|waitNewEvent|query|boolean|false|If set to true, the RPC call will not resolve until there is a new event which matches<br> the `history_event_filter_type`, or a timeout is hit.|
|historyEventFilterType|query|string(enum)|false|Filter returned events such that they match the specified filter type.<br> Default: HISTORY_EVENT_FILTER_TYPE_ALL_EVENT.|
|skipArchival|query|boolean|false|none|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|historyEventFilterType|HISTORY_EVENT_FILTER_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED|
|historyEventFilterType|HISTORY_EVENT_FILTER_TYPE_ALL_EVENT|
|historyEventFilterType|HISTORY_EVENT_FILTER_TYPE_CLOSE_EVENT|

<aside class="success">

</aside>

## GetWorkflowExecutionHistoryReverse

<a id="opIdGetWorkflowExecutionHistoryReverse"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/namespaces/string/workflows/string/history-reverse \
  -H 'Accept: application/json'
```

`GET /namespaces/{namespace}/workflows/{execution.workflow_id}/history-reverse`

GetWorkflowExecutionHistoryReverse returns the history of specified workflow execution in reverse
 order (starting from last event). Fails with`NotFound` if the specified workflow execution is
 unknown to the service.

<h3 id="getworkflowexecutionhistoryreverse-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|execution.workflow_id|path|string|true|none|
|execution.workflowId|query|string|false|none|
|execution.runId|query|string|false|none|
|maximumPageSize|query|integer(int32)|false|none|
|nextPageToken|query|string(bytes)|false|none|

`POST /namespaces/{namespace}/workflows/{execution.workflow_id}/query/{query.query_type}`

QueryWorkflow requests a query be executed for a specified workflow execution.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "execution": {
    "workflowId": "string",
    "runId": "string"
  },
  "query": {
    "queryType": "string",
    "queryArgs": {
      "payloads": [
        null
      ]
    },
    "header": {
      "fields": {
        "property1": null,
        "property2": null
      }
    }
  },
  "queryRejectCondition": "QUERY_REJECT_CONDITION_UNSPECIFIED"
}
```

<h3 id="queryworkflow-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|execution.workflow_id|path|string|true|none|
|query.query_type|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[QueryWorkflowRequest](#schemaqueryworkflowrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|none|
|» execution|body|[WorkflowExecution](#schemaworkflowexecution)|false|Identifies a specific workflow within a namespace. Practically speaking, because run_id is a<br> uuid, a workflow execution is globally unique. Note that many commands allow specifying an empty<br> run id as a way of saying "target the latest run of the workflow".|
|» query|body|[WorkflowQuery](#schemaworkflowquery)|false|See https://docs.temporal.io/docs/concepts/queries/|
|» queryRejectCondition|body|string(enum)|false|QueryRejectCondition can used to reject the query if workflow state does not satisfy condition.<br> Default: QUERY_REJECT_CONDITION_NONE.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» queryRejectCondition|QUERY_REJECT_CONDITION_UNSPECIFIED|
|» queryRejectCondition|QUERY_REJECT_CONDITION_NONE|
|» queryRejectCondition|QUERY_REJECT_CONDITION_NOT_OPEN|
|» queryRejectCondition|QUERY_REJECT_CONDITION_NOT_COMPLETED_CLEANLY|

```json
    "payloads": [

    ]
```

## TriggerWorkflowRule

<a id="opIdTriggerWorkflowRule"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/namespaces/string/workflows/string/trigger-rule \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "namespace": "string",
    "execution": {
      "workflowId": "string",
      "runId": "string"
    },
    "id": "string",
    "spec": {
      "id": "string",
      "activityStart": {
        "predicate": "string"
      },
      "visibilityQuery": "string",
      "actions": [
        {
          "activityPause": {}
        }
      ],
      "expirationTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
    },
    "identity": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /namespaces/{namespace}/workflows/{execution.workflow_id}/trigger-rule`

TriggerWorkflowRule allows to:
  * trigger existing rule for a specific workflow execution;
  * trigger rule for a specific workflow execution without creating a rule;
 This is useful for one-off operations.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "execution": {
    "workflowId": "string",
    "runId": "string"
  },
  "id": "string",
  "spec": {
    "id": "string",
    "activityStart": {
      "predicate": "string"
    },
    "visibilityQuery": "string",
    "actions": [
      {
        "activityPause": {}
      }
    ],
    "expirationTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  },
  "identity": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="triggerworkflowrule-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|none|
|execution.workflow_id|path|string|true|none|
|body|body|[TriggerWorkflowRuleRequest](#schematriggerworkflowrulerequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|none|
|» execution|body|object|false|Execution info of the workflow which scheduled this activity|
|» » workflowId|body|string|false|none|
|» » runId|body|string|false|none|
|» id|body|string|false|none|
|» spec|body|object|false|Note: Rule ID and expiration date are not used in the trigger request.|
|» » id|body|string|false|The id of the new workflow rule. Must be unique within the namespace.<br> Can be set by the user, and can have business meaning.|
|» » activityStart|body|[WorkflowRuleSpec_ActivityStartingTrigger](#schemaworkflowrulespec_activitystartingtrigger)|false|Activity trigger will be triggered when an activity is about to start.|
|» » visibilityQuery|body|string|false|Restricted Visibility query.<br> This query is used to filter workflows in this namespace to which this rule should apply.<br> It is applied to any running workflow each time a triggering event occurs, before the trigger predicate is evaluated.<br> The following workflow attributes are supported:<br> - WorkflowType<br> - WorkflowId<br> - StartTime<br> - ExecutionStatus|
|» » actions|body|[[WorkflowRuleAction](#schemaworkflowruleaction)]|false|WorkflowRuleAction to be taken when the rule is triggered and predicate is matched.|
|» » expirationTime|body|string(date-time)|false|Expiration time of the rule. After this time, the rule will be deleted.<br> Can be empty if the rule should never expire.|
|» identity|body|string|false|The identity of the client who initiated this request|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "applied": true
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "details": [
    {
      "@type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|OK|[TriggerWorkflowRuleResponse](#schematriggerworkflowruleresponse)|
|default|Default|Default error response|[Status](#schemastatus)|

<aside class="success">
This operation does not require authentication

|» » behavior|body|string(enum)|false|Required.<br> Deprecated. Use `override`.|
|» » deployment|body|object|false|Required if behavior is `PINNED`. Must be null if behavior is `AUTO_UPGRADE`.<br> Identifies the worker deployment to pin the workflow to.<br> Deprecated. Use `override.pinned.version`.|
|» » » seriesName|body|string|false|Different versions of the same worker service/application are related together by having a<br> shared series name.<br> Out of all deployments of a series, one can be designated as the current deployment, which<br> receives new workflow executions and new tasks of workflows with<br> `VERSIONING_BEHAVIOR_AUTO_UPGRADE` versioning behavior.|
|» » » buildId|body|string|false|Build ID changes with each version of the worker when the worker program code and/or config<br> changes.|
|» » pinnedVersion|body|string|false|Required if behavior is `PINNED`. Must be absent if behavior is not `PINNED`.<br> Identifies the worker deployment version to pin the workflow to, in the format<br> "<deployment_name>.<build_id>".<br> Deprecated. Use `override.pinned.version`.|
|» onConflictOptions|body|object|false|Defines actions to be done to the existing running workflow when the conflict policy<br> WORKFLOW_ID_CONFLICT_POLICY_USE_EXISTING is used. If not set (ie., nil value) or set to a<br> empty object (ie., all options with default value), it won't do anything to the existing<br> running workflow. If set, it will add a history event to the running workflow.|
|» » attachRequestId|body|boolean|false|Attaches the request ID to the running execution.|
|» » attachCompletionCallbacks|body|boolean|false|Attaches the completion callbacks to the running execution.|
|» » attachLinks|body|boolean|false|Attaches the links to the running execution.|
|» priority|body|object|false|Priority metadata|
|» » priorityKey|body|integer(int32)|false|Priority key is a positive integer from 1 to n, where smaller integers<br> correspond to higher priorities (tasks run sooner). In general, tasks in<br> a queue should be processed in close to priority order, although small<br> deviations are possible.<br><br> The maximum priority value (minimum priority) is determined by server<br> configuration, and defaults to 5.<br><br> If priority is not present (or zero), then the effective priority will be<br> the default priority, which is calculated by (min+max)/2. With the<br> default max of 5, and min of 1, that comes out to 3.|
|» » fairnessKey|body|string|false|Fairness key is a short string that's used as a key for a fairness<br> balancing mechanism. It may correspond to a tenant id, or to a fixed<br> string like "high" or "low". The default is the empty string.<br><br> The fairness mechanism attempts to dispatch tasks for a given key in<br> proportion to its weight. For example, using a thousand distinct tenant<br> ids, each with a weight of 1.0 (the default) will result in each tenant<br> getting a roughly equal share of task dispatch throughput.<br><br> (Note: this does not imply equal share of worker capacity! Fairness<br> decisions are made based on queue statistics, not<br> current worker load.)<br><br> As another example, using keys "high" and "low" with weight 9.0 and 1.0<br> respectively will prefer dispatching "high" tasks over "low" tasks at a<br> 9:1 ratio, while allowing either key to use all worker capacity if the<br> other is not present.<br><br> All fairness mechanisms, including rate limits, are best-effort and<br> probabilistic. The results may not match what a "perfect" algorithm with<br> infinite resources would produce. The more unique keys are used, the less<br> accurate the results will be.<br><br> Fairness keys are limited to 64 bytes.|
|» » fairnessWeight|body|number(float)|false|Fairness weight for a task can come from multiple sources for<br> flexibility. From highest to lowest precedence:<br> 1. Weights for a small set of keys can be overridden in task queue<br>    configuration with an API.<br> 2. It can be attached to the workflow/activity in this field.<br> 3. The default weight of 1.0 will be used.<br><br> Weight values are clamped to the range [0.001, 1000].|
|» eagerWorkerDeploymentOptions|body|object|false|Deployment Options of the worker who will process the eager task. Passed when `request_eager_execution=true`.|
|» » deploymentName|body|string|false|Required when `worker_versioning_mode==VERSIONED`.|
|» » buildId|body|string|false|The Build ID of the worker. Required when `worker_versioning_mode==VERSIONED`, in which case,<br> the worker will be part of a Deployment Version.|
|» » workerVersioningMode|body|string(enum)|false|Required. Versioning Mode for this worker. Must be the same for all workers with the<br> same `deployment_name` and `build_id` combination, across all Task Queues.<br> When `worker_versioning_mode==VERSIONED`, the worker will be part of a Deployment Version.|
|» timeSkippingConfig|body|object|false|Time-skipping configuration. If not set, time skipping is disabled.|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|Enables or disables time skipping for this workflow execution.|
|» » maxSkippedDuration|body|string|false|Maximum total virtual time that can be skipped.|
|» » maxElapsedDuration|body|string|false|Maximum elapsed time since time skipping was enabled.<br> This includes both skipped time and real time elapsing.|

## PauseActivityExecution

<a id="opIdPauseActivityExecution"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/namespaces/string/workflows/string/activities/string/pause \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "namespace": "string",
    "workflowId": "string",
    "activityId": "string",
    "runId": "string",
    "identity": "string",
    "reason": "string",
    "resourceId": "string",
    "requestId": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /namespaces/{namespace}/workflows/{workflowId}/activities/{activityId}/pause`

PauseActivityExecution pauses the execution of an activity specified by its ID.
 This API can be used to target a workflow activity or a standalone activity

 Pausing an activity means:
 - If the activity is currently waiting for a retry or is running and subsequently fails,
   it will not be rescheduled until it is unpaused.
 - If the activity is already paused, calling this method will have no effect.
 - If the activity is running and finishes successfully, the activity will be completed.
 - If the activity is running and finishes with failure:
   * if there is no retry left - the activity will be completed.
   * if there are more retries left - the activity will be paused.
 For long-running activities:
 - activities in paused state will send a cancellation with "activity_paused" set to 'true' in response to 'RecordActivityTaskHeartbeat'.

 Returns a `NotFound` error if there is no pending activity with the provided ID

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "workflowId": "string",
  "activityId": "string",
  "runId": "string",
  "identity": "string",
  "reason": "string",
  "resourceId": "string",
  "requestId": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="pauseactivityexecution-3-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace of the workflow which scheduled this activity.|

## ResetActivityExecution

<a id="opIdResetActivityExecution"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/namespaces/string/workflows/string/activities/string/reset \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \

  -d '{
    "namespace": "string",
    "workflowId": "string",
    "activityId": "string",
    "runId": "string",
    "identity": "string",
    "resetHeartbeat": true,
    "keepPaused": true,
    "jitter": "string",
    "restoreOriginalOptions": true,
    "resourceId": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /namespaces/{namespace}/workflows/{workflowId}/activities/{activityId}/reset`

ResetActivityExecution resets the execution of an activity specified by its ID.
 This API can be used to target a workflow activity or a standalone activity.

 Resetting an activity means:
 * number of attempts will be reset to 0.
 * activity timeouts will be reset.
 * if the activity is waiting for retry, and it is not paused or 'keep_paused' is not provided:
    it will be scheduled immediately (* see 'jitter' flag)

 Returns a `NotFound` error if there is no pending activity with the provided ID or type.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "workflowId": "string",
  "activityId": "string",
  "runId": "string",
  "identity": "string",
  "resetHeartbeat": true,
  "keepPaused": true,
  "jitter": "string",
  "restoreOriginalOptions": true,
  "resourceId": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="resetactivityexecution-3-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace of the workflow which scheduled this activity.|
|workflowId|path|string|true|If provided, targets a workflow activity for the given workflow ID.<br> If empty, targets a standalone activity.|
|activityId|path|string|true|The ID of the activity to target.|
|body|body|[ResetActivityExecutionRequest](#schemaresetactivityexecutionrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|Namespace of the workflow which scheduled this activity.|
|» workflowId|body|string|false|If provided, targets a workflow activity for the given workflow ID.<br> If empty, targets a standalone activity.|
|» activityId|body|string|false|The ID of the activity to target.|
|» runId|body|string|false|Run ID of the workflow or standalone activity.|
|» identity|body|string|false|The identity of the client who initiated this request.|
|» resetHeartbeat|body|boolean|false|Indicates that activity should reset heartbeat details.<br> This flag will be applied only to the new instance of the activity.|
|» keepPaused|body|boolean|false|If activity is paused, it will remain paused after reset|
|» jitter|body|string|false|If set, and activity is in backoff, the activity will start at a random time within the specified jitter duration.<br> (unless it is paused and keep_paused is set)|
|» restoreOriginalOptions|body|boolean|false|If set, the activity options will be restored to the defaults.<br> Default options are then options activity was created with.<br> They are part of the first schedule event.|
|» resourceId|body|string|false|Resource ID for routing. Contains "workflow:{workflow_id}" for workflow activities or "activity:{activity_id}" for standalone activities.|

```json
{}
```

```json
    }
```

`POST /namespaces/{namespace}/workflows/{workflowId}/activities/{activityId}/unpause`

UnpauseActivityExecution unpauses the execution of an activity specified by its ID.
 This API can be used to target a workflow activity or a standalone activity.

 If activity is not paused, this call will have no effect.
 If the activity was paused while waiting for retry, it will be scheduled immediately (* see 'jitter' flag).
 Once the activity is unpaused, all timeout timers will be regenerated.

 Returns a `NotFound` error if there is no pending activity with the provided ID

> Body parameter

|» » » maximumAttempts|body|integer(int32)|false|Maximum number of attempts. When exceeded the retries stop even if not expired yet.<br> 1 disables retries. 0 means unlimited (up to the timeouts)|
|» » » nonRetryableErrorTypes|body|[string]|false|Non-Retryable errors types. Will stop retrying if the error type matches this list. Note that<br> this is not a substring match, the error *type* (not message) must match exactly.|

|» » » priorityKey|body|integer(int32)|false|Priority key is a positive integer from 1 to n, where smaller integers<br> correspond to higher priorities (tasks run sooner). In general, tasks in<br> a queue should be processed in close to priority order, although small<br> deviations are possible.<br><br> The maximum priority value (minimum priority) is determined by server<br> configuration, and defaults to 5.<br><br> If priority is not present (or zero), then the effective priority will be<br> the default priority, which is calculated by (min+max)/2. With the<br> default max of 5, and min of 1, that comes out to 3.|
|» » » fairnessKey|body|string|false|Fairness key is a short string that's used as a key for a fairness<br> balancing mechanism. It may correspond to a tenant id, or to a fixed<br> string like "high" or "low". The default is the empty string.<br><br> The fairness mechanism attempts to dispatch tasks for a given key in<br> proportion to its weight. For example, using a thousand distinct tenant<br> ids, each with a weight of 1.0 (the default) will result in each tenant<br> getting a roughly equal share of task dispatch throughput.<br><br> (Note: this does not imply equal share of worker capacity! Fairness<br> decisions are made based on queue statistics, not<br> current worker load.)<br><br> As another example, using keys "high" and "low" with weight 9.0 and 1.0<br> respectively will prefer dispatching "high" tasks over "low" tasks at a<br> 9:1 ratio, while allowing either key to use all worker capacity if the<br> other is not present.<br><br> All fairness mechanisms, including rate limits, are best-effort and<br> probabilistic. The results may not match what a "perfect" algorithm with<br> infinite resources would produce. The more unique keys are used, the less<br> accurate the results will be.<br><br> Fairness keys are limited to 64 bytes.|
|» » » fairnessWeight|body|number(float)|false|Fairness weight for a task can come from multiple sources for<br> flexibility. From highest to lowest precedence:<br> 1. Weights for a small set of keys can be overridden in task queue<br>    configuration with an API.<br> 2. It can be attached to the workflow/activity in this field.<br> 3. The default weight of 1.0 will be used.<br><br> Weight values are clamped to the range [0.001, 1000].|

## PauseWorkflowExecution

<a id="opIdPauseWorkflowExecution"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl http://localhost:7243/namespaces/string/workflows/string/pause \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -d '{
    "namespace": "string",
    "workflowId": "string",
    "runId": "string",
    "identity": "string",
    "reason": "string",
    "requestId": "string"
  }'
```

`POST /namespaces/{namespace}/workflows/{workflowId}/pause`

Note: This is an experimental API and the behavior may change in a future release.
 PauseWorkflowExecution pauses the workflow execution specified in the request. Pausing a workflow execution results in
 - The workflow execution status changes to `PAUSED` and a new WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_PAUSED event is added to the history
 - No new workflow tasks or activity tasks are dispatched.
   - Any workflow task currently executing on the worker will be allowed to complete.
   - Any activity task currently executing will be paused.
 - All server-side events will continue to be processed by the server.
 - Queries & Updates on a paused workflow will be rejected.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "workflowId": "string",
  "runId": "string",
  "identity": "string",
  "reason": "string",
  "requestId": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="pauseworkflowexecution-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace of the workflow to pause.|
|workflowId|path|string|true|ID of the workflow execution to be paused. Required.|
|body|body|[PauseWorkflowExecutionRequest](#schemapauseworkflowexecutionrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|Namespace of the workflow to pause.|
|» workflowId|body|string|false|ID of the workflow execution to be paused. Required.|
|» runId|body|string|false|Run ID of the workflow execution to be paused. Optional. If not provided, the current run of the workflow will be paused.|
|» identity|body|string|false|The identity of the client who initiated this request.|
|» reason|body|string|false|Reason to pause the workflow execution.|
|» requestId|body|string|false|A unique identifier for this pause request for idempotence. Typically UUIDv4.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",

    {
      "@type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

`POST /namespaces/{namespace}/workflows/{workflowId}/signal-with-start/{signalName}`

SignalWithStartWorkflowExecution is used to ensure a signal is sent to a workflow, even if
 it isn't yet started.

 If the workflow is running, a `WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_SIGNALED` event is recorded in the history
 and a workflow task is generated.

 If the workflow is not running or not found, then the workflow is created with
 `WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_STARTED` and `WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_SIGNALED` events in its history, and a
 workflow task is generated.

 (-- api-linter: core::0136::prepositions=disabled
     aip.dev/not-precedent: "With" is used to indicate combined operation. --)

|» » priorityKey|body|integer(int32)|false|Priority key is a positive integer from 1 to n, where smaller integers<br> correspond to higher priorities (tasks run sooner). In general, tasks in<br> a queue should be processed in close to priority order, although small<br> deviations are possible.<br><br> The maximum priority value (minimum priority) is determined by server<br> configuration, and defaults to 5.<br><br> If priority is not present (or zero), then the effective priority will be<br> the default priority, which is calculated by (min+max)/2. With the<br> default max of 5, and min of 1, that comes out to 3.|
|» » fairnessKey|body|string|false|Fairness key is a short string that's used as a key for a fairness<br> balancing mechanism. It may correspond to a tenant id, or to a fixed<br> string like "high" or "low". The default is the empty string.<br><br> The fairness mechanism attempts to dispatch tasks for a given key in<br> proportion to its weight. For example, using a thousand distinct tenant<br> ids, each with a weight of 1.0 (the default) will result in each tenant<br> getting a roughly equal share of task dispatch throughput.<br><br> (Note: this does not imply equal share of worker capacity! Fairness<br> decisions are made based on queue statistics, not<br> current worker load.)<br><br> As another example, using keys "high" and "low" with weight 9.0 and 1.0<br> respectively will prefer dispatching "high" tasks over "low" tasks at a<br> 9:1 ratio, while allowing either key to use all worker capacity if the<br> other is not present.<br><br> All fairness mechanisms, including rate limits, are best-effort and<br> probabilistic. The results may not match what a "perfect" algorithm with<br> infinite resources would produce. The more unique keys are used, the less<br> accurate the results will be.<br><br> Fairness keys are limited to 64 bytes.|
|» » fairnessWeight|body|number(float)|false|Fairness weight for a task can come from multiple sources for<br> flexibility. From highest to lowest precedence:<br> 1. Weights for a small set of keys can be overridden in task queue<br>    configuration with an API.<br> 2. It can be attached to the workflow/activity in this field.<br> 3. The default weight of 1.0 will be used.<br><br> Weight values are clamped to the range [0.001, 1000].|
|» timeSkippingConfig|body|object|false|Time-skipping configuration. If not set, time skipping is disabled.|
|» » enabled|body|boolean|false|Enables or disables time skipping for this workflow execution.|
|» » maxSkippedDuration|body|string|false|Maximum total virtual time that can be skipped.|
|» » maxElapsedDuration|body|string|false|Maximum elapsed time since time skipping was enabled.<br> This includes both skipped time and real time elapsing.|

`POST /namespaces/{namespace}/workflows/{workflowId}/unpause`

Note: This is an experimental API and the behavior may change in a future release.
 UnpauseWorkflowExecution unpauses a previously paused workflow execution specified in the request.
 Unpausing a workflow execution results in
 - The workflow execution status changes to `RUNNING` and a new WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_UNPAUSED event is added to the history
 - Workflow tasks and activity tasks are resumed.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "workflowId": "string",
  "runId": "string",
  "identity": "string",
  "reason": "string",
  "requestId": "string"
}
```

<h3 id="unpauseworkflowexecution-1-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|path|string|true|Namespace of the workflow to unpause.|
|workflowId|path|string|true|ID of the workflow execution to be paused. Required.|
|body|body|[UnpauseWorkflowExecutionRequest](#schemaunpauseworkflowexecutionrequest)|true|none|
|» namespace|body|string|false|Namespace of the workflow to unpause.|
|» workflowId|body|string|false|ID of the workflow execution to be paused. Required.|
|» runId|body|string|false|Run ID of the workflow execution to be paused. Optional. If not provided, the current run of the workflow will be paused.|
|» identity|body|string|false|The identity of the client who initiated this request.|
|» reason|body|string|false|Reason to unpause the workflow execution.|
|» requestId|body|string|false|A unique identifier for this unpause request for idempotence. Typically UUIDv4.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{}
```

```json
    {
      "@type": "string"

  ]
}
```

`POST /namespaces/{namespace}/workflows/{workflow_execution.workflow_id}/cancel`

RequestCancelWorkflowExecution is called by workers when they want to request cancellation of
 a workflow execution.

 This results in a new `WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_CANCEL_REQUESTED` event being written to the
 workflow history and a new workflow task created for the workflow. It returns success if the requested
 workflow is already closed. It fails with 'NotFound' if the requested workflow doesn't exist.

> Body parameter

```json
  "namespace": "string",
  "workflowExecution": {
    "workflowId": "string",
    "runId": "string"
  },

  "firstExecutionRunId": "string",
  "reason": "string",
  "links": [

          "eventType": "EVENT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED"
        },
        "requestIdRef": {

          "eventType": "EVENT_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED"
        }
      },

      },

}
```

`POST /namespaces/{namespace}/workflows/{workflow_execution.workflow_id}/reset`

ResetWorkflowExecution will reset an existing workflow execution to a specified
 `WORKFLOW_TASK_COMPLETED` event (exclusive). It will immediately terminate the current
 execution instance. "Exclusive" means the identified completed event itself is not replayed
 in the reset history; the preceding `WORKFLOW_TASK_STARTED` event remains and will be marked as failed
 immediately, and a new workflow task will be scheduled to retry it.

|» » » pinnedVersion|body|string|false|Required if behavior is `PINNED`. Must be absent if behavior is not `PINNED`.<br> Identifies the worker deployment version to pin the workflow to, in the format<br> "<deployment_name>.<build_id>".<br> Deprecated. Use `override.pinned.version`.|
|» » priority|body|object|false|If set, overrides the workflow's priority sent by the SDK.|
|» » » priorityKey|body|integer(int32)|false|Priority key is a positive integer from 1 to n, where smaller integers<br> correspond to higher priorities (tasks run sooner). In general, tasks in<br> a queue should be processed in close to priority order, although small<br> deviations are possible.<br><br> The maximum priority value (minimum priority) is determined by server<br> configuration, and defaults to 5.<br><br> If priority is not present (or zero), then the effective priority will be<br> the default priority, which is calculated by (min+max)/2. With the<br> default max of 5, and min of 1, that comes out to 3.|
|» » » fairnessKey|body|string|false|Fairness key is a short string that's used as a key for a fairness<br> balancing mechanism. It may correspond to a tenant id, or to a fixed<br> string like "high" or "low". The default is the empty string.<br><br> The fairness mechanism attempts to dispatch tasks for a given key in<br> proportion to its weight. For example, using a thousand distinct tenant<br> ids, each with a weight of 1.0 (the default) will result in each tenant<br> getting a roughly equal share of task dispatch throughput.<br><br> (Note: this does not imply equal share of worker capacity! Fairness<br> decisions are made based on queue statistics, not<br> current worker load.)<br><br> As another example, using keys "high" and "low" with weight 9.0 and 1.0<br> respectively will prefer dispatching "high" tasks over "low" tasks at a<br> 9:1 ratio, while allowing either key to use all worker capacity if the<br> other is not present.<br><br> All fairness mechanisms, including rate limits, are best-effort and<br> probabilistic. The results may not match what a "perfect" algorithm with<br> infinite resources would produce. The more unique keys are used, the less<br> accurate the results will be.<br><br> Fairness keys are limited to 64 bytes.|
|» » » fairnessWeight|body|number(float)|false|Fairness weight for a task can come from multiple sources for<br> flexibility. From highest to lowest precedence:<br> 1. Weights for a small set of keys can be overridden in task queue<br>    configuration with an API.<br> 2. It can be attached to the workflow/activity in this field.<br> 3. The default weight of 1.0 will be used.<br><br> Weight values are clamped to the range [0.001, 1000].|
|» » timeSkippingConfig|body|object|false|Time-skipping configuration for this workflow execution.<br> If not set, the time-skipping configuration is not updated by this request;<br> the existing configuration is preserved.|
|» » » enabled|body|boolean|false|Enables or disables time skipping for this workflow execution.|
|» » » maxSkippedDuration|body|string|false|Maximum total virtual time that can be skipped.|
|» » » maxElapsedDuration|body|string|false|Maximum elapsed time since time skipping was enabled.<br> This includes both skipped time and real time elapsing.|
|» updateMask|body|string(field-mask)|false|Controls which fields from `workflow_execution_options` will be applied.<br> To unset a field, set it to null and use the update mask to indicate that it should be mutated.|
|» identity|body|string|false|Optional. The identity of the client who initiated this request.|

### Properties

|---|---|---|---|---|
|activityId|string|false|none|Unique identifier of this activity within its namespace along with run ID (below).|

|activityType|object|false|none|The type of the activity, a string that maps to a registered activity on a worker.|
|status|string(enum)|false|none|A general status for this activity, indicates whether it is currently running or in one of the terminal statuses.|
|runState|string(enum)|false|none|More detailed breakdown of ACTIVITY_EXECUTION_STATUS_RUNNING.|
|taskQueue|string|false|none|none|
|scheduleToCloseTimeout|string|false|none|Indicates how long the caller is willing to wait for an activity completion. Limits how long<br> retries will be attempted.<br><br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "to" is used to indicate interval. --)|
|scheduleToStartTimeout|string|false|none|Limits time an activity task can stay in a task queue before a worker picks it up. This<br> timeout is always non retryable, as all a retry would achieve is to put it back into the same<br> queue. Defaults to `schedule_to_close_timeout`.<br><br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "to" is used to indicate interval. --)|
|startToCloseTimeout|string|false|none|Maximum time a single activity attempt is allowed to execute after being picked up by a worker. This<br> timeout is always retryable.<br><br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "to" is used to indicate interval. --)|
|heartbeatTimeout|string|false|none|Maximum permitted time between successful worker heartbeats.|
|retryPolicy|object|false|none|The retry policy for the activity. Will never exceed `schedule_to_close_timeout`.|
|heartbeatDetails|object|false|none|Details provided in the last recorded activity heartbeat.|
|lastHeartbeatTime|string(date-time)|false|none|Time the last heartbeat was recorded.|
|lastStartedTime|string(date-time)|false|none|Time the last attempt was started.|
|attempt|integer(int32)|false|none|The attempt this activity is currently on. Incremented each time a new attempt is scheduled.|
|executionDuration|string|false|none|How long this activity has been running for, including all attempts and backoff between attempts.|
|scheduleTime|string(date-time)|false|none|Time the activity was originally scheduled via a StartActivityExecution request.|
|expirationTime|string(date-time)|false|none|Scheduled time + schedule to close timeout.|
|closeTime|string(date-time)|false|none|Time when the activity transitioned to a closed state.|
|lastFailure|object|false|none|Failure details from the last failed attempt.|
|lastWorkerIdentity|string|false|none|none|
|currentRetryInterval|string|false|none|Time from the last attempt failure to the next activity retry.<br> If the activity is currently running, this represents the next retry interval in case the attempt fails.<br> If activity is currently backing off between attempt, this represents the current retry interval.<br> If there is no next retry allowed, this field will be null.<br> This interval is typically calculated from the specified retry policy, but may be modified if an activity fails<br> with a retryable application failure specifying a retry delay.|
|lastAttemptCompleteTime|string(date-time)|false|none|The time when the last activity attempt completed. If activity has not been completed yet, it will be null.|
|nextAttemptScheduleTime|string(date-time)|false|none|The time when the next activity attempt will be scheduled.<br> If activity is currently scheduled or started, this field will be null.|
|lastDeploymentVersion|object|false|none|The Worker Deployment Version this activity was dispatched to most recently.<br> If nil, the activity has not yet been dispatched or was last dispatched to an unversioned worker.|
|priority|object|false|none|Priority metadata.|
|stateTransitionCount|string|false|none|Incremented each time the activity's state is mutated in persistence.|
|stateSizeBytes|string|false|none|Updated once on scheduled and once on terminal status.|
|searchAttributes|[SearchAttributes](#schemasearchattributes)|false|none|A user-defined set of *indexed* fields that are used/exposed when listing/searching workflows.<br> The payload is not serialized in a user-defined way.|
|header|[Header](#schemaheader)|false|none|Contains metadata that can be attached to a variety of requests, like starting a workflow, and<br> can be propagated between, for example, workflows and activities.|
|userMetadata|object|false|none|Metadata for use by user interfaces to display the fixed as-of-start summary and details of the activity.|
|canceledReason|string|false|none|Set if activity cancelation was requested.|
|links|[[Link](#schemalink)]|false|none|Links to related entities, such as the entity that started this activity.|
|totalHeartbeatCount|string|false|none|Total number of heartbeats recorded across all attempts of this activity, including retries.|

<h2 id="tocS_BuildIdAssignmentRule">BuildIdAssignmentRule</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemabuildidassignmentrule"></a>
<a id="schema_BuildIdAssignmentRule"></a>
<a id="tocSbuildidassignmentrule"></a>
<a id="tocsbuildidassignmentrule"></a>

```json
{
  "targetBuildId": "string",
  "percentageRamp": {
    "rampPercentage": 0
  }
}
```

Assignment rules are applied to *new* Workflow and Activity executions at
 schedule time to assign them to a Build ID.

 Assignment rules will not be used in the following cases:
    - Child Workflows or Continue-As-New Executions who inherit their
      parent/previous Workflow's assigned Build ID (by setting the
      `inherit_build_id` flag - default behavior in SDKs when the same Task Queue
      is used.)
    - An Activity that inherits the assigned Build ID of its Workflow (by
      setting the `use_workflow_build_id` flag - default behavior in SDKs
      when the same Task Queue is used.)

 In absence of (applicable) redirect rules (`CompatibleBuildIdRedirectRule`s)
 the task will be dispatched to Workers of the Build ID determined by the
 assignment rules (or inherited). Otherwise, the final Build ID will be
 determined by the redirect rules.

 Once a Workflow completes its first Workflow Task in a particular Build ID it
 stays in that Build ID regardless of changes to assignment rules. Redirect
 rules can be used to move the workflow to another compatible Build ID.

 When using Worker Versioning on a Task Queue, in the steady state,
 there should typically be a single assignment rule to send all new executions
 to the latest Build ID. Existence of at least one such "unconditional"
 rule at all times is enforces by the system, unless the `force` flag is used
 by the user when replacing/deleting these rules (for exceptional cases).

 During a deployment, one or more additional rules can be added to assign a
 subset of the tasks to a new Build ID based on a "ramp percentage".

 When there are multiple assignment rules for a Task Queue, the rules are
 evaluated in order, starting from index 0. The first applicable rule will be
 applied and the rest will be ignored.

 In the event that no assignment rule is applicable on a task (or the Task
 Queue is simply not versioned), the tasks will be dispatched to an
 unversioned Worker.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|targetBuildId|string|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_CalendarSpec">CalendarSpec</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacalendarspec"></a>
<a id="schema_CalendarSpec"></a>
<a id="tocScalendarspec"></a>
<a id="tocscalendarspec"></a>

```json
{
  "second": "string",
  "minute": "string",
  "hour": "string",
  "dayOfMonth": "string",
  "month": "string",
  "year": "string",
  "dayOfWeek": "string",
  "comment": "string"
}
```

CalendarSpec describes an event specification relative to the calendar,
 similar to a traditional cron specification, but with labeled fields. Each
 field can be one of:
   *: matches always
   x: matches when the field equals x
   x/y : matches when the field equals x+n*y where n is an integer
   x-z: matches when the field is between x and z inclusive
   w,x,y,...: matches when the field is one of the listed values
 Each x, y, z, ... is either a decimal integer, or a month or day of week name
 or abbreviation (in the appropriate fields).
 A timestamp matches if all fields match.
 Note that fields have different default values, for convenience.
 Note that the special case that some cron implementations have for treating
 day_of_month and day_of_week as "or" instead of "and" when both are set is
 not implemented.
 day_of_week can accept 0 or 7 as Sunday
 CalendarSpec gets compiled into StructuredCalendarSpec, which is what will be
 returned if you describe the schedule.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|second|string|false|none|Expression to match seconds. Default: 0|
|minute|string|false|none|Expression to match minutes. Default: 0|
|hour|string|false|none|Expression to match hours. Default: 0|
|dayOfMonth|string|false|none|Expression to match days of the month. Default: *<br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: standard name of field --)|
|month|string|false|none|Expression to match months. Default: *|
|year|string|false|none|Expression to match years. Default: *|
|dayOfWeek|string|false|none|Expression to match days of the week. Default: *|
|comment|string|false|none|Free-form comment describing the intention of this spec.|

<h2 id="tocS_CompatibleBuildIdRedirectRule">CompatibleBuildIdRedirectRule</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemacompatiblebuildidredirectrule"></a>
<a id="schema_CompatibleBuildIdRedirectRule"></a>
<a id="tocScompatiblebuildidredirectrule"></a>
<a id="tocscompatiblebuildidredirectrule"></a>

```json
{
  "sourceBuildId": "string",
  "targetBuildId": "string"
}
```

These rules apply to tasks assigned to a particular Build ID
 (`source_build_id`) to redirect them to another *compatible* Build ID
 (`target_build_id`).

 It is user's responsibility to ensure that the target Build ID is compatible
 with the source Build ID (e.g. by using the Patching API).

 Most deployments are not expected to need these rules, however following
 situations can greatly benefit from redirects:
  - Need to move long-running Workflow Executions from an old Build ID to a
    newer one.
  - Need to hotfix some broken or stuck Workflow Executions.

 In steady state, redirect rules are beneficial when dealing with old
 Executions ran on now-decommissioned Build IDs:
  - To redirecting the Workflow Queries to the current (compatible) Build ID.
  - To be able to Reset an old Execution so it can run on the current
    (compatible) Build ID.

 Redirect rules can be chained.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sourceBuildId|string|false|none|none|
|targetBuildId|string|false|none|Target Build ID must be compatible with the Source Build ID; that is it<br> must be able to process event histories made by the Source Build ID by<br> using [Patching](https://docs.temporal.io/workflows#patching) or other<br> means.|

ComputeProvider stores information used by a worker control plane controller
 to respond to worker lifecycle events. For example, when a Task is received
 on a TaskQueue that has no active pollers, a serverless worker lifecycle
 controller might need to invoke an AWS Lambda Function that itself ends up
 calling the SDK's worker.New() function.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|type|string|false|none|Type of the compute provider. This string is implementation-specific and<br> can be used by implementations to understand how to interpret the<br> contents of the provider_details field.|
|details|object|false|none|Contains provider-specific instructions and configuration.<br> For server-implemented providers, use the SDK's default content<br> converter to ensure the server can understand it.<br> For remote-implemented providers, you might use your own content<br> converters according to what the remote endpoints understand.|
|nexusEndpoint|string|false|none|Optional. If the compute provider is a Nexus service, this should point<br> there.|

`Deployment` identifies a deployment of Temporal workers. The combination of deployment series
 name + build ID serves as the identifier. User can use `WorkerDeploymentOptions` in their worker
 programs to specify these values.
 Deprecated.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|seriesName|string|false|none|Different versions of the same worker service/application are related together by having a<br> shared series name.<br> Out of all deployments of a series, one can be designated as the current deployment, which<br> receives new workflow executions and new tasks of workflows with<br> `VERSIONING_BEHAVIOR_AUTO_UPGRADE` versioning behavior.|
|buildId|string|false|none|Build ID changes with each version of the worker when the worker program code and/or config<br> changes.|

|outcome|object|false|none|Only set if the activity is completed and include_outcome was true in the request.|
|longPollToken|string(bytes)|false|none|Token for follow-on long-poll requests. Absent only if the activity is complete.|
|callbacks|[[CallbackInfo](#schemacallbackinfo)]|false|none|Callbacks attached to this activity execution and their current state.|

|memo|object|false|none|The memo and search attributes that the schedule was created with.|
|searchAttributes|[SearchAttributes](#schemasearchattributes)|false|none|A user-defined set of *indexed* fields that are used/exposed when listing/searching workflows.<br> The payload is not serialized in a user-defined way.|
|conflictToken|string(bytes)|false|none|This value can be passed back to UpdateSchedule to ensure that the<br> schedule was not modified between a Describe and an Update, which could<br> lead to lost updates and other confusion.|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pollers|[[PollerInfo](#schemapollerinfo)]|false|none|none|
|stats|object|false|none|Statistics for the task queue.<br> Only set if `report_stats` is set on the request.|
|statsByPriorityKey|object|false|none|Task queue stats breakdown by priority key. Only contains actively used priority keys.<br> Only set if `report_stats` is set on the request.<br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "by" is used to clarify the keys and values. --)|
|versioningInfo|object|false|none|Specifies which Worker Deployment Version(s) Server routes this Task Queue's tasks to.<br> When not present, it means the tasks are routed to Unversioned workers (workers with<br> UNVERSIONED or unspecified WorkerVersioningMode.)<br> Task Queue Versioning info is updated indirectly by calling SetWorkerDeploymentCurrentVersion<br> and SetWorkerDeploymentRampingVersion on Worker Deployments.<br> Note: This information is not relevant to Pinned workflow executions and their activities as<br> they are always routed to their Pinned Deployment Version. However, new workflow executions<br> are typically not Pinned until they complete their first task (unless they are started with<br> a Pinned VersioningOverride or are Child Workflows of a Pinned parent).|
|config|object|false|none|Only populated if report_task_queue_config is set to true.|
|effectiveRateLimit|[DescribeTaskQueueResponse_EffectiveRateLimit](#schemadescribetaskqueueresponse_effectiveratelimit)|false|none|none|
|taskQueueStatus|object|false|none|Deprecated.<br> Status of the task queue. Only populated when `include_task_queue_status` is set to true in the request.|
|versionsInfo|object|false|none|Deprecated.<br> Only returned in ENHANCED mode.<br> This map contains Task Queue information for each Build ID. Empty string as key value means unversioned.|

|internalErrorDifferentiation|boolean|false|none|True if internal errors are differentiated from other types of errors for purposes of<br> retrying non-internal errors.<br><br> When unset/false, clients retry all failures. When true, clients should only retry<br> non-internal errors.|
|activityFailureIncludeHeartbeat|boolean|false|none|True if RespondActivityTaskFailed API supports including heartbeat details|
|supportsSchedules|boolean|false|none|Supports scheduled workflow features.|
|encodedFailureAttributes|boolean|false|none|True if server uses protos that include temporal.api.failure.v1.Failure.encoded_attributes|
|buildIdBasedVersioning|boolean|false|none|True if server supports dispatching Workflow and Activity tasks based on a worker's build_id<br> (see:<br> https://github.com/temporalio/proposals/blob/a123af3b559f43db16ea6dd31870bfb754c4dc5e/versioning/worker-versions.md)|
|upsertMemo|boolean|false|none|True if server supports upserting workflow memo|
|eagerWorkflowStart|boolean|false|none|True if server supports eager workflow task dispatching for the StartWorkflowExecution API|
|sdkMetadata|boolean|false|none|True if the server knows about the sdk metadata field on WFT completions and will record<br> it in history|
|countGroupByExecutionStatus|boolean|false|none|True if the server supports count group by execution status|
|nexus|boolean|false|none|True if the server supports Nexus operations.<br> This flag is dependent both on server version and for Nexus to be enabled via server configuration.|
|serverScaledDeployments|boolean|false|none|True if the server supports server-scaled deployments.<br> This flag is dependent both on server version and for server-scaled deployments<br> to be enabled via server configuration.|

```json
{
  "majorVersionSets": [
    {
      "buildIds": [
        "string"
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

[cleanup-wv-pre-release]

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|majorVersionSets|[[CompatibleVersionSet](#schemacompatibleversionset)]|false|none|Major version sets, in order from oldest to newest. The last element of the list will always<br> be the current default major version. IE: New workflows will target the most recent version<br> in that version set.<br><br> There may be fewer sets returned than exist, if the request chose to limit this response.|

<h2 id="tocS_GetWorkerTaskReachabilityResponse">GetWorkerTaskReachabilityResponse</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemagetworkertaskreachabilityresponse"></a>
<a id="schema_GetWorkerTaskReachabilityResponse"></a>
<a id="tocSgetworkertaskreachabilityresponse"></a>
<a id="tocsgetworkertaskreachabilityresponse"></a>

```json
{
  "buildIdReachability": [
    {
      "buildId": "string",
      "taskQueueReachability": [
        {
          "taskQueue": "string",
          "reachability": [
            "TASK_REACHABILITY_UNSPECIFIED"
          ]
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

[cleanup-wv-pre-release]
 Deprecated. Use `DescribeTaskQueue`.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|buildIdReachability|[[BuildIdReachability](#schemabuildidreachability)]|false|none|Task reachability, broken down by build id and then task queue.<br> When requesting a large number of task queues or all task queues associated with the given build ids in a<br> namespace, all task queues will be listed in the response but some of them may not contain reachability<br> information due to a server enforced limit. When reaching the limit, task queues that reachability information<br> could not be retrieved for will be marked with a single TASK_REACHABILITY_UNSPECIFIED entry. The caller may issue<br> another call to get the reachability for those task queues.<br><br> Open source users can adjust this limit by setting the server's dynamic config value for<br> `limit.reachabilityTaskQueueScan` with the caveat that this call can strain the visibility store.|

<h2 id="tocS_InheritedAutoUpgradeInfo">InheritedAutoUpgradeInfo</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemainheritedautoupgradeinfo"></a>
<a id="schema_InheritedAutoUpgradeInfo"></a>
<a id="tocSinheritedautoupgradeinfo"></a>
<a id="tocsinheritedautoupgradeinfo"></a>

```json
{
  "sourceDeploymentVersion": {
    "buildId": "string",
    "deploymentName": "string"
  },
  "sourceDeploymentRevisionNumber": "string",
  "continueAsNewInitialVersioningBehavior": "CONTINUE_AS_NEW_VERSIONING_BEHAVIOR_UNSPECIFIED"
}
```

Used as part of WorkflowExecutionStartedEventAttributes to pass down the AutoUpgrade behavior and source deployment version
 to a workflow execution whose parent/previous workflow has an AutoUpgrade behavior.
 Also used for Upgrade-on-CaN behaviors AutoUpgrade and UseRampingVersion.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sourceDeploymentVersion|object|false|none|The source deployment version of the parent/previous workflow.|
|sourceDeploymentRevisionNumber|string|false|none|The revision number of the source deployment version of the parent/previous workflow.|
|continueAsNewInitialVersioningBehavior|string(enum)|false|none|Experimental.<br> If this workflow is the result of a continue-as-new, this field is set to the initial_versioning_behavior<br> specified in that command.<br> Only used for the initial task of this run and the initial task of any retries of this run.<br> Not passed to children or to future continue-as-new.<br><br> Note: In the first release of Upgrade-on-CaN, when the only ContinueAsNewVersioningBehavior was AutoUpgrade,<br> a non-empty InheritedAutoUpgradeInfo meant that the workflow should start as AutoUpgrade. So for compatibility<br> with history events generated during that time, know that an UNSPECIFIED value here is equivalent to AutoUpgrade<br> value if the InheritedAutoUpgradeInfo is non-empty.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|continueAsNewInitialVersioningBehavior|CONTINUE_AS_NEW_VERSIONING_BEHAVIOR_UNSPECIFIED|
|continueAsNewInitialVersioningBehavior|CONTINUE_AS_NEW_VERSIONING_BEHAVIOR_AUTO_UPGRADE|
|continueAsNewInitialVersioningBehavior|CONTINUE_AS_NEW_VERSIONING_BEHAVIOR_USE_RAMPING_VERSION|

<h2 id="tocS_IntervalSpec">IntervalSpec</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaintervalspec"></a>
<a id="schema_IntervalSpec"></a>
<a id="tocSintervalspec"></a>
<a id="tocsintervalspec"></a>

```json
{
  "interval": "string",
  "phase": "string"
}
```

IntervalSpec matches times that can be expressed as:
 epoch + n * interval + phase
 where n is an integer.
 phase defaults to zero if missing. interval is required.
 Both interval and phase must be non-negative and are truncated to the nearest
 second before any calculations.
 For example, an interval of 1 hour with phase of zero would match every hour,
 on the hour. The same interval but a phase of 19 minutes would match every
 xx:19:00. An interval of 28 days with phase zero would match
 2022-02-17T00:00:00Z (among other times). The same interval with a phase of 3
 days, 5 hours, and 23 minutes would match 2022-02-20T05:23:00Z instead.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|interval|string|false|none|none|
|phase|string|false|none|none|

Link can be associated with history events. It might contain information about an external entity
 related to the history event. For example, workflow A makes a Nexus call that starts workflow B:
 in this case, a history event in workflow A could contain a Link to the workflow started event in
 workflow B, and vice-versa.

|activity|[Link_Activity](#schemalink_activity)|false|none|A link to an activity.|
|nexusOperation|[Link_NexusOperation](#schemalink_nexusoperation)|false|none|A link to a standalone Nexus operation.|

|supportsSchedules|boolean|false|none|Whether scheduled workflows are supported on this namespace. This is only needed<br> temporarily while the feature is experimental, so we can give it a high tag.|

|Property|Value|

|state|NAMESPACE_STATE_DEPRECATED|
|state|NAMESPACE_STATE_DELETED|

Namespace capability details. Should contain what features are enabled in a namespace.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|eagerWorkflowStart|boolean|false|none|True if the namespace supports eager workflow start.|
|syncUpdate|boolean|false|none|True if the namespace supports sync update|
|asyncUpdate|boolean|false|none|True if the namespace supports async update|
|workerHeartbeats|boolean|false|none|True if the namespace supports worker heartbeats|
|reportedProblemsSearchAttribute|boolean|false|none|True if the namespace supports reported problems search attribute|
|workflowPause|boolean|false|none|True if the namespace supports pausing workflows|
|standaloneActivities|boolean|false|none|True if the namespace supports standalone activities|
|workerPollCompleteOnShutdown|boolean|false|none|True if the namespace supports server-side completion of outstanding worker polls on shutdown.<br> When enabled, the server will complete polls for workers that send WorkerInstanceKey in their<br> poll requests and call ShutdownWorker with the same WorkerInstanceKey. The poll will return<br> an empty response. When this flag is true, workers should allow polls to return gracefully<br> rather than terminating any open polls on shutdown.|
|pollerAutoscaling|boolean|false|none|True if the namespace supports poller autoscaling|
|workerCommands|boolean|false|none|True if the namespace supports worker commands (server-to-worker communication via control queues).|

NewWorkflowExecutionInfo is a shared message that encapsulates all the
 required arguments to starting a workflow in different contexts.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workflowId|string|false|none|none|
|workflowType|[WorkflowType](#schemaworkflowtype)|false|none|Represents the identifier used by a workflow author to define the workflow. Typically, the<br> name of a function. This is sometimes referred to as the workflow's "name"|
|taskQueue|[TaskQueue](#schemataskqueue)|false|none|See https://docs.temporal.io/docs/concepts/task-queues/|
|input|object|false|none|Serialized arguments to the workflow.|
|workflowExecutionTimeout|string|false|none|Total workflow execution timeout including retries and continue as new.|
|workflowRunTimeout|string|false|none|Timeout of a single workflow run.|
|workflowTaskTimeout|string|false|none|Timeout of a single workflow task.|
|workflowIdReusePolicy|string(enum)|false|none|Default: WORKFLOW_ID_REUSE_POLICY_ALLOW_DUPLICATE.|
|retryPolicy|object|false|none|The retry policy for the workflow. Will never exceed `workflow_execution_timeout`.|
|cronSchedule|string|false|none|See https://docs.temporal.io/docs/content/what-is-a-temporal-cron-job/|
|memo|[Memo](#schemamemo)|false|none|A user-defined set of *unindexed* fields that are exposed when listing/searching workflows|
|searchAttributes|[SearchAttributes](#schemasearchattributes)|false|none|A user-defined set of *indexed* fields that are used/exposed when listing/searching workflows.<br> The payload is not serialized in a user-defined way.|
|header|[Header](#schemaheader)|false|none|Contains metadata that can be attached to a variety of requests, like starting a workflow, and<br> can be propagated between, for example, workflows and activities.|
|userMetadata|object|false|none|Metadata on the workflow if it is started. This is carried over to the WorkflowExecutionConfig<br> for use by user interfaces to display the fixed as-of-start summary and details of the<br> workflow.|
|versioningOverride|object|false|none|If set, takes precedence over the Versioning Behavior sent by the SDK on Workflow Task completion.<br> To unset the override after the workflow is running, use UpdateWorkflowExecutionOptions.|
|priority|object|false|none|Priority metadata|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|workflowIdReusePolicy|WORKFLOW_ID_REUSE_POLICY_UNSPECIFIED|
|workflowIdReusePolicy|WORKFLOW_ID_REUSE_POLICY_ALLOW_DUPLICATE|
|workflowIdReusePolicy|WORKFLOW_ID_REUSE_POLICY_ALLOW_DUPLICATE_FAILED_ONLY|
|workflowIdReusePolicy|WORKFLOW_ID_REUSE_POLICY_REJECT_DUPLICATE|
|workflowIdReusePolicy|WORKFLOW_ID_REUSE_POLICY_TERMINATE_IF_RUNNING|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|requestedTime|string(date-time)|false|none|The time when cancellation was requested.|
|state|string(enum)|false|none|none|
|attempt|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of attempts made to deliver the cancel operation request.<br> This number represents a minimum bound since the attempt is incremented after the request completes.|
|lastAttemptCompleteTime|string(date-time)|false|none|The time when the last attempt completed.|
|lastAttemptFailure|object|false|none|The last attempt's failure, if any.|
|nextAttemptScheduleTime|string(date-time)|false|none|The time when the next attempt is scheduled.|
|blockedReason|string|false|none|If the state is BLOCKED, blocked reason provides additional information.|

Full current state of a standalone Nexus operation, as of the time of the request.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|operationId|string|false|none|Unique identifier of this Nexus operation within its namespace along with run ID (below).|
|runId|string|false|none|none|
|endpoint|string|false|none|Endpoint name, resolved to a URL via the cluster's endpoint registry.|
|service|string|false|none|Service name.|
|operation|string|false|none|Operation name.|
|status|string(enum)|false|none|A general status for this operation, indicates whether it is currently running or in one of the terminal statuses.<br> Updated once when the operation is originally scheduled, and again when it reaches a terminal status.|
|state|string(enum)|false|none|More detailed breakdown of NEXUS_OPERATION_EXECUTION_STATUS_RUNNING.|
|scheduleToCloseTimeout|string|false|none|Schedule-to-close timeout for this operation.<br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "to" is used to indicate interval. --)|
|scheduleToStartTimeout|string|false|none|Schedule-to-start timeout for this operation.<br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "to" is used to indicate interval. --)|
|startToCloseTimeout|string|false|none|Start-to-close timeout for this operation.<br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "to" is used to indicate interval. --)|
|attempt|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of attempts made to deliver the start operation request.<br> This number is approximate, it is incremented when a task is added to the history queue.<br> In practice, there could be more attempts if a task is executed but fails to commit, or less attempts if a task<br> was never executed.|
|scheduleTime|string(date-time)|false|none|Time the operation was originally scheduled via a StartNexusOperation request.|
|expirationTime|string(date-time)|false|none|Scheduled time + schedule to close timeout.|
|closeTime|string(date-time)|false|none|Time when the operation transitioned to a closed state.|
|lastAttemptCompleteTime|string(date-time)|false|none|The time when the last attempt completed.|
|lastAttemptFailure|object|false|none|The last attempt's failure, if any.|
|nextAttemptScheduleTime|string(date-time)|false|none|The time when the next attempt is scheduled.|
|executionDuration|string|false|none|Elapsed time from schedule_time to now for running operations or to close_time for closed<br> operations, including all attempts and backoff between attempts.|
|cancellationInfo|[NexusOperationExecutionCancellationInfo](#schemanexusoperationexecutioncancellationinfo)|false|none|NexusOperationExecutionCancellationInfo contains the state of a Nexus operation cancellation.|
|blockedReason|string|false|none|If the state is BLOCKED, blocked reason provides additional information.|
|requestId|string|false|none|Server-generated request ID used as an idempotency token when submitting start requests to<br> the handler. Distinct from the request_id in StartNexusOperationRequest, which is the<br> caller-side idempotency key for the StartNexusOperation RPC itself.|
|operationToken|string|false|none|Operation token. Only set for asynchronous operations after a successful StartOperation call.|
|stateTransitionCount|string|false|none|Incremented each time the operation's state is mutated in persistence.|
|searchAttributes|[SearchAttributes](#schemasearchattributes)|false|none|A user-defined set of *indexed* fields that are used/exposed when listing/searching workflows.<br> The payload is not serialized in a user-defined way.|
|nexusHeader|object|false|none|Header for context propagation and tracing purposes.|
|userMetadata|object|false|none|Metadata for use by user interfaces to display the fixed as-of-start summary and details of the operation.|
|links|[[Link](#schemalink)]|false|none|Links attached by the handler of this operation on start or completion.|
|identity|string|false|none|The identity of the client who started this operation.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|endpoint|string|false|none|Endpoint name, must exist in the endpoint registry.|
|service|string|false|none|Service name.|
|operation|string|false|none|Operation name.|
|input|object|false|none|Input for the operation. The server converts this into Nexus request content and the appropriate content headers<br> internally when sending the StartOperation request. On the handler side, if it is also backed by Temporal, the<br> content is transformed back to the original Payload stored in this event.|
|scheduleToCloseTimeout|string|false|none|Schedule-to-close timeout for this operation.<br> Indicates how long the caller is willing to wait for operation completion.<br> Calls are retried internally by the server.<br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "to" is used to indicate interval. --)<br> (-- api-linter: core::0142::time-field-names=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "timeout" is an acceptable suffix for duration fields in this API. --)|
|nexusHeader|object|false|none|Header to attach to the Nexus request. Note these headers are not the same as Temporal headers on internal<br> activities and child workflows, these are transmitted to Nexus operations that may be external and are not<br> traditional payloads.|
|workflowTaskCompletedEventId|string|false|none|The `WORKFLOW_TASK_COMPLETED` event that the corresponding ScheduleNexusOperation command was reported with.|
|requestId|string|false|none|A unique ID generated by the history service upon creation of this event.<br> The ID will be transmitted with all nexus StartOperation requests and is used as an idempotentency key.|
|endpointId|string|false|none|Endpoint ID as resolved in the endpoint registry at the time this event was generated.<br> This is stored on the event and used internally by the server in case the endpoint is renamed from the time the<br> event was originally scheduled.|
|scheduleToStartTimeout|string|false|none|Schedule-to-start timeout for this operation.<br> See ScheduleNexusOperationCommandAttributes.schedule_to_start_timeout for details.<br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "to" is used to indicate interval. --)|
|startToCloseTimeout|string|false|none|Start-to-close timeout for this operation.<br> See ScheduleNexusOperationCommandAttributes.start_to_close_timeout for details.<br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "to" is used to indicate interval. --)|

Event marking an asynchronous operation was started by the responding Nexus handler.
 If the operation completes synchronously, this event is not generated.
 In rare situations, such as request timeouts, the service may fail to record the actual start time and will fabricate
 this event upon receiving the operation completion via callback.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|scheduledEventId|string|false|none|The ID of the `NEXUS_OPERATION_SCHEDULED` event this task corresponds to.|
|operationId|string|false|none|The operation ID returned by the Nexus handler in the response to the StartOperation request.<br> This ID is used when canceling the operation.<br><br> Deprecated: Renamed to operation_token.|
|requestId|string|false|none|The request ID allocated at schedule time.|
|operationToken|string|false|none|The operation token returned by the Nexus handler in the response to the StartOperation request.<br> This token is used when canceling the operation.|

PendingNexusOperationInfo contains the state of a pending Nexus operation.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|endpoint|string|false|none|Endpoint name.<br> Resolved to a URL via the cluster's endpoint registry.|
|service|string|false|none|Service name.|
|operation|string|false|none|Operation name.|
|operationId|string|false|none|Operation ID. Only set for asynchronous operations after a successful StartOperation call.<br><br> Deprecated. Renamed to operation_token.|
|scheduleToCloseTimeout|string|false|none|Schedule-to-close timeout for this operation.<br> This is the only timeout settable by a workflow.<br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "to" is used to indicate interval. --)|
|scheduledTime|string(date-time)|false|none|The time when the operation was scheduled.|
|state|string(enum)|false|none|none|
|attempt|integer(int32)|false|none|The number of attempts made to deliver the start operation request.<br> This number is approximate, it is incremented when a task is added to the history queue.<br> In practice, there could be more attempts if a task is executed but fails to commit, or less attempts if a task<br> was never executed.|
|lastAttemptCompleteTime|string(date-time)|false|none|The time when the last attempt completed.|
|lastAttemptFailure|object|false|none|The last attempt's failure, if any.|
|nextAttemptScheduleTime|string(date-time)|false|none|The time when the next attempt is scheduled.|
|cancellationInfo|[NexusOperationCancellationInfo](#schemanexusoperationcancellationinfo)|false|none|NexusOperationCancellationInfo contains the state of a nexus operation cancellation.|
|scheduledEventId|string|false|none|The event ID of the NexusOperationScheduled event. Can be used to correlate an operation in the<br> DescribeWorkflowExecution response with workflow history.|
|blockedReason|string|false|none|If the state is BLOCKED, blocked reason provides additional information.|
|operationToken|string|false|none|Operation token. Only set for asynchronous operations after a successful StartOperation call.|
|scheduleToStartTimeout|string|false|none|Schedule-to-start timeout for this operation.<br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "to" is used to indicate interval. --)|
|startToCloseTimeout|string|false|none|Start-to-close timeout for this operation.<br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "to" is used to indicate interval. --)|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|state|PENDING_NEXUS_OPERATION_STATE_UNSPECIFIED|
|state|PENDING_NEXUS_OPERATION_STATE_SCHEDULED|
|state|PENDING_NEXUS_OPERATION_STATE_BACKING_OFF|
|state|PENDING_NEXUS_OPERATION_STATE_STARTED|
|state|PENDING_NEXUS_OPERATION_STATE_BLOCKED|

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
