|taskToken|string(bytes)|false|none|A unique identifier for this task|
|workflowExecution|[WorkflowExecution](#schemaworkflowexecution)|false|none|Identifies a specific workflow within a namespace. Practically speaking, because run_id is a<br> uuid, a workflow execution is globally unique. Note that many commands allow specifying an empty<br> run id as a way of saying "target the latest run of the workflow".|
|workflowType|[WorkflowType](#schemaworkflowtype)|false|none|Represents the identifier used by a workflow author to define the workflow. Typically, the<br> name of a function. This is sometimes referred to as the workflow's "name"|
|previousStartedEventId|string|false|none|The last workflow task started event which was processed by some worker for this execution.<br> Will be zero if no task has ever started.|
|startedEventId|string|false|none|The id of the most recent workflow task started event, which will have been generated as a<br> result of this poll request being served. Will be zero if the task<br> does not contain any events which would advance history (no new WFT started).<br> Currently this can happen for queries.|
|attempt|integer(int32)|false|none|Starting at 1, the number of attempts to complete this task by any worker.|
|backlogCountHint|string|false|none|A hint that there are more tasks already present in this task queue<br> partition. Can be used to prioritize draining a sticky queue.<br><br> Specifically, the returned number is the number of tasks remaining in<br> the in-memory buffer for this partition, which is currently capped at<br> 1000. Because sticky queues only have one partition, this number is<br> more useful when draining them. Normal queues, typically having more than one<br> partition, will return a number representing only some portion of the<br> overall backlog. Subsequent RPCs may not hit the same partition as<br> this call.|
|history|object|false|none|The history for this workflow, which will either be complete or partial. Partial histories<br> are sent to workers who have signaled that they are using a sticky queue when completing<br> a workflow task.|
|nextPageToken|string(bytes)|false|none|Will be set if there are more history events than were included in this response. Such events<br> should be fetched via `GetWorkflowExecutionHistory`.|
|query|object|false|none|Legacy queries appear in this field. The query must be responded to via<br> `RespondQueryTaskCompleted`. If the workflow is already closed (queries are permitted on<br> closed workflows) then the `history` field will be populated with the entire history. It<br> may also be populated if this task originates on a non-sticky queue.|
|workflowExecutionTaskQueue|object|false|none|The task queue this task originated from, which will always be the original non-sticky name<br> for the queue, even if this response came from polling a sticky queue.|
|scheduledTime|string(date-time)|false|none|When this task was scheduled by the server|
|startedTime|string(date-time)|false|none|When the current workflow task started event was generated, meaning the current attempt.|
|queries|object|false|none|Queries that should be executed after applying the history in this task. Responses should be<br> attached to `RespondWorkflowTaskCompletedRequest::query_results`|
|messages|[[Message](#schemamessage)]|false|none|Protocol messages piggybacking on a WFT as a transport|
|pollerScalingDecision|object|false|none|Server-advised information the SDK may use to adjust its poller count.|
|pollerGroupId|string|false|none|This poller group ID identifies the owner of the workflow task awaiting for query response.<br> Corresponding RespondQueryTaskCompleted should pass this value for proper routing.|
|pollerGroupInfos|[[PollerGroupInfo](#schemapollergroupinfo)]|false|none|The weighted list of poller groups IDs that client should use for future polls to this task<br> queue. Client is expected to:<br>   1. Maintain minimum number of pollers no less than the number of groups.<br>   2. Try to assign the next poll to a group without any pending polls,<br>   3. If every group has some pending polls, assign the next poll to a group randomly<br>     according to the weights.|

<h2 id="tocS_Priority">Priority</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemapriority"></a>
<a id="schema_Priority"></a>
<a id="tocSpriority"></a>
<a id="tocspriority"></a>

```json
{
  "priorityKey": 0,
  "fairnessKey": "string",
  "fairnessWeight": 0
}
```

Priority contains metadata that controls relative ordering of task processing
 when tasks are backed up in a queue. Initially, Priority will be used in
 matching (workflow and activity) task queues. Later it may be used in history
 task queues and in rate limiting decisions.

 Priority is attached to workflows and activities. By default, activities
 inherit Priority from the workflow that created them, but may override fields
 when an activity is started or modified.

 Despite being named "Priority", this message also contains fields that
 control "fairness" mechanisms.

 For all fields, the field not present or equal to zero/empty string means to
 inherit the value from the calling workflow, or if there is no calling
 workflow, then use the default value.

 For all fields other than fairness_key, the zero value isn't meaningful so
 there's no confusion between inherit/default and a meaningful value. For
 fairness_key, the empty string will be interpreted as "inherit". This means
 that if a workflow has a non-empty fairness key, you can't override the
 fairness key of its activity to the empty string.

 The overall semantics of Priority are:
 1. First, consider "priority": higher priority (lower number) goes first.
 2. Then, consider fairness: try to dispatch tasks for different fairness keys
    in proportion to their weight.

 Applications may use any subset of mechanisms that are useful to them and
 leave the other fields to use default values.

 Not all queues in the system may support the "full" semantics of all priority
 fields. (Currently only support in matching task queues is planned.)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|priorityKey|integer(int32)|false|none|Priority key is a positive integer from 1 to n, where smaller integers<br> correspond to higher priorities (tasks run sooner). In general, tasks in<br> a queue should be processed in close to priority order, although small<br> deviations are possible.<br><br> The maximum priority value (minimum priority) is determined by server<br> configuration, and defaults to 5.<br><br> If priority is not present (or zero), then the effective priority will be<br> the default priority, which is calculated by (min+max)/2. With the<br> default max of 5, and min of 1, that comes out to 3.|
|fairnessKey|string|false|none|Fairness key is a short string that's used as a key for a fairness<br> balancing mechanism. It may correspond to a tenant id, or to a fixed<br> string like "high" or "low". The default is the empty string.<br><br> The fairness mechanism attempts to dispatch tasks for a given key in<br> proportion to its weight. For example, using a thousand distinct tenant<br> ids, each with a weight of 1.0 (the default) will result in each tenant<br> getting a roughly equal share of task dispatch throughput.<br><br> (Note: this does not imply equal share of worker capacity! Fairness<br> decisions are made based on queue statistics, not<br> current worker load.)<br><br> As another example, using keys "high" and "low" with weight 9.0 and 1.0<br> respectively will prefer dispatching "high" tasks over "low" tasks at a<br> 9:1 ratio, while allowing either key to use all worker capacity if the<br> other is not present.<br><br> All fairness mechanisms, including rate limits, are best-effort and<br> probabilistic. The results may not match what a "perfect" algorithm with<br> infinite resources would produce. The more unique keys are used, the less<br> accurate the results will be.<br><br> Fairness keys are limited to 64 bytes.|
|fairnessWeight|number(float)|false|none|Fairness weight for a task can come from multiple sources for<br> flexibility. From highest to lowest precedence:<br> 1. Weights for a small set of keys can be overridden in task queue<br>    configuration with an API.<br> 2. It can be attached to the workflow/activity in this field.<br> 3. The default weight of 1.0 will be used.<br><br> Weight values are clamped to the range [0.001, 1000].|

<h2 id="tocS_Range">Range</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemarange"></a>
<a id="schema_Range"></a>
<a id="tocSrange"></a>
<a id="tocsrange"></a>

```json
{
  "start": 0,
  "end": 0,
  "step": 0
}
```

Range represents a set of integer values, used to match fields of a calendar
 time in StructuredCalendarSpec. If end < start, then end is interpreted as
 equal to start. This means you can use a Range with start set to a value, and
 end and step unset (defaulting to 0) to represent a single value.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|start|integer(int32)|false|none|Start of range (inclusive).|
|end|integer(int32)|false|none|End of range (inclusive).|
|step|integer(int32)|false|none|Step (optional, default 1).|

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "workflowId": "string",
  "activityId": "string",
  "runId": "string",
  "identity": "string",
  "resetHeartbeat": true,
  "keepPaused": true,
  "jitter": "string",
  "restoreOriginalOptions": true,
  "resourceId": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|string|false|none|Namespace of the workflow which scheduled this activity.|
|workflowId|string|false|none|If provided, targets a workflow activity for the given workflow ID.<br> If empty, targets a standalone activity.|
|activityId|string|false|none|The ID of the activity to target.|
|runId|string|false|none|Run ID of the workflow or standalone activity.|
|identity|string|false|none|The identity of the client who initiated this request.|
|resetHeartbeat|boolean|false|none|Indicates that activity should reset heartbeat details.<br> This flag will be applied only to the new instance of the activity.|
|keepPaused|boolean|false|none|If activity is paused, it will remain paused after reset|
|jitter|string|false|none|If set, and activity is in backoff, the activity will start at a random time within the specified jitter duration.<br> (unless it is paused and keep_paused is set)|
|restoreOriginalOptions|boolean|false|none|If set, the activity options will be restored to the defaults.<br> Default options are then options activity was created with.<br> They are part of the first schedule event.|
|resourceId|string|false|none|Resource ID for routing. Contains "workflow:{workflow_id}" for workflow activities or "activity:{activity_id}" for standalone activities.|

<h2 id="tocS_ResetOptions">ResetOptions</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaresetoptions"></a>
<a id="schema_ResetOptions"></a>
<a id="tocSresetoptions"></a>
<a id="tocsresetoptions"></a>

```json
{
  "workflowTaskId": "string",
  "buildId": "string",
  "resetReapplyType": "RESET_REAPPLY_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED",
  "currentRunOnly": true,
  "resetReapplyExcludeTypes": [
    "RESET_REAPPLY_EXCLUDE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED"
  ]
}
```

Describes where and how to reset a workflow, used for batch reset currently
 and may be used for single-workflow reset later.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workflowTaskId|string|false|none|The id of a specific `WORKFLOW_TASK_COMPLETED`,`WORKFLOW_TASK_TIMED_OUT`, `WORKFLOW_TASK_FAILED`, or<br> `WORKFLOW_TASK_STARTED` event to reset to.<br> Note that this option doesn't make sense when used as part of a batch request.|
|buildId|string|false|none|Resets to the first workflow task processed by this build id.<br> If the workflow was not processed by the build id, or the workflow task can't be<br> determined, no reset will be performed.<br> Note that by default, this reset is allowed to be to a prior run in a chain of<br> continue-as-new.|
|resetReapplyType|string(enum)|false|none|Deprecated. Use `options`.<br> Default: RESET_REAPPLY_TYPE_SIGNAL|
|currentRunOnly|boolean|false|none|If true, limit the reset to only within the current run. (Applies to build_id targets and<br> possibly others in the future.)|
|resetReapplyExcludeTypes|[string(enum)]|false|none|Event types not to be reapplied|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|resetReapplyType|RESET_REAPPLY_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED|
|resetReapplyType|RESET_REAPPLY_TYPE_SIGNAL|
|resetReapplyType|RESET_REAPPLY_TYPE_NONE|
|resetReapplyType|RESET_REAPPLY_TYPE_ALL_ELIGIBLE|
|resetReapplyExcludeTypes|RESET_REAPPLY_EXCLUDE_TYPE_UNSPECIFIED|
|resetReapplyExcludeTypes|RESET_REAPPLY_EXCLUDE_TYPE_SIGNAL|
|resetReapplyExcludeTypes|RESET_REAPPLY_EXCLUDE_TYPE_UPDATE|
|resetReapplyExcludeTypes|RESET_REAPPLY_EXCLUDE_TYPE_NEXUS|
|resetReapplyExcludeTypes|RESET_REAPPLY_EXCLUDE_TYPE_CANCEL_REQUEST|

<h2 id="tocS_ResetPointInfo">ResetPointInfo</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaresetpointinfo"></a>
<a id="schema_ResetPointInfo"></a>
<a id="tocSresetpointinfo"></a>
<a id="tocsresetpointinfo"></a>

```json
{
  "buildId": "string",
  "binaryChecksum": "string",
  "runId": "string",
  "firstWorkflowTaskCompletedId": "string",
  "createTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "expireTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "resettable": true
}
```

ResetPointInfo records the workflow event id that is the first one processed by a given
 build id or binary checksum. A new reset point will be created if either build id or binary
 checksum changes (although in general only one or the other will be used at a time).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|buildId|string|false|none|Worker build id.|
|binaryChecksum|string|false|none|Deprecated. A worker binary version identifier.|
|runId|string|false|none|The first run ID in the execution chain that was touched by this worker build.|
|firstWorkflowTaskCompletedId|string|false|none|Event ID of the first WorkflowTaskCompleted event processed by this worker build.|
|createTime|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|expireTime|string(date-time)|false|none|(-- api-linter: core::0214::resource-expiry=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: TTL is not defined for ResetPointInfo. --)<br> The time that the run is deleted due to retention.|
|resettable|boolean|false|none|false if the reset point has pending childWFs/reqCancels/signalExternals.|

<h2 id="tocS_RetryPolicy">RetryPolicy</h2>

```json
{
  "initialInterval": "string",
  "backoffCoefficient": 0,
  "maximumInterval": "string",
  "maximumAttempts": 0,
  "nonRetryableErrorTypes": [
    "string"
  ]
}
```

How retries ought to be handled, usable by both workflows and activities

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|initialInterval|string|false|none|Interval of the first retry. If retryBackoffCoefficient is 1.0 then it is used for all retries.|
|backoffCoefficient|number(double)|false|none|Coefficient used to calculate the next retry interval.<br> The next retry interval is previous interval multiplied by the coefficient.<br> Must be 1 or larger.|
|maximumInterval|string|false|none|Maximum interval between retries. Exponential backoff leads to interval increase.<br> This value is the cap of the increase. Default is 100x of the initial interval.|
|maximumAttempts|integer(int32)|false|none|Maximum number of attempts. When exceeded the retries stop even if not expired yet.<br> 1 disables retries. 0 means unlimited (up to the timeouts)|
|nonRetryableErrorTypes|[string]|false|none|Non-Retryable errors types. Will stop retrying if the error type matches this list. Note that<br> this is not a substring match, the error *type* (not message) must match exactly.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|currentDeploymentVersion|object|false|none|Specifies which Deployment Version should receive new workflow executions and tasks of<br> existing unversioned or AutoUpgrade workflows.<br> Nil value means no Version in this Deployment (except Ramping Version, if present) receives traffic other than tasks of previously Pinned workflows. In absence of a Current Version, remaining traffic after any ramp (if set)  goes to unversioned workers (those with `UNVERSIONED` (or unspecified) `WorkerVersioningMode`.).<br> Note: Current Version is overridden by the Ramping Version for a portion of traffic when ramp percentage<br> is non-zero (see `ramping_deployment_version` and `ramping_version_percentage`).|
|currentVersion|string|false|none|Deprecated. Use `current_deployment_version`.|
|rampingDeploymentVersion|object|false|none|When ramp percentage is non-zero, that portion of traffic is shifted from the Current Version to the Ramping Version.<br> Must always be different from `current_deployment_version` unless both are nil.<br> Nil value represents all the unversioned workers (those with `UNVERSIONED` (or unspecified) `WorkerVersioningMode`.)<br> Note that it is possible to ramp from one Version to another Version, or from unversioned<br> workers to a particular Version, or from a particular Version to unversioned workers.|
|rampingVersion|string|false|none|Deprecated. Use `ramping_deployment_version`.|
|rampingVersionPercentage|number(float)|false|none|Percentage of tasks that are routed to the Ramping Version instead of the Current Version.<br> Valid range: [0, 100]. A 100% value means the Ramping Version is receiving full traffic but<br> not yet "promoted" to be the Current Version, likely due to pending validations.<br> A 0% value means the Ramping Version is receiving no traffic.|
|currentVersionChangedTime|string(date-time)|false|none|Last time current version was changed.|
|rampingVersionChangedTime|string(date-time)|false|none|Last time ramping version was changed. Not updated if only the ramp percentage changes.|
|rampingVersionPercentageChangedTime|string(date-time)|false|none|Last time ramping version percentage was changed.<br> If ramping version is changed, this is also updated, even if the percentage stays the same.|
|revisionNumber|string|false|none|Monotonically increasing value which is incremented on every mutation<br> to any field of this message to achieve eventual consistency between task queues and their partitions.|

The meaning of a<br> ScheduleSpec depends only on its contents and never changes, except that the<br> definition of a time zone can change over time (most commonly, when daylight<br> saving time policy changes for an area). To create a totally self-contained<br> ScheduleSpec, use UTC or include timezone_data.<br><br> For input, you can provide zero or more of: structured_calendar, calendar,<br> cron_string, interval, and exclude_structured_calendar, and all of them will<br> be used (the schedule will take action at the union of all of their times,<br> minus the ones that match exclude_structured_calendar).<br><br> On input, calendar and cron_string fields will be compiled into<br> structured_calendar (and maybe interval and timezone_name), so if you<br> Describe a schedule, you'll see only structured_calendar, interval, etc.<br><br> If a spec has no matching times after the current time, then the schedule<br> will be subject to automatic deletion (after several days).|

|policies|[SchedulePolicies](#schemaschedulepolicies)|false|none|none|

```json
{
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|startWorkflow|object|false|none|All fields of NewWorkflowExecutionInfo are valid except for:<br> - workflow_id_reuse_policy<br> - cron_schedule<br> The workflow id of the started workflow may not match this exactly,<br> it may have a timestamp appended for uniqueness.|

<h2 id="tocS_ScheduleActionResult">ScheduleActionResult</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemascheduleactionresult"></a>
<a id="schema_ScheduleActionResult"></a>
<a id="tocSscheduleactionresult"></a>
<a id="tocsscheduleactionresult"></a>

```json
{
  "scheduleTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "actualTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "startWorkflowResult": {
    "workflowId": "string",
    "runId": "string"
  },
  "startWorkflowStatus": "WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|scheduleTime|string(date-time)|false|none|Time that the action was taken (according to the schedule, including jitter).|
|actualTime|string(date-time)|false|none|Time that the action was taken (real time).|
|startWorkflowResult|object|false|none|If action was start_workflow:|
|startWorkflowStatus|string(enum)|false|none|If the action was start_workflow, this field will reflect an<br> eventually-consistent view of the started workflow's status.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|startWorkflowStatus|WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED|
|startWorkflowStatus|WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_STATUS_RUNNING|
|startWorkflowStatus|WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_STATUS_COMPLETED|
|startWorkflowStatus|WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_STATUS_FAILED|
|startWorkflowStatus|WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_STATUS_CANCELED|
|startWorkflowStatus|WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_STATUS_TERMINATED|
|startWorkflowStatus|WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_STATUS_CONTINUED_AS_NEW|
|startWorkflowStatus|WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_STATUS_TIMED_OUT|
|startWorkflowStatus|WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_STATUS_PAUSED|

<h2 id="tocS_ScheduleInfo">ScheduleInfo</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemascheduleinfo"></a>
<a id="schema_ScheduleInfo"></a>
<a id="tocSscheduleinfo"></a>
<a id="tocsscheduleinfo"></a>

```json
{
  "actionCount": "string",
  "missedCatchupWindow": "string",
  "overlapSkipped": "string",
  "bufferDropped": "string",
  "bufferSize": "string",
  "runningWorkflows": [
    {
      "workflowId": "string",
      "runId": "string"
    }
  ],
  "recentActions": [
    {
      "scheduleTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "actualTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "startWorkflowResult": {
        "workflowId": "string",
        "runId": "string"
      },
      "startWorkflowStatus": "WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED"
    }
  ],
  "futureActionTimes": [
    "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  ],
  "createTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "updateTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
  "invalidScheduleError": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|actionCount|string|false|none|Number of actions taken so far.|
|missedCatchupWindow|string|false|none|Number of times a scheduled action was skipped due to missing the catchup window.|
|overlapSkipped|string|false|none|Number of skipped actions due to overlap.|
|bufferDropped|string|false|none|Number of dropped actions due to buffer limit.|
|bufferSize|string|false|none|Number of actions in the buffer. The buffer holds the actions that cannot<br> be immediately triggered (due to the overlap policy). These actions can be a result of<br> the normal schedule or a backfill.|
|runningWorkflows|[[WorkflowExecution](#schemaworkflowexecution)]|false|none|Currently-running workflows started by this schedule. (There might be<br> more than one if the overlap policy allows overlaps.)<br> Note that the run_ids in here are the original execution run ids as<br> started by the schedule. If the workflows retried, did continue-as-new,<br> or were reset, they might still be running but with a different run_id.|
|recentActions|[[ScheduleActionResult](#schemascheduleactionresult)]|false|none|Most recent ten actual action times (including manual triggers).|
|futureActionTimes|[string(date-time)]|false|none|Next ten scheduled action times.|
|createTime|string(date-time)|false|none|Timestamps of schedule creation and last update.|
|updateTime|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|invalidScheduleError|string|false|none|Deprecated.|

<a id="tocsschedulepatch"></a>

```json
{
  "triggerImmediately": {
    "overlapPolicy": "SCHEDULE_OVERLAP_POLICY_UNSPECIFIED",
    "scheduledTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z"
  },
  "backfillRequest": [
    {
      "startTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "endTime": "1970-01-01T00:00:00Z",
      "overlapPolicy": "SCHEDULE_OVERLAP_POLICY_UNSPECIFIED"
    }
  ],
  "pause": "string",
  "unpause": "string"
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|triggerImmediately|object|false|none|If set, trigger one action immediately.|
|backfillRequest|[[BackfillRequest](#schemabackfillrequest)]|false|none|If set, runs though the specified time period(s) and takes actions as if that time<br> passed by right now, all at once. The overlap policy can be overridden for the<br> scope of the backfill.|
|pause|string|false|none|If set, change the state to paused or unpaused (respectively) and set the<br> notes field to the value of the string.|
|unpause|string|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_SchedulePolicies">SchedulePolicies</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaschedulepolicies"></a>
<a id="schema_SchedulePolicies"></a>
<a id="tocSschedulepolicies"></a>
<a id="tocsschedulepolicies"></a>

```json
{
  "overlapPolicy": "SCHEDULE_OVERLAP_POLICY_UNSPECIFIED",
  "catchupWindow": "string",
  "pauseOnFailure": true,
  "keepOriginalWorkflowId": true
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|overlapPolicy|string(enum)|false|none|Policy for overlaps.<br> Note that this can be changed after a schedule has taken some actions,<br> and some changes might produce unintuitive results. In general, the later<br> policy overrides the earlier policy.|
|catchupWindow|string|false|none|Policy for catchups:<br> If the Temporal server misses an action due to one or more components<br> being down, and comes back up, the action will be run if the scheduled<br> time is within this window from the current time.<br> This value defaults to one year, and can't be less than 10 seconds.|
|pauseOnFailure|boolean|false|none|If true, and a workflow run fails or times out, turn on "paused".<br> This applies after retry policies: the full chain of retries must fail to<br> trigger a pause here.|
|keepOriginalWorkflowId|boolean|false|none|If true, and the action would start a workflow, a timestamp will not be<br> appended to the scheduled workflow id.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|overlapPolicy|SCHEDULE_OVERLAP_POLICY_UNSPECIFIED|
|overlapPolicy|SCHEDULE_OVERLAP_POLICY_SKIP|
|overlapPolicy|SCHEDULE_OVERLAP_POLICY_BUFFER_ONE|
|overlapPolicy|SCHEDULE_OVERLAP_POLICY_BUFFER_ALL|
|overlapPolicy|SCHEDULE_OVERLAP_POLICY_CANCEL_OTHER|
|overlapPolicy|SCHEDULE_OVERLAP_POLICY_TERMINATE_OTHER|
|overlapPolicy|SCHEDULE_OVERLAP_POLICY_ALLOW_ALL|

ScheduleSpec is a complete description of a set of absolute timestamps
 (possibly infinite) that an action should occur at. The meaning of a
 ScheduleSpec depends only on its contents and never changes, except that the
 definition of a time zone can change over time (most commonly, when daylight
 saving time policy changes for an area). To create a totally self-contained
 ScheduleSpec, use UTC or include timezone_data.

 For input, you can provide zero or more of: structured_calendar, calendar,
 cron_string, interval, and exclude_structured_calendar, and all of them will
 be used (the schedule will take action at the union of all of their times,
 minus the ones that match exclude_structured_calendar).

 On input, calendar and cron_string fields will be compiled into
 structured_calendar (and maybe interval and timezone_name), so if you
 Describe a schedule, you'll see only structured_calendar, interval, etc.

 If a spec has no matching times after the current time, then the schedule
 will be subject to automatic deletion (after several days).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|structuredCalendar|[[StructuredCalendarSpec](#schemastructuredcalendarspec)]|false|none|Calendar-based specifications of times.|
|cronString|[string]|false|none|cron_string holds a traditional cron specification as a string. It<br> accepts 5, 6, or 7 fields, separated by spaces, and interprets them the<br> same way as CalendarSpec.<br> 5 fields:         minute, hour, day_of_month, month, day_of_week<br> 6 fields:         minute, hour, day_of_month, month, day_of_week, year<br> 7 fields: second, minute, hour, day_of_month, month, day_of_week, year<br> If year is not given, it defaults to *. If second is not given, it<br> defaults to 0.<br> Shorthands @yearly, @monthly, @weekly, @daily, and @hourly are also<br> accepted instead of the 5-7 time fields.<br> Optionally, the string can be preceded by CRON_TZ=<timezone name> or<br> TZ=<timezone name>, which will get copied to timezone_name. (There must<br> not also be a timezone_name present.)<br> Optionally "#" followed by a comment can appear at the end of the string.<br> Note that the special case that some cron implementations have for<br> treating day_of_month and day_of_week as "or" instead of "and" when both<br> are set is not implemented.<br> @every <interval>[/<phase>] is accepted and gets compiled into an<br> IntervalSpec instead. <interval> and <phase> should be a decimal integer<br> with a unit suffix s, m, h, or d.|
|calendar|[[CalendarSpec](#schemacalendarspec)]|false|none|Calendar-based specifications of times.|
|interval|[[IntervalSpec](#schemaintervalspec)]|false|none|Interval-based specifications of times.|
|excludeCalendar|[[CalendarSpec](#schemacalendarspec)]|false|none|Any timestamps matching any of exclude_* will be skipped.<br> Deprecated. Use exclude_structured_calendar.|
|excludeStructuredCalendar|[[StructuredCalendarSpec](#schemastructuredcalendarspec)]|false|none|none|
|startTime|string(date-time)|false|none|If start_time is set, any timestamps before start_time will be skipped.<br> (Together, start_time and end_time make an inclusive interval.)|
|endTime|string(date-time)|false|none|If end_time is set, any timestamps after end_time will be skipped.|
|jitter|string|false|none|All timestamps will be incremented by a random value from 0 to this<br> amount of jitter. Default: 0|
|timezoneName|string|false|none|Time zone to interpret all calendar-based specs in.<br><br> If unset, defaults to UTC. We recommend using UTC for your application if<br> at all possible, to avoid various surprising properties of time zones.<br><br> Time zones may be provided by name, corresponding to names in the IANA<br> time zone database (see https://www.iana.org/time-zones). The definition<br> will be loaded by the Temporal server from the environment it runs in.<br><br> If your application requires more control over the time zone definition<br> used, it may pass in a complete definition in the form of a TZif file<br> from the time zone database. If present, this will be used instead of<br> loading anything from the environment. You are then responsible for<br> updating timezone_data when the definition changes.<br><br> Calendar spec matching is based on literal matching of the clock time<br> with no special handling of DST: if you write a calendar spec that fires<br> at 2:30am and specify a time zone that follows DST, that action will not<br> be triggered on the day that has no 2:30am. Similarly, an action that<br> fires at 1:30am will be triggered twice on the day that has two 1:30s.<br><br> Also note that no actions are taken on leap-seconds (e.g. 23:59:60 UTC).|
|timezoneData|string(bytes)|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_SetWorkerDeploymentCurrentVersionRequest">SetWorkerDeploymentCurrentVersionRequest</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasetworkerdeploymentcurrentversionrequest"></a>
<a id="schema_SetWorkerDeploymentCurrentVersionRequest"></a>
<a id="tocSsetworkerdeploymentcurrentversionrequest"></a>
<a id="tocssetworkerdeploymentcurrentversionrequest"></a>

```json
{
  "namespace": "string",
  "deploymentName": "string",
  "version": "string",
  "buildId": "string",
  "conflictToken": "string",
  "identity": "string",
  "ignoreMissingTaskQueues": true,
  "allowNoPollers": true
}
```

Set/unset the Current Version of a Worker Deployment.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|string|false|none|none|
|deploymentName|string|false|none|none|
|version|string|false|none|Deprecated. Use `build_id`.|
|buildId|string|false|none|The build id of the Version that you want to set as Current.<br> Pass an empty value to set the Current Version to nil.<br> A nil Current Version represents all the unversioned workers (those with `UNVERSIONED` (or unspecified) `WorkerVersioningMode`.)|
|conflictToken|string(bytes)|false|none|Optional. This can be the value of conflict_token from a Describe, or another Worker<br> Deployment API. Passing a non-nil conflict token will cause this request to fail if the<br> Deployment's configuration has been modified between the API call that generated the<br> token and this one.|
|identity|string|false|none|Optional. The identity of the client who initiated this request.|
|ignoreMissingTaskQueues|boolean|false|none|Optional. By default this request would be rejected if not all the expected Task Queues are<br> being polled by the new Version, to protect against accidental removal of Task Queues, or<br> worker health issues. Pass `true` here to bypass this protection.<br> The set of expected Task Queues is the set of all the Task Queues that were ever poller by<br> the existing Current Version of the Deployment, with the following exclusions:<br>   - Task Queues that are not used anymore (inferred by having empty backlog and a task<br>     add_rate of 0.)<br>   - Task Queues that are moved to another Worker Deployment (inferred by the Task Queue<br>     having a different Current Version than the Current Version of this deployment.)<br> WARNING: Do not set this flag unless you are sure that the missing task queue pollers are not<br> needed. If the request is unexpectedly rejected due to missing pollers, then that means the<br> pollers have not reached to the server yet. Only set this if you expect those pollers to<br> never arrive.|
|allowNoPollers|boolean|false|none|Optional. By default this request will be rejected if no pollers have been seen for the proposed<br> Current Version, in order to protect users from routing tasks to pollers that do not exist, leading<br> to possible timeouts. Pass `true` here to bypass this protection.|

|previousDeploymentVersion|object|false|none|The version that was current before executing this operation.<br> Deprecated in favor of idempotency of the API. Use `DescribeWorkerDeployment` to get the<br> Current version info before calling this API. By passing the `conflict_token` got from the<br> `DescribeWorkerDeployment` call to this API you can ensure there is no interfering changes<br> between the two calls.|

```json
  "ignoreMissingTaskQueues": true,
  "allowNoPollers": true
}
```

Set/unset the Ramping Version of a Worker Deployment and its ramp percentage.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|string|false|none|none|
|deploymentName|string|false|none|none|
|version|string|false|none|Deprecated. Use `build_id`.|
|buildId|string|false|none|The build id of the Version that you want to ramp traffic to.<br> Pass an empty value to set the Ramping Version to nil.<br> A nil Ramping Version represents all the unversioned workers (those with `UNVERSIONED` (or unspecified) `WorkerVersioningMode`.)|
|percentage|number(float)|false|none|Ramp percentage to set. Valid range: [0,100].|
|conflictToken|string(bytes)|false|none|Optional. This can be the value of conflict_token from a Describe, or another Worker<br> Deployment API. Passing a non-nil conflict token will cause this request to fail if the<br> Deployment's configuration has been modified between the API call that generated the<br> token and this one.|
|identity|string|false|none|Optional. The identity of the client who initiated this request.|
|ignoreMissingTaskQueues|boolean|false|none|Optional. By default this request would be rejected if not all the expected Task Queues are<br> being polled by the new Version, to protect against accidental removal of Task Queues, or<br> worker health issues. Pass `true` here to bypass this protection.<br> The set of expected Task Queues equals to all the Task Queues ever polled from the existing<br> Current Version of the Deployment, with the following exclusions:<br>   - Task Queues that are not used anymore (inferred by having empty backlog and a task<br>     add_rate of 0.)<br>   - Task Queues that are moved to another Worker Deployment (inferred by the Task Queue<br>     having a different Current Version than the Current Version of this deployment.)<br> WARNING: Do not set this flag unless you are sure that the missing task queue poller are not<br> needed. If the request is unexpectedly rejected due to missing pollers, then that means the<br> pollers have not reached to the server yet. Only set this if you expect those pollers to<br> never arrive.<br> Note: this check only happens when the ramping version is about to change, not every time<br> that the percentage changes. Also note that the check is against the deployment's Current<br> Version, not the previous Ramping Version.|
|allowNoPollers|boolean|false|none|Optional. By default this request will be rejected if no pollers have been seen for the proposed<br> Current Version, in order to protect users from routing tasks to pollers that do not exist, leading<br> to possible timeouts. Pass `true` here to bypass this protection.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|string|false|none|none|
|workflowId|string|false|none|none|

|input|object|false|none|Serialized arguments to the workflow. These are passed as arguments to the workflow function.|
|workflowExecutionTimeout|string|false|none|Total workflow execution timeout including retries and continue as new|
|workflowRunTimeout|string|false|none|Timeout of a single workflow run|
|workflowTaskTimeout|string|false|none|Timeout of a single workflow task|
|identity|string|false|none|The identity of the worker/client|
|requestId|string|false|none|Used to de-dupe signal w/ start requests|
|workflowIdReusePolicy|string(enum)|false|none|Defines whether to allow re-using the workflow id from a previously *closed* workflow.<br> The default policy is WORKFLOW_ID_REUSE_POLICY_ALLOW_DUPLICATE.<br><br> See `workflow_id_reuse_policy` for handling a workflow id duplication with a *running* workflow.|
|workflowIdConflictPolicy|string(enum)|false|none|Defines how to resolve a workflow id conflict with a *running* workflow.<br> The default policy is WORKFLOW_ID_CONFLICT_POLICY_USE_EXISTING.<br> Note that WORKFLOW_ID_CONFLICT_POLICY_FAIL is an invalid option.<br><br> See `workflow_id_reuse_policy` for handling a workflow id duplication with a *closed* workflow.|
|signalName|string|false|none|The workflow author-defined name of the signal to send to the workflow|
|signalInput|object|false|none|Serialized value(s) to provide with the signal|
|control|string|false|none|Deprecated.|
|retryPolicy|object|false|none|Retry policy for the workflow|
|cronSchedule|string|false|none|See https://docs.temporal.io/docs/content/what-is-a-temporal-cron-job/|
|memo|[Memo](#schemamemo)|false|none|A user-defined set of *unindexed* fields that are exposed when listing/searching workflows|
|searchAttributes|[SearchAttributes](#schemasearchattributes)|false|none|A user-defined set of *indexed* fields that are used/exposed when listing/searching workflows.<br> The payload is not serialized in a user-defined way.|
|header|[Header](#schemaheader)|false|none|Contains metadata that can be attached to a variety of requests, like starting a workflow, and<br> can be propagated between, for example, workflows and activities.|
|workflowStartDelay|string|false|none|Time to wait before dispatching the first workflow task. Cannot be used with `cron_schedule`.<br> Note that the signal will be delivered with the first workflow task. If the workflow gets<br> another SignalWithStartWorkflow before the delay a workflow task will be dispatched immediately<br> and the rest of the delay period will be ignored, even if that request also had a delay.<br> Signal via SignalWorkflowExecution will not unblock the workflow.|
|userMetadata|object|false|none|Metadata on the workflow if it is started. This is carried over to the WorkflowExecutionInfo<br> for use by user interfaces to display the fixed as-of-start summary and details of the<br> workflow.|

|timeSkippingConfig|object|false|none|Time-skipping configuration. If not set, time skipping is disabled.|

|scheduleToStartTimeout|string|false|none|Limits time an activity task can stay in a task queue before a worker picks it up. This<br> timeout is always non retryable, as all a retry would achieve is to put it back into the same<br> queue. Defaults to `schedule_to_close_timeout` if not specified.<br><br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "to" is used to indicate interval. --)|
|startToCloseTimeout|string|false|none|Maximum time an activity is allowed to execute after being picked up by a worker. This<br> timeout is always retryable. |heartbeatTimeout|string|false|none|Maximum permitted time between successful worker heartbeats.|
|retryPolicy|object|false|none|The retry policy for the activity. Will never exceed `schedule_to_close_timeout`.|

|idConflictPolicy|string(enum)|false|none|Defines how to resolve an activity id conflict with a *running* activity.<br> The default policy is ACTIVITY_ID_CONFLICT_POLICY_FAIL.|
|searchAttributes|object|false|none|Search attributes for indexing.|
|header|object|false|none|Header for context propagation and tracing purposes.|
|userMetadata|object|false|none|Metadata for use by user interfaces to display the fixed as-of-start summary and details of the activity.|
|priority|object|false|none|Priority metadata.|
|completionCallbacks|[[Callback](#schemacallback)]|false|none|Callbacks to be called by the server when this activity reaches a terminal state.<br> Callback addresses must be whitelisted in the server's dynamic configuration.|
|links|[[Link](#schemalink)]|false|none|Links to be associated with the activity. Callbacks may also have associated links;<br> links already included with a callback should not be duplicated here.|

|executions|[[WorkflowExecution](#schemaworkflowexecution)]|false|none|Executions to apply the batch operation<br> This field and `visibility_query` are mutually exclusive|
|maxOperationsPerSecond|number(float)|false|none|Limit for the number of operations processed per second within this batch.<br> Its purpose is to reduce the stress on the system caused by batch operations, which helps to prevent system<br> overload and minimize potential delays in executing ongoing tasks for user workers.<br> Note that when no explicit limit is provided, the server will operate according to its limit defined by the<br> dynamic configuration key `worker.batcherRPS`. This also applies if the value in this field exceeds the<br> server's configured limit.|

|service|string|false|none|Service name.|
|operation|string|false|none|Operation name.|
|scheduleToCloseTimeout|string|false|none|Schedule-to-close timeout for this operation.<br> Indicates how long the caller is willing to wait for operation completion.<br> Calls are retried internally by the server.<br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "to" is used to indicate interval. --)|
|scheduleToStartTimeout|string|false|none|Schedule-to-start timeout for this operation.<br> Indicates how long the caller is willing to wait for the operation to be started (or completed if synchronous)<br> by the handler.<br> If not set or zero, no schedule-to-start timeout is enforced.<br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "to" is used to indicate interval. --)|
|startToCloseTimeout|string|false|none|Start-to-close timeout for this operation.<br> Indicates how long the caller is willing to wait for an asynchronous operation to complete after it has been<br> started. Synchronous operations ignore this timeout.<br> If not set or zero, no start-to-close timeout is enforced.<br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: "to" is used to indicate interval. --)|
|input|object|false|none|Serialized input to the operation. Passed as the request payload.|
|idReusePolicy|string(enum)|false|none|Defines whether to allow re-using the operation id from a previously *closed* operation.<br> The default policy is NEXUS_OPERATION_ID_REUSE_POLICY_ALLOW_DUPLICATE.|
|idConflictPolicy|string(enum)|false|none|Defines how to resolve an operation id conflict with a *running* operation.<br> The default policy is NEXUS_OPERATION_ID_CONFLICT_POLICY_FAIL.|
|searchAttributes|object|false|none|Search attributes for indexing.|
|nexusHeader|object|false|none|Header to attach to the Nexus request.<br> Users are responsible for encrypting sensitive data in this header as it is stored in workflow history and<br> transmitted to external services as-is.<br> This is useful for propagating tracing information.<br> Note these headers are not the same as Temporal headers on internal activities and child workflows, these are<br> transmitted to Nexus operations that may be external and are not traditional payloads.|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|namespace|string|false|none|none|

|identity|string|false|none|The identity of the client who initiated this request|
|requestId|string|false|none|A unique identifier for this start request. Typically UUIDv4.|
|workflowIdReusePolicy|string(enum)|false|none|Defines whether to allow re-using the workflow id from a previously *closed* workflow.<br> The default policy is WORKFLOW_ID_REUSE_POLICY_ALLOW_DUPLICATE.<br><br> See `workflow_id_conflict_policy` for handling a workflow id duplication with a *running* workflow.|
|workflowIdConflictPolicy|string(enum)|false|none|Defines how to resolve a workflow id conflict with a *running* workflow.<br> The default policy is WORKFLOW_ID_CONFLICT_POLICY_FAIL.<br><br> See `workflow_id_reuse_policy` for handling a workflow id duplication with a *closed* workflow.|
|retryPolicy|object|false|none|The retry policy for the workflow. Will never exceed `workflow_execution_timeout`.|
|cronSchedule|string|false|none|See https://docs.temporal.io/docs/content/what-is-a-temporal-cron-job/|
|memo|[Memo](#schemamemo)|false|none|A user-defined set of *unindexed* fields that are exposed when listing/searching workflows|
|searchAttributes|[SearchAttributes](#schemasearchattributes)|false|none|A user-defined set of *indexed* fields that are used/exposed when listing/searching workflows.<br> The payload is not serialized in a user-defined way.|
|header|[Header](#schemaheader)|false|none|Contains metadata that can be attached to a variety of requests, like starting a workflow, and<br> can be propagated between, for example, workflows and activities.|
|requestEagerExecution|boolean|false|none|Request to get the first workflow task inline in the response bypassing matching service and worker polling.<br> If set to `true` the caller is expected to have a worker available and capable of processing the task.<br> The returned task will be marked as started and is expected to be completed by the specified<br> `workflow_task_timeout`.|
|continuedFailure|object|false|none|These values will be available as ContinuedFailure and LastCompletionResult in the<br> WorkflowExecutionStarted event and through SDKs. The are currently only used by the<br> server itself (for the schedules feature) and are not intended to be exposed in<br> StartWorkflowExecution.|
|lastCompletionResult|[Payloads](#schemapayloads)|false|none|See `Payload`|
|workflowStartDelay|string|false|none|Time to wait before dispatching the first workflow task. Cannot be used with `cron_schedule`.<br> If the workflow gets a signal before the delay, a workflow task will be dispatched and the rest<br> of the delay will be ignored.|
|completionCallbacks|[[Callback](#schemacallback)]|false|none|Callbacks to be called by the server when this workflow reaches a terminal state.<br> If the workflow continues-as-new, these callbacks will be carried over to the new execution.<br> Callback addresses must be whitelisted in the server's dynamic configuration.|
|userMetadata|object|false|none|Metadata on the workflow if it is started. This is carried over to the WorkflowExecutionInfo<br> for use by user interfaces to display the fixed as-of-start summary and details of the<br> workflow.|
|links|[[Link](#schemalink)]|false|none|Links to be associated with the workflow.|
|versioningOverride|object|false|none|If set, takes precedence over the Versioning Behavior sent by the SDK on Workflow Task completion.<br> To unset the override after the workflow is running, use UpdateWorkflowExecutionOptions.|
|onConflictOptions|object|false|none|Defines actions to be done to the existing running workflow when the conflict policy<br> WORKFLOW_ID_CONFLICT_POLICY_USE_EXISTING is used. If not set (ie., nil value) or set to a<br> empty object (ie., all options with default value), it won't do anything to the existing<br> running workflow. If set, it will add a history event to the running workflow.|
|priority|object|false|none|Priority metadata|
|eagerWorkerDeploymentOptions|object|false|none|Deployment Options of the worker who will process the eager task. Passed when `request_eager_execution=true`.|
|timeSkippingConfig|object|false|none|Time-skipping configuration. If not set, time skipping is disabled.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|workflowIdReusePolicy|WORKFLOW_ID_REUSE_POLICY_UNSPECIFIED|
|workflowIdReusePolicy|WORKFLOW_ID_REUSE_POLICY_ALLOW_DUPLICATE|
|workflowIdReusePolicy|WORKFLOW_ID_REUSE_POLICY_ALLOW_DUPLICATE_FAILED_ONLY|
|workflowIdReusePolicy|WORKFLOW_ID_REUSE_POLICY_REJECT_DUPLICATE|
|workflowIdReusePolicy|WORKFLOW_ID_REUSE_POLICY_TERMINATE_IF_RUNNING|
|workflowIdConflictPolicy|WORKFLOW_ID_CONFLICT_POLICY_UNSPECIFIED|
|workflowIdConflictPolicy|WORKFLOW_ID_CONFLICT_POLICY_FAIL|
|workflowIdConflictPolicy|WORKFLOW_ID_CONFLICT_POLICY_USE_EXISTING|
|workflowIdConflictPolicy|WORKFLOW_ID_CONFLICT_POLICY_TERMINATE_EXISTING|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|runId|string|false|none|The run id of the workflow that was started - or used (via WorkflowIdConflictPolicy USE_EXISTING).|
|started|boolean|false|none|If true, a new workflow was started.|
|status|string(enum)|false|none|Current execution status of the workflow. Typically remains WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_STATUS_RUNNING<br> unless a de-dupe occurs or in specific scenarios handled within the ExecuteMultiOperation (refer to its docs).|
|eagerWorkflowTask|object|false|none|When `request_eager_execution` is set on the `StartWorkflowExecutionRequest`, the server - if supported - will<br> return the first workflow task to be eagerly executed.<br> The caller is expected to have a worker available to process the task.|
|link|object|false|none|Link to the workflow event.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED|
|status|WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_STATUS_RUNNING|
|status|WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_STATUS_COMPLETED|
|status|WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_STATUS_FAILED|
|status|WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_STATUS_CANCELED|
|status|WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_STATUS_TERMINATED|
|status|WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_STATUS_CONTINUED_AS_NEW|
|status|WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_STATUS_TIMED_OUT|
|status|WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_STATUS_PAUSED|

<h2 id="tocS_Status">Status</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemastatus"></a>
<a id="schema_Status"></a>
<a id="tocSstatus"></a>
<a id="tocsstatus"></a>

```json
{
  "code": 0,
  "message": "string",
  "details": [
    {
      "@type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

The `Status` type defines a logical error model that is suitable for different programming environments, including REST APIs and RPC APIs. It is used by [gRPC](https://github.com/grpc). Each `Status` message contains three pieces of data: error code, error message, and error details. You can find out more about this error model and how to work with it in the [API Design Guide](https://cloud.google.com/apis/design/errors).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|code|integer(int32)|false|none|The status code, which should be an enum value of [google.rpc.Code][google.rpc.Code].|
|message|string|false|none|A developer-facing error message, which should be in English. Any user-facing error message should be localized and sent in the [google.rpc.Status.details][google.rpc.Status.details] field, or localized by the client.|
|details|[[GoogleProtobufAny](#schemagoogleprotobufany)]|false|none|A list of messages that carry the error details.  There is a common set of message types for APIs to use.|

<h2 id="tocS_StructuredCalendarSpec">StructuredCalendarSpec</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemastructuredcalendarspec"></a>
<a id="schema_StructuredCalendarSpec"></a>
<a id="tocSstructuredcalendarspec"></a>
<a id="tocsstructuredcalendarspec"></a>

```json
{
  "second": [
    {
      "start": 0,
      "end": 0,
      "step": 0
    }
  ],
  "minute": [
    {
      "start": 0,
      "end": 0,
      "step": 0
    }
  ],
  "hour": [
    {
      "start": 0,
      "end": 0,
      "step": 0
    }
  ],
  "dayOfMonth": [
    {
      "start": 0,
      "end": 0,
      "step": 0
    }
  ],
  "month": [
    {
      "start": 0,
      "end": 0,
      "step": 0
    }
  ],
  "year": [
    {
      "start": 0,
      "end": 0,
      "step": 0
    }
  ],
  "dayOfWeek": [
    {
      "start": 0,
      "end": 0,
      "step": 0
    }
  ],
  "comment": "string"
}
```

StructuredCalendarSpec describes an event specification relative to the
 calendar, in a form that's easy to work with programmatically. Each field can
 be one or more ranges.
 A timestamp matches if at least one range of each field matches the
 corresponding fields of the timestamp, except for year: if year is missing,
 that means all years match. For all fields besides year, at least one Range
 must be present to match anything.
 Relative expressions such as "last day of the month" or "third Monday" are not currently
 representable; callers must enumerate the concrete days they require.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|second|[[Range](#schemarange)]|false|none|Match seconds (0-59)|
|minute|[[Range](#schemarange)]|false|none|Match minutes (0-59)|
|hour|[[Range](#schemarange)]|false|none|Match hours (0-23)|
|dayOfMonth|[[Range](#schemarange)]|false|none|Match days of the month (1-31)<br> (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: standard name of field --)|
|month|[[Range](#schemarange)]|false|none|Match months (1-12)|
|year|[[Range](#schemarange)]|false|none|Match years.|
|dayOfWeek|[[Range](#schemarange)]|false|none|Match days of the week (0-6; 0 is Sunday).|
|comment|string|false|none|Free-form comment describing the intention of this spec.|

<h2 id="tocS_TaskQueueStats">TaskQueueStats</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemataskqueuestats"></a>
<a id="schema_TaskQueueStats"></a>
<a id="tocStaskqueuestats"></a>
<a id="tocstaskqueuestats"></a>

```json
{
  "approximateBacklogCount": "string",
  "approximateBacklogAge": "string",
  "tasksAddRate": 0,
  "tasksDispatchRate": 0
}
```

TaskQueueStats contains statistics about task queue backlog and activity.

 For workflow task queue type, this result is partial because tasks sent to sticky queues are not included. Read
 comments above each metric to understand the impact of sticky queue exclusion on that metric accuracy.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|approximateBacklogCount|string|false|none|The approximate number of tasks backlogged in this task queue. May count expired tasks but eventually<br> converges to the right value. Can be relied upon for scaling decisions.<br><br> Special note for workflow task queue type: this metric does not count sticky queue tasks. However, because<br> those tasks only remain valid for a few seconds, the inaccuracy becomes less significant as the backlog size<br> grows.|
|approximateBacklogAge|string|false|none|Approximate age of the oldest task in the backlog based on the creation time of the task at the head of<br> the queue. Can be relied upon for scaling decisions.<br><br> Special note for workflow task queue type: this metric does not count sticky queue tasks. However, because<br> those tasks only remain valid for a few seconds, they should not affect the result when backlog is older than<br> few seconds.|
|tasksAddRate|number(float)|false|none|The approximate tasks per second added to the task queue, averaging the last 30 seconds. These includes tasks<br> whether or not they were added to/dispatched from the backlog or they were dispatched immediately without going<br> to the backlog (sync-matched).<br><br> The difference between `tasks_add_rate` and `tasks_dispatch_rate` is a reliable metric for the rate at which<br> backlog grows/shrinks.<br><br> Note: the actual tasks delivered to the workers may significantly be higher than the numbers reported by<br> tasks_add_rate, because:<br> - Tasks can be sent to workers without going to the task queue. This is called Eager dispatch. Eager dispatch is<br>   enable for activities by default in the latest SDKs.<br> - Tasks going to Sticky queue are not accounted for. Note that, typically, only the first workflow task of each<br>   workflow goes to a normal queue, and the rest workflow tasks go to the Sticky queue associated with a specific<br>   worker instance.|
|tasksDispatchRate|number(float)|false|none|The approximate tasks per second dispatched from the task queue, averaging the last 30 seconds. These includes<br> tasks whether or not they were added to/dispatched from the backlog or they were dispatched immediately without<br> going to the backlog (sync-matched).<br><br> The difference between `tasks_add_rate` and `tasks_dispatch_rate` is a reliable metric for the rate at which<br> backlog grows/shrinks.<br><br> Note: the actual tasks delivered to the workers may significantly be higher than the numbers reported by<br> tasks_dispatch_rate, because:<br> - Tasks can be sent to workers without going to the task queue. This is called Eager dispatch. Eager dispatch is<br>   enable for activities by default in the latest SDKs.<br> - Tasks going to Sticky queue are not accounted for. Note that, typically, only the first workflow task of each<br>   workflow goes to a normal queue, and the rest workflow tasks go to the Sticky queue associated with a specific<br>   worker instance.|

<h2 id="tocS_TimeSkippingConfig">TimeSkippingConfig</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schematimeskippingconfig"></a>
<a id="schema_TimeSkippingConfig"></a>
<a id="tocStimeskippingconfig"></a>
<a id="tocstimeskippingconfig"></a>

```json
{
  "enabled": true,
  "maxSkippedDuration": "string",
  "maxElapsedDuration": "string"
}
```

Configuration for time skipping during a workflow execution.
 When enabled, virtual time advances automatically whenever there is no in-flight work.
 In-flight work includes activities, child workflows, Nexus operations, signal/cancel external workflow operations,
 and possibly other features added in the future.
 User timers are not classified as in-flight work and will be skipped over.
 When time advances, it skips to the earlier of the next user timer or the configured bound, if either exists.
 
 Propagation behavior of time skipping:
 The enabled flag, bound fields, and accumulated skipped duration are propagated to related executions as follows:
 (1) Child workflows and continue-as-new: both the configuration and the accumulated skipped duration are
     inherited from the current execution. The configured bound is shared between the inherited skipped
     duration and any additional duration skipped by the new run.
 (2) Retry and cron: the configuration and accumulated skipped duration are inherited as recorded when the
     current workflow started; the accumulated skipped duration of the current run is not propagated.
 (3) Reset: the new run retains the time-skipping configuration of the current execution. Because reset replays
     all events up to the reset point and re-applies any UpdateWorkflowExecutionOptions changes made after that
     point, the resulting run ends up with the same final time-skipping configuration as the previous run.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|enabled|boolean|false|none|Enables or disables time skipping for this workflow execution.|
|maxSkippedDuration|string|false|none|Maximum total virtual time that can be skipped.|
|maxElapsedDuration|string|false|none|Maximum elapsed time since time skipping was enabled.<br> This includes both skipped time and real time elapsing.|

|rule|[BuildIdAssignmentRule](#schemabuildidassignmentrule)|false|none|Assignment rules are applied to *new* Workflow and Activity executions at<br> schedule time to assign them to a Build ID.<br><br> Assignment rules will not be used in the following cases:<br>    - Child Workflows or Continue-As-New Executions who inherit their<br>      parent/previous Workflow's assigned Build ID (by setting the<br>      `inherit_build_id` flag - default behavior in SDKs when the same Task Queue<br>      is used.)<br>    - An Activity that inherits the assigned Build ID of its Workflow (by<br>      setting the `use_workflow_build_id` flag - default behavior in SDKs<br>      when the same Task Queue is used.)<br><br> In absence of (applicable) redirect rules (`CompatibleBuildIdRedirectRule`s)<br> the task will be dispatched to Workers of the Build ID determined by the<br> assignment rules (or inherited). Otherwise, the final Build ID will be<br> determined by the redirect rules.<br><br> Once a Workflow completes its first Workflow Task in a particular Build ID it<br> stays in that Build ID regardless of changes to assignment rules. Redirect<br> rules can be used to move the workflow to another compatible Build ID.<br><br> When using Worker Versioning on a Task Queue, in the steady state,<br> there should typically be a single assignment rule to send all new executions<br> to the latest Build ID. Existence of at least one such "unconditional"<br> rule at all times is enforces by the system, unless the `force` flag is used<br> by the user when replacing/deleting these rules (for exceptional cases).<br><br> During a deployment, one or more additional rules can be added to assign a<br> subset of the tasks to a new Build ID based on a "ramp percentage".<br><br> When there are multiple assignment rules for a Task Queue, the rules are<br> evaluated in order, starting from index 0. The first applicable rule will be<br> applied and the rest will be ignored.<br><br> In the event that no assignment rule is applicable on a task (or the Task<br> Queue is simply not versioned), the tasks will be dispatched to an<br> unversioned Worker.|
|createTime|string(date-time)|false|none|none|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|rule|[CompatibleBuildIdRedirectRule](#schemacompatiblebuildidredirectrule)|false|none|These rules apply to tasks assigned to a particular Build ID<br> (`source_build_id`) to redirect them to another *compatible* Build ID<br> (`target_build_id`).<br><br> It is user's responsibility to ensure that the target Build ID is compatible<br> with the source Build ID (e.g. by using the Patching API).<br><br> Most deployments are not expected to need these rules, however following<br> situations can greatly benefit from redirects:<br>  - Need to move long-running Workflow Executions from an old Build ID to a<br>    newer one.<br>  - Need to hotfix some broken or stuck Workflow Executions.<br><br> In steady state, redirect rules are beneficial when dealing with old<br> Executions ran on now-decommissioned Build IDs:<br>  - To redirecting the Workflow Queries to the current (compatible) Build ID.<br>  - To be able to Reset an old Execution so it can run on the current<br>    (compatible) Build ID.<br><br> Redirect rules can be chained.|
|createTime|string(date-time)|false|none|none|

<h2 id="tocS_VersioningOverride">VersioningOverride</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaversioningoverride"></a>

```json
  "pinned": {
    "behavior": "PINNED_OVERRIDE_BEHAVIOR_UNSPECIFIED",
    "version": {
      "buildId": "string",
      "deploymentName": "string"
    }
  },
  "autoUpgrade": true,
  "behavior": "VERSIONING_BEHAVIOR_UNSPECIFIED",
  "deployment": {
    "seriesName": "string",
    "buildId": "string"
  },
  "pinnedVersion": "string"
}
```

Used to override the versioning behavior (and pinned deployment version, if applicable) of a
 specific workflow execution. If set, this override takes precedence over worker-sent values.
 See `WorkflowExecutionInfo.VersioningInfo` for more information.

 To remove the override, call `UpdateWorkflowExecutionOptions` with a null
 `VersioningOverride`, and use the `update_mask` to indicate that it should be mutated.

 Pinned behavior overrides are automatically inherited by child workflows, workflow retries, continue-as-new
 workflows, and cron workflows.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|pinned|object|false|none|Override the workflow to have Pinned behavior.|
|autoUpgrade|boolean|false|none|Override the workflow to have AutoUpgrade behavior.|
|behavior|string(enum)|false|none|Required.<br> Deprecated. Use `override`.|
|deployment|object|false|none|Required if behavior is `PINNED`. Must be null if behavior is `AUTO_UPGRADE`.<br> Identifies the worker deployment to pin the workflow to.<br> Deprecated. Use `override.pinned.version`.|
|pinnedVersion|string|false|none|Required if behavior is `PINNED`. Must be absent if behavior is not `PINNED`.<br> Identifies the worker deployment version to pin the workflow to, in the format<br> "<deployment_name>.<build_id>".<br> Deprecated. Use `override.pinned.version`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|behavior|VERSIONING_BEHAVIOR_UNSPECIFIED|
|behavior|VERSIONING_BEHAVIOR_PINNED|
|behavior|VERSIONING_BEHAVIOR_AUTO_UPGRADE|


A Worker Deployment (Deployment, for short) represents all workers serving
 a shared set of Task Queues. Typically, a Deployment represents one service or
 application.
 A Deployment contains multiple Deployment Versions, each representing a different
 version of workers. (see documentation of WorkerDeploymentVersionInfo)
 Deployment records are created in Temporal server automatically when their
 first poller arrives to the server.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|name|string|false|none|Identifies a Worker Deployment. Must be unique within the namespace.|
|versionSummaries|[[WorkerDeploymentInfo_WorkerDeploymentVersionSummary](#schemaworkerdeploymentinfo_workerdeploymentversionsummary)]|false|none|Deployment Versions that are currently tracked in this Deployment. A DeploymentVersion will be<br> cleaned up automatically if all the following conditions meet:<br> - It does not receive new executions (is not current or ramping)<br> - It has no active pollers (see WorkerDeploymentVersionInfo.pollers_status)<br> - It is drained (see WorkerDeploymentVersionInfo.drainage_status)|
|createTime|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|routingConfig|[RoutingConfig](#schemaroutingconfig)|false|none|none|
|lastModifierIdentity|string|false|none|Identity of the last client who modified the configuration of this Deployment. Set to the<br> `identity` value sent by APIs such as `SetWorkerDeploymentCurrentVersion` and<br> `SetWorkerDeploymentRampingVersion`.|
|managerIdentity|string|false|none|Identity of the client that has the exclusive right to make changes to this Worker Deployment.<br> Empty by default.<br> If this is set, clients whose identity does not match `manager_identity` will not be able to make changes<br> to this Worker Deployment. They can either set their own identity as the manager or unset the field to proceed.|
|routingConfigUpdateState|string(enum)|false|none|Indicates whether the routing_config has been fully propagated to all<br> relevant task queues and their partitions.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|routingConfigUpdateState|ROUTING_CONFIG_UPDATE_STATE_UNSPECIFIED|
|routingConfigUpdateState|ROUTING_CONFIG_UPDATE_STATE_IN_PROGRESS|
|routingConfigUpdateState|ROUTING_CONFIG_UPDATE_STATE_COMPLETED|

Worker Deployment options set in SDK that need to be sent to server in every poll.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|deploymentName|string|false|none|Required when `worker_versioning_mode==VERSIONED`.|
|buildId|string|false|none|The Build ID of the worker. Required when `worker_versioning_mode==VERSIONED`, in which case,<br> the worker will be part of a Deployment Version.|
|workerVersioningMode|string(enum)|false|none|Required. Versioning Mode for this worker. Must be the same for all workers with the<br> same `deployment_name` and `build_id` combination, across all Task Queues.<br> When `worker_versioning_mode==VERSIONED`, the worker will be part of a Deployment Version.|

|---|---|

|workerVersioningMode|WORKER_VERSIONING_MODE_UNVERSIONED|
|workerVersioningMode|WORKER_VERSIONING_MODE_VERSIONED|

<h2 id="tocS_WorkerDeploymentVersion">WorkerDeploymentVersion</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaworkerdeploymentversion"></a>
<a id="schema_WorkerDeploymentVersion"></a>
<a id="tocSworkerdeploymentversion"></a>
<a id="tocsworkerdeploymentversion"></a>

```json
{
  "buildId": "string",
  "deploymentName": "string"
}
```

A Worker Deployment Version (Version, for short) represents a
 version of workers within a Worker Deployment. (see documentation of WorkerDeploymentVersionInfo)
 Version records are created in Temporal server automatically when their
 first poller arrives to the server.
 Experimental. Worker Deployment Versions are experimental and might significantly change in the future.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|buildId|string|false|none|A unique identifier for this Version within the Deployment it is a part of.<br> Not necessarily unique within the namespace.<br> The combination of `deployment_name` and `build_id` uniquely identifies this<br> Version within the namespace, because Deployment names are unique within a namespace.|
|deploymentName|string|false|none|Identifies the Worker Deployment this Version is part of.|

A Worker Deployment Version (Version, for short) represents all workers of the same
 code and config within a Deployment. Workers of the same Version are expected to
 behave exactly the same so when executions move between them there are no
 non-determinism issues.
 Worker Deployment Versions are created in Temporal server automatically when
 their first poller arrives to the server.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|version|string|false|none|Deprecated. Use `deployment_version`.|
|status|string(enum)|false|none|The status of the Worker Deployment Version.|
|deploymentVersion|object|false|none|Required.|
|deploymentName|string|false|none|Deprecated. User deployment_version.deployment_name.|
|createTime|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|routingChangedTime|string(date-time)|false|none|Last time `current_since_time`, `ramping_since_time, or `ramp_percentage` of this version changed.|
|currentSinceTime|string(date-time)|false|none|(-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: 'Since' captures the field semantics despite being a preposition. --)<br> Unset if not current.|
|rampingSinceTime|string(date-time)|false|none|(-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: 'Since' captures the field semantics despite being a preposition. --)<br> Unset if not ramping. Updated when the version first starts ramping, not on each ramp change.|
|firstActivationTime|string(date-time)|false|none|Timestamp when this version first became current or ramping.|
|lastCurrentTime|string(date-time)|false|none|Timestamp when this version last became current.<br> Can be used to determine whether a version has ever been Current.|
|lastDeactivationTime|string(date-time)|false|none|Timestamp when this version last stopped being current or ramping.<br> Cleared if the version becomes current or ramping again.|
|rampPercentage|number(float)|false|none|Range: [0, 100]. Must be zero if the version is not ramping (i.e. `ramping_since_time` is nil).<br> Can be in the range [0, 100] if the version is ramping.|
|taskQueueInfos|[[WorkerDeploymentVersionInfo_VersionTaskQueueInfo](#schemaworkerdeploymentversioninfo_versiontaskqueueinfo)]|false|none|All the Task Queues that have ever polled from this Deployment version.<br> Deprecated. Use `version_task_queues` in DescribeWorkerDeploymentVersionResponse instead.|
|drainageInfo|object|false|none|Helps user determine when it is safe to decommission the workers of this<br> Version. Not present when version is current or ramping.<br> Current limitations:<br> - Not supported for Unversioned mode.<br> - Periodically refreshed, may have delays up to few minutes (consult the<br>   last_checked_time value).<br> - Refreshed only when version is not current or ramping AND the status is not<br>   "drained" yet.<br> - Once the status is changed to "drained", it is not changed until the Version<br>   becomes Current or Ramping again, at which time the drainage info is cleared.<br>   This means if the Version is "drained" but new workflows are sent to it via<br>   Pinned Versioning Override, the status does not account for those Pinned-override<br>   executions and remains "drained".|
|metadata|object|false|none|Arbitrary user-provided metadata attached to this version.|
|computeConfig|object|false|none|Optional. Contains the new worker compute configuration for the Worker<br> Deployment. Used for worker scale management.|
|lastModifierIdentity|string|false|none|Identity of the last client who modified the configuration of this Version.<br> As of now, this field only covers changes through the following APIs:<br> - `CreateWorkerDeploymentVersion`<br> - `UpdateWorkerDeploymentVersionComputeConfig`<br> - `UpdateWorkerDeploymentVersionMetadata`|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|WORKER_DEPLOYMENT_VERSION_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED|
|status|WORKER_DEPLOYMENT_VERSION_STATUS_INACTIVE|
|status|WORKER_DEPLOYMENT_VERSION_STATUS_CURRENT|
|status|WORKER_DEPLOYMENT_VERSION_STATUS_RAMPING|
|status|WORKER_DEPLOYMENT_VERSION_STATUS_DRAINING|
|status|WORKER_DEPLOYMENT_VERSION_STATUS_DRAINED|
|status|WORKER_DEPLOYMENT_VERSION_STATUS_CREATED|

Worker info message, contains information about the worker and its current state.
 All information is provided by the worker itself.
 (-- api-linter: core::0140::prepositions=disabled
     aip.dev/not-precedent: Removing those words make names less clear. --)

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workerInstanceKey|string|false|none|Worker identifier, should be unique for the namespace.<br> It is distinct from worker identity, which is not necessarily namespace-unique.|
|workerIdentity|string|false|none|Worker identity, set by the client, may not be unique.<br> Usually host_name+(user group name)+process_id, but can be overwritten by the user.|
|hostInfo|object|false|none|Worker host information.|
|taskQueue|string|false|none|Task queue this worker is polling for tasks.|
|deploymentVersion|[WorkerDeploymentVersion](#schemaworkerdeploymentversion)|false|none|A Worker Deployment Version (Version, for short) represents a<br> version of workers within a Worker Deployment. (see documentation of WorkerDeploymentVersionInfo)<br> Version records are created in Temporal server automatically when their<br> first poller arrives to the server.<br> Experimental. Worker Deployment Versions are experimental and might significantly change in the future.|
|sdkName|string|false|none|none|
|sdkVersion|string|false|none|none|
|status|string(enum)|false|none|Worker status. Defined by SDK.|
|startTime|string(date-time)|false|none|Worker start time.<br> It can be used to determine worker uptime. (current time - start time)|
|heartbeatTime|string(date-time)|false|none|Timestamp of this heartbeat, coming from the worker. Worker should set it to "now".<br> Note that this timestamp comes directly from the worker and is subject to workers' clock skew.|
|elapsedSinceLastHeartbeat|string|false|none|Elapsed time since the last heartbeat from the worker.|
|workflowTaskSlotsInfo|[WorkerSlotsInfo](#schemaworkerslotsinfo)|false|none|none|
|activityTaskSlotsInfo|[WorkerSlotsInfo](#schemaworkerslotsinfo)|false|none|none|
|nexusTaskSlotsInfo|[WorkerSlotsInfo](#schemaworkerslotsinfo)|false|none|none|
|localActivitySlotsInfo|[WorkerSlotsInfo](#schemaworkerslotsinfo)|false|none|none|
|workflowPollerInfo|[WorkerPollerInfo](#schemaworkerpollerinfo)|false|none|none|
|workflowStickyPollerInfo|[WorkerPollerInfo](#schemaworkerpollerinfo)|false|none|none|
|activityPollerInfo|[WorkerPollerInfo](#schemaworkerpollerinfo)|false|none|none|
|nexusPollerInfo|[WorkerPollerInfo](#schemaworkerpollerinfo)|false|none|none|
|totalStickyCacheHit|integer(int32)|false|none|A Workflow Task found a cached Workflow Execution to run against.|
|totalStickyCacheMiss|integer(int32)|false|none|A Workflow Task did not find a cached Workflow execution to run against.|
|currentStickyCacheSize|integer(int32)|false|none|Current cache size, expressed in number of Workflow Executions.|
|plugins|[[PluginInfo](#schemaplugininfo)]|false|none|Plugins currently in use by this SDK.|
|drivers|[[StorageDriverInfo](#schemastoragedriverinfo)]|false|none|Storage drivers in use by this SDK.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|WORKER_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED|
|status|WORKER_STATUS_RUNNING|
|status|WORKER_STATUS_SHUTTING_DOWN|
|status|WORKER_STATUS_SHUTDOWN|

```json
}
```

Holds everything needed to identify the worker host/process context

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|hostName|string|false|none|Worker host identifier.|
|workerGroupingKey|string|false|none|Worker grouping identifier. A key to group workers that share the same client+namespace+process.<br> This will be used to build the worker command nexus task queue name:<br> "temporal-sys/worker-commands/{worker_grouping_key}"|
|processId|string|false|none|Worker process identifier. This id only needs to be unique<br> within one host (so using e.g. a unix pid would be appropriate).|
|currentHostCpuUsage|number(float)|false|none|System used CPU as a float in the range [0.0, 1.0] where 1.0 is defined as all<br> cores on the host pegged.|
|currentHostMemUsage|number(float)|false|none|System used memory as a float in the range [0.0, 1.0] where 1.0 is defined as<br> all available memory on the host is used.|
