```json
      "name": "string",
      "version": "string"
    }
  ],
  "drivers": [
    {
      "type": "string"
    }
  ]
}
```

Limited worker information returned in the list response.
 When adding fields here, ensure that it is also added to WorkerInfo (as it carries the full worker information).

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workerInstanceKey|string|false|none|Worker identifier, should be unique for the namespace.<br> It is distinct from worker identity, which is not necessarily namespace-unique.|
|workerIdentity|string|false|none|Worker identity, set by the client, may not be unique.<br> Usually host_name+(user group name)+process_id, but can be overwritten by the user.|
|taskQueue|string|false|none|Task queue this worker is polling for tasks.|
|deploymentVersion|[WorkerDeploymentVersion](#schemaworkerdeploymentversion)|false|none|A Worker Deployment Version (Version, for short) represents a<br> version of workers within a Worker Deployment. (see documentation of WorkerDeploymentVersionInfo)<br> Version records are created in Temporal server automatically when their<br> first poller arrives to the server.<br> Experimental. Worker Deployment Versions are experimental and might significantly change in the future.|
|sdkName|string|false|none|none|
|sdkVersion|string|false|none|none|
|status|string(enum)|false|none|Worker status. Defined by SDK.|
|startTime|string(date-time)|false|none|Worker start time.<br> It can be used to determine worker uptime. (current time - start time)|
|hostName|string|false|none|Worker host identifier.|
|workerGroupingKey|string|false|none|Worker grouping identifier. A key to group workers that share the same client+namespace+process.<br> This will be used to build the worker command nexus task queue name:<br> "temporal-sys/worker-commands/{worker_grouping_key}"|
|processId|string|false|none|Worker process identifier. This id only needs to be unique<br> within one host (so using e.g. a unix pid would be appropriate).|
|plugins|[[PluginInfo](#schemaplugininfo)]|false|none|Plugins currently in use by this SDK.|
|drivers|[[StorageDriverInfo](#schemastoragedriverinfo)]|false|none|Storage drivers in use by this SDK.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|status|WORKER_STATUS_UNSPECIFIED|
|status|WORKER_STATUS_RUNNING|
|status|WORKER_STATUS_SHUTTING_DOWN|
|status|WORKER_STATUS_SHUTDOWN|

<h2 id="tocS_WorkerSlotsInfo">WorkerSlotsInfo</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaworkerslotsinfo"></a>
<a id="schema_WorkerSlotsInfo"></a>
<a id="tocSworkerslotsinfo"></a>
<a id="tocsworkerslotsinfo"></a>

```json
{
  "currentAvailableSlots": 0,
  "currentUsedSlots": 0,
  "slotSupplierKind": "string",
  "totalProcessedTasks": 0,
  "totalFailedTasks": 0,
  "lastIntervalProcessedTasks": 0,
  "lastIntervalFailureTasks": 0
}
```

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|currentAvailableSlots|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of slots available for the worker to specific tasks.<br> May be -1 if the upper bound is not known.|
|currentUsedSlots|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of slots used by the worker for specific tasks.|
|slotSupplierKind|string|false|none|Kind of the slot supplier, which is used to determine how the slots are allocated.<br> Possible values: "Fixed \| ResourceBased \| Custom String"|
|totalProcessedTasks|integer(int32)|false|none|Total number of tasks processed (completed both successfully and unsuccesfully, or any other way)<br> by the worker since the worker started. This is a cumulative counter.|
|totalFailedTasks|integer(int32)|false|none|Total number of failed tasks processed by the worker so far.|
|lastIntervalProcessedTasks|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of tasks processed in since the last heartbeat from the worker.<br> This is a cumulative counter, and it is reset to 0 each time the worker sends a heartbeat.<br> Contains both successful and failed tasks.|
|lastIntervalFailureTasks|integer(int32)|false|none|Number of failed tasks processed since the last heartbeat from the worker.|

<h2 id="tocS_WorkerVersionCapabilities">WorkerVersionCapabilities</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemaworkerversioncapabilities"></a>
<a id="schema_WorkerVersionCapabilities"></a>
<a id="tocSworkerversioncapabilities"></a>
<a id="tocsworkerversioncapabilities"></a>

```json
{
  "buildId": "string",
  "useVersioning": true,
  "deploymentSeriesName": "string"
}
```

Identifies the version that a worker is compatible with when polling or identifying itself,
 and whether or not this worker is opting into the build-id based versioning feature. This is
 used by matching to determine which workers ought to receive what tasks.
 Deprecated. Use WorkerDeploymentOptions instead.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|buildId|string|false|none|An opaque whole-worker identifier|
|useVersioning|boolean|false|none|If set, the worker is opting in to worker versioning, and wishes to only receive appropriate<br> tasks.|
|deploymentSeriesName|string|false|none|Must be sent if user has set a deployment series name (versioning-3).|

<h2 id="tocS_WorkerVersionStamp">WorkerVersionStamp</h2>

<a id="tocSworkerversionstamp"></a>
<a id="tocsworkerversionstamp"></a>

```json
{
  "buildId": "string",
  "useVersioning": true
}
```

Deprecated. This message is replaced with `Deployment` and `VersioningBehavior`.
 Identifies the version(s) of a worker that processed a task

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|buildId|string|false|none|An opaque whole-worker identifier. Replaces the deprecated `binary_checksum` field when this<br> message is included in requests which previously used that.|
|useVersioning|boolean|false|none|If set, the worker is opting in to worker versioning. Otherwise, this is used only as a<br> marker for workflow reset points and the BuildIDs search attribute.|

Now (when supported by server<br> and sdk) the final event will be `WORKFLOW_EXECUTION_FAILED` with `new_execution_run_id` set.|

|originalStartTime|string(date-time)|false|none|Original workflow start time.|
|resetRunId|string|false|none|Reset Run ID points to the new run when this execution is reset. If the execution is reset multiple times, it points to the latest run.|
|requestIdInfos|object|false|none|Request ID information (eg: history event information associated with the request ID).<br> Note: It only contains request IDs from StartWorkflowExecution requests, including indirect<br> calls (eg: if SignalWithStartWorkflowExecution starts a new workflow, then the request ID is<br> used in the StartWorkflowExecution request).|
|pauseInfo|object|false|none|Information about the workflow execution pause operation.|

Hold basic information about a workflow execution.
 This structure is a part of visibility, and thus contain a limited subset of information.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|execution|[WorkflowExecution](#schemaworkflowexecution)|false|none|Identifies a specific workflow within a namespace. Practically speaking, because run_id is a<br> uuid, a workflow execution is globally unique. Note that many commands allow specifying an empty<br> run id as a way of saying "target the latest run of the workflow".|
|type|[WorkflowType](#schemaworkflowtype)|false|none|Represents the identifier used by a workflow author to define the workflow. Typically, the<br> name of a function. This is sometimes referred to as the workflow's "name"|
|startTime|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|closeTime|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|status|string(enum)|false|none|none|
|historyLength|string|false|none|none|
|parentNamespaceId|string|false|none|none|
|parentExecution|[WorkflowExecution](#schemaworkflowexecution)|false|none|Identifies a specific workflow within a namespace. Practically speaking, because run_id is a<br> uuid, a workflow execution is globally unique. Note that many commands allow specifying an empty<br> run id as a way of saying "target the latest run of the workflow".|
|executionTime|string(date-time)|false|none|none|
|memo|[Memo](#schemamemo)|false|none|A user-defined set of *unindexed* fields that are exposed when listing/searching workflows|
|searchAttributes|[SearchAttributes](#schemasearchattributes)|false|none|A user-defined set of *indexed* fields that are used/exposed when listing/searching workflows.<br> The payload is not serialized in a user-defined way.|
|autoResetPoints|[ResetPoints](#schemaresetpoints)|false|none|none|
|taskQueue|string|false|none|none|
|stateTransitionCount|string|false|none|none|
|historySizeBytes|string|false|none|none|
|mostRecentWorkerVersionStamp|object|false|none|If set, the most recent worker version stamp that appeared in a workflow task completion<br> Deprecated. This field should be cleaned up when versioning-2 API is removed. [cleanup-experimental-wv]|
|executionDuration|string|false|none|Workflow execution duration is defined as difference between close time and execution time.<br> This field is only populated if the workflow is closed.|
|rootExecution|object|false|none|Contains information about the root workflow execution.<br> The root workflow execution is defined as follows:<br> 1. A workflow without parent workflow is its own root workflow.<br> 2. A workflow that has a parent workflow has the same root workflow as its parent workflow.<br> Note: workflows continued as new or reseted may or may not have parents, check examples below.<br><br> Examples:<br>   Scenario 1: Workflow W1 starts child workflow W2, and W2 starts child workflow W3.<br>     - The root workflow of all three workflows is W1.<br>   Scenario 2: Workflow W1 starts child workflow W2, and W2 continued as new W3.<br>     - The root workflow of all three workflows is W1.<br>   Scenario 3: Workflow W1 continued as new W2.<br>     - The root workflow of W1 is W1 and the root workflow of W2 is W2.<br>   Scenario 4: Workflow W1 starts child workflow W2, and W2 is reseted, creating W3<br>     - The root workflow of all three workflows is W1.<br>   Scenario 5: Workflow W1 is reseted, creating W2.<br>     - The root workflow of W1 is W1 and the root workflow of W2 is W2.|
|assignedBuildId|string|false|none|The currently assigned build ID for this execution. Presence of this value means worker versioning is used<br> for this execution. Assigned build ID is selected based on Worker Versioning Assignment Rules<br> when the first workflow task of the execution is scheduled. If the first workflow task fails and is scheduled<br> again, the assigned build ID may change according to the latest versioning rules.<br> Assigned build ID can also change in the middle of a execution if Compatible Redirect Rules are applied to<br> this execution.<br> Deprecated. This field should be cleaned up when versioning-2 API is removed. [cleanup-experimental-wv]|
|inheritedBuildId|string|false|none|Build ID inherited from a previous/parent execution. If present, assigned_build_id will be set to this, instead<br> of using the assignment rules.<br> Deprecated. This field should be cleaned up when versioning-2 API is removed. [cleanup-experimental-wv]|
|firstRunId|string|false|none|The first run ID in the execution chain.<br> Executions created via the following operations are considered to be in the same chain<br> - ContinueAsNew<br> - Workflow Retry<br> - Workflow Reset<br> - Cron Schedule|
|versioningInfo|object|false|none|Absent value means the workflow execution is not versioned. When present, the execution might<br> be versioned or unversioned, depending on `versioning_info.behavior` and `versioning_info.versioning_override`.<br> Experimental. Versioning info is experimental and might change in the future.|
|workerDeploymentName|string|false|none|The name of Worker Deployment that completed the most recent workflow task.|
|priority|object|false|none|Priority metadata|
|externalPayloadSizeBytes|string|false|none|Total size in bytes of all external payloads referenced in workflow history.|
|externalPayloadCount|string|false|none|Count of external payloads referenced in workflow history.|

Always the first event in workflow history

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|workflowType|[WorkflowType](#schemaworkflowtype)|false|none|Represents the identifier used by a workflow author to define the workflow. Typically, the<br> name of a function. This is sometimes referred to as the workflow's "name"|
|parentWorkflowNamespace|string|false|none|If this workflow is a child, the namespace our parent lives in.<br> SDKs and UI tools should use `parent_workflow_namespace` field but server must use `parent_workflow_namespace_id` only.|
|parentWorkflowNamespaceId|string|false|none|none|
|parentWorkflowExecution|object|false|none|Contains information about parent workflow execution that initiated the child workflow these attributes belong to.<br> If the workflow these attributes belong to is not a child workflow of any other execution, this field will not be populated.|
|parentInitiatedEventId|string|false|none|EventID of the child execution initiated event in parent workflow|
|taskQueue|[TaskQueue](#schemataskqueue)|false|none|See https://docs.temporal.io/docs/concepts/task-queues/|
|input|object|false|none|SDK will deserialize this and provide it as arguments to the workflow function|
|workflowExecutionTimeout|string|false|none|Total workflow execution timeout including retries and continue as new.|
|workflowRunTimeout|string|false|none|Timeout of a single workflow run.|
|workflowTaskTimeout|string|false|none|Timeout of a single workflow task.|
|continuedExecutionRunId|string|false|none|Run id of the previous workflow which continued-as-new or retried or cron executed into this<br> workflow.|
|initiator|string(enum)|false|none|none|
|continuedFailure|[Failure](#schemafailure)|false|none|none|
|lastCompletionResult|[Payloads](#schemapayloads)|false|none|See `Payload`|
|originalExecutionRunId|string|false|none|This is the run id when the WorkflowExecutionStarted event was written.<br> A workflow reset changes the execution run_id, but preserves this field.|
|identity|string|false|none|Identity of the client who requested this execution|
|firstExecutionRunId|string|false|none|This is the very first runId along the chain of ContinueAsNew, Retry, Cron and Reset.<br> Used to identify a chain.|
|retryPolicy|[RetryPolicy](#schemaretrypolicy)|false|none|How retries ought to be handled, usable by both workflows and activities|
|attempt|integer(int32)|false|none|Starting at 1, the number of times we have tried to execute this workflow|
|workflowExecutionExpirationTime|string(date-time)|false|none|The absolute time at which the workflow will be timed out.<br> This is passed without change to the next run/retry of a workflow.|
|cronSchedule|string|false|none|If this workflow runs on a cron schedule, it will appear here|
|firstWorkflowTaskBackoff|string|false|none|For a cron workflow, this contains the amount of time between when this iteration of<br> the cron workflow was scheduled and when it should run next per its cron_schedule.|
|memo|[Memo](#schemamemo)|false|none|A user-defined set of *unindexed* fields that are exposed when listing/searching workflows|
|searchAttributes|[SearchAttributes](#schemasearchattributes)|false|none|A user-defined set of *indexed* fields that are used/exposed when listing/searching workflows.<br> The payload is not serialized in a user-defined way.|
|prevAutoResetPoints|[ResetPoints](#schemaresetpoints)|false|none|none|
|header|[Header](#schemaheader)|false|none|Contains metadata that can be attached to a variety of requests, like starting a workflow, and<br> can be propagated between, for example, workflows and activities.|
|parentInitiatedEventVersion|string|false|none|Version of the child execution initiated event in parent workflow<br> It should be used together with parent_initiated_event_id to identify<br> a child initiated event for global namespace|
|workflowId|string|false|none|This field is new in 1.21.|
|sourceVersionStamp|object|false|none|If this workflow intends to use anything other than the current overall default version for<br> the queue, then we include it here.<br> Deprecated. [cleanup-experimental-wv]|
|completionCallbacks|[[Callback](#schemacallback)]|false|none|Completion callbacks attached when this workflow was started.|
|rootWorkflowExecution|object|false|none|Contains information about the root workflow execution.<br> The root workflow execution is defined as follows:<br>   1. A workflow without parent workflow is its own root workflow.<br>   2. A workflow that has a parent workflow has the same root workflow as its parent workflow.<br> When the workflow is its own root workflow, then root_workflow_execution is nil.<br> Note: workflows continued as new or reseted may or may not have parents, check examples below.<br><br> Examples:<br>   Scenario 1: Workflow W1 starts child workflow W2, and W2 starts child workflow W3.<br>     - The root workflow of all three workflows is W1.<br>     - W1 has root_workflow_execution set to nil.<br>     - W2 and W3 have root_workflow_execution set to W1.<br>   Scenario 2: Workflow W1 starts child workflow W2, and W2 continued as new W3.<br>     - The root workflow of all three workflows is W1.<br>     - W1 has root_workflow_execution set to nil.<br>     - W2 and W3 have root_workflow_execution set to W1.<br>   Scenario 3: Workflow W1 continued as new W2.<br>     - The root workflow of W1 is W1 and the root workflow of W2 is W2.<br>     - W1 and W2 have root_workflow_execution set to nil.<br>   Scenario 4: Workflow W1 starts child workflow W2, and W2 is reseted, creating W3<br>     - The root workflow of all three workflows is W1.<br>     - W1 has root_workflow_execution set to nil.<br>     - W2 and W3 have root_workflow_execution set to W1.<br>   Scenario 5: Workflow W1 is reseted, creating W2.<br>     - The root workflow of W1 is W1 and the root workflow of W2 is W2.<br>     - W1 and W2 have root_workflow_execution set to nil.|
|inheritedBuildId|string|false|none|When present, this execution is assigned to the build ID of its parent or previous execution.<br> Deprecated. This field should be cleaned up when versioning-2 API is removed. [cleanup-experimental-wv]|
|versioningOverride|object|false|none|Versioning override applied to this workflow when it was started.<br> Children, crons, retries, and continue-as-new will inherit source run's override if pinned<br> and if the new workflow's Task Queue belongs to the override version.|
|parentPinnedWorkerDeploymentVersion|string|false|none|When present, it means this is a child workflow of a parent that is Pinned to this Worker<br> Deployment Version. In this case, child workflow will start as Pinned to this Version instead<br> of starting on the Current Version of its Task Queue.<br> This is set only if the child workflow is starting on a Task Queue belonging to the same<br> Worker Deployment Version.<br> Deprecated. Use `parent_versioning_info`.|
|priority|object|false|none|Priority metadata|
|inheritedPinnedVersion|object|false|none|If present, the new workflow should start on this version with pinned base behavior.<br> Child of pinned parent will inherit the parent's version if the Child's Task Queue belongs to that version.<br><br> A new run initiated by workflow ContinueAsNew of pinned run, will inherit the previous run's version if the<br> new run's Task Queue belongs to that version.<br><br> A new run initiated by workflow Cron will never inherit.<br><br> A new run initiated by workflow Retry will only inherit if the retried run is effectively pinned at the time<br> of retry, and the retried run inherited a pinned version when it started (ie. it is a child of a pinned<br> parent, or a CaN of a pinned run, and is running on a Task Queue in the inherited version).<br><br> Pinned override is inherited if Task Queue of new run is compatible with the override version.<br> Override is inherited separately and takes precedence over inherited base version.<br><br> Note: This field is mutually exclusive with inherited_auto_upgrade_info.<br> Additionaly, versioning_override, if present, overrides this field during routing decisions.|
|inheritedAutoUpgradeInfo|object|false|none|If present, the new workflow begins with AutoUpgrade behavior. Before dispatching the<br> first workflow task, this field is set to the deployment version on which the parent/<br> previous run was operating. This inheritance only happens when the task queues belong to<br> the same deployment version. The first workflow task will then be dispatched to either<br> this inherited deployment version, or the current deployment version of the task queue's<br> Deployment. After the first workflow task, the effective behavior depends on worker-sent<br> values in subsequent workflow tasks.<br><br> Inheritance rules:<br>   - ContinueAsNew and child workflows: inherit AutoUpgrade behavior and deployment version<br>   - Cron: never inherits<br>   - Retry: inherits only if the retried run is effectively AutoUpgrade at the time of<br>     retry, and inherited AutoUpgrade behavior when it started (i.e. it is a child of an<br>     AutoUpgrade parent or ContinueAsNew of an AutoUpgrade run, running on the same<br>     deployment as the parent/previous run)<br><br> Additional notes:<br> - This field is mutually exclusive with `inherited_pinned_version`.<br> - `versioning_override`, if present, overrides this field during routing decisions.<br> - SDK implementations do not interact with this field and is only used internally by<br>   the server to ensure task routing correctness.|
|eagerExecutionAccepted|boolean|false|none|A boolean indicating whether the SDK has asked to eagerly execute the first workflow task for this workflow and<br> eager execution was accepted by the server.<br> Only populated by server with version >= 1.29.0.|
|declinedTargetVersionUpgrade|object|false|none|During a previous run of this workflow, the server may have notified the SDK<br> that the Target Worker Deployment Version changed, but the SDK declined to<br> upgrade (e.g., by continuing-as-new with PINNED behavior). This field records<br> the target version that was declined.<br><br> This is a wrapper message to distinguish "never declined" (nil wrapper) from<br> "declined an unversioned target" (non-nil wrapper with nil deployment_version).<br><br> Used internally by the server during continue-as-new and retry.<br> Should not be read or interpreted by SDKs.|
|timeSkippingConfig|object|false|none|Initial time-skipping configuration for this workflow execution, recorded at start time.<br> This may have been set explicitly via the start workflow request, or propagated from a<br> parent/previous execution.<br><br> The configuration may be updated after start via UpdateWorkflowExecutionOptions, which<br> will be reflected in the WorkflowExecutionOptionsUpdatedEvent.|
|initialSkippedDuration|string|false|none|The time skipped by the previous execution that started this workflow.<br> It can happen in cases of child workflows and continue-as-new workflows.|

|initiator|CONTINUE_AS_NEW_INITIATOR_RETRY|
|initiator|CONTINUE_AS_NEW_INITIATOR_CRON_SCHEDULE|


Holds all the information about worker versioning for a particular workflow execution.
 Experimental. Versioning info is experimental and might change in the future.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|behavior|string(enum)|false|none|Versioning behavior determines how the server should treat this execution when workers are<br> upgraded. When present it means this workflow execution is versioned; UNSPECIFIED means<br> unversioned. See the comments in `VersioningBehavior` enum for more info about different<br> behaviors.<br><br> Child workflows or CaN executions **inherit** their parent/previous run's effective Versioning <br> Behavior and Version (except when the new execution runs on a task queue not belonging to the <br> same deployment version as the parent/previous run's task queue). The first workflow task will<br> be dispatched according to the inherited behavior (or to the current version of the task-queue's <br> deployment in the case of AutoUpgrade.) After completion of their first workflow task the <br> Deployment Version and Behavior of the execution will update according to configuration on the worker.<br> <br> Note that `behavior` is overridden by `versioning_override` if the latter is present.|
|deployment|object|false|none|The worker deployment that completed the last workflow task of this workflow execution. Must<br> be present if `behavior` is set. Absent value means no workflow task is completed, or the<br> last workflow task was completed by an unversioned worker. Unversioned workers may still send<br> a deployment value which will be stored here, so the right way to check if an execution is<br> versioned if an execution is versioned or not is via the `behavior` field.<br> Note that `deployment` is overridden by `versioning_override` if the latter is present.<br> Deprecated. Use `deployment_version`.|
|version|string|false|none|Deprecated. Use `deployment_version`.|
|deploymentVersion|object|false|none|The Worker Deployment Version that completed the last workflow task of this workflow execution.<br> An absent value means no workflow task is completed, or the workflow is unversioned.<br> If present, and `behavior` is UNSPECIFIED, the last task of this workflow execution was completed<br> by a worker that is not using versioning but _is_ passing Deployment Name and Build ID.<br><br> Child workflows or CaN executions **inherit** their parent/previous run's effective Versioning <br> Behavior and Version (except when the new execution runs on a task queue not belonging to the <br> same deployment version as the parent/previous run's task queue). The first workflow task will<br> be dispatched according to the inherited behavior (or to the current version of the task-queue's <br> deployment in the case of AutoUpgrade.) After completion of their first workflow task the <br> Deployment Version and Behavior of the execution will update according to configuration on the worker.<br><br> Note that if `versioning_override.behavior` is PINNED then `versioning_override.pinned_version`<br> will override this value.|
|versioningOverride|object|false|none|Present if user has set an execution-specific versioning override. This override takes<br> precedence over SDK-sent `behavior` (and `version` when override is PINNED). An<br> override can be set when starting a new execution, as well as afterwards by calling the<br> `UpdateWorkflowExecutionOptions` API.<br> Pinned overrides are automatically inherited by child workflows, continue-as-new workflows,<br> workflow retries, and cron workflows.|
|deploymentTransition|object|false|none|When present, indicates the workflow is transitioning to a different deployment. Can<br> indicate one of the following transitions: unversioned -> versioned, versioned -> versioned<br> on a different deployment, or versioned -> unversioned.<br> Not applicable to workflows with PINNED behavior.<br> When a workflow with AUTO_UPGRADE behavior creates a new workflow task, it will automatically<br> start a transition to the task queue's current deployment if the task queue's current<br> deployment is different from the workflow's deployment.<br> If the AUTO_UPGRADE workflow is stuck due to backlogged activity or workflow tasks, those<br> tasks will be redirected to the task queue's current deployment. As soon as a poller from<br> that deployment is available to receive the task, the workflow will automatically start a<br> transition to that deployment and continue execution there.<br> A deployment transition can only exist while there is a pending or started workflow task.<br> Once the pending workflow task completes on the transition's target deployment, the<br> transition completes and the workflow's `deployment` and `behavior` fields are updated per<br> the worker's task completion response.<br> Pending activities will not start new attempts during a transition. Once the transition is<br> completed, pending activities will start their next attempt on the new deployment.<br> Deprecated. Use version_transition.|
|versionTransition|object|false|none|When present, indicates the workflow is transitioning to a different deployment version<br> (which may belong to the same deployment name or another). Can indicate one of the following<br> transitions: unversioned -> versioned, versioned -> versioned<br> on a different deployment version, or versioned -> unversioned.<br> Not applicable to workflows with PINNED behavior.<br> When a workflow with AUTO_UPGRADE behavior creates a new workflow task, it will automatically<br> start a transition to the task queue's current version if the task queue's current version is<br> different from the workflow's current deployment version.<br> If the AUTO_UPGRADE workflow is stuck due to backlogged activity or workflow tasks, those<br> tasks will be redirected to the task queue's current version. As soon as a poller from<br> that deployment version is available to receive the task, the workflow will automatically<br> start a transition to that version and continue execution there.<br> A version transition can only exist while there is a pending or started workflow task.<br> Once the pending workflow task completes on the transition's target version, the<br> transition completes and the workflow's `behavior`, and `deployment_version` fields are updated per the<br> worker's task completion response.<br> Pending activities will not start new attempts during a transition. Once the transition is<br> completed, pending activities will start their next attempt on the new version.|
|revisionNumber|string|false|none|Monotonic counter reflecting the latest routing decision for this workflow execution.<br> Used for staleness detection between history and matching when dispatching tasks to workers.<br> Incremented when a workflow execution routes to a new deployment version, which happens<br> when a worker of the new deployment version completes a workflow task.<br> Note: Pinned tasks and sticky tasks send a value of 0 for this field since these tasks do not<br> face the problem of inconsistent dispatching that arises from eventual consistency between<br> task queues and their partitions.|
|continueAsNewInitialVersioningBehavior|string(enum)|false|none|Experimental.<br> If this workflow is the result of a continue-as-new, this field is set to the initial_versioning_behavior<br> specified in that command.<br> Only used for the initial task of this run and the initial task of any retries of this run.<br> Not passed to children or to future continue-as-new.<br><br> Note: In the first release of Upgrade-on-CaN, when the only ContinueAsNewVersioningBehavior was AutoUpgrade,<br> a non-empty InheritedAutoUpgradeInfo meant that the workflow should start as AutoUpgrade. So for compatibility<br> with ContinueAsNew history commands generated during that time, know that an UNSPECIFIED value here is equivalent<br> to ContinueAsNewVersioningBehaviorAutoUpgrade if the behavior of the workflow is AutoUpgrade.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|behavior|VERSIONING_BEHAVIOR_UNSPECIFIED|
|behavior|VERSIONING_BEHAVIOR_PINNED|
|behavior|VERSIONING_BEHAVIOR_AUTO_UPGRADE|
|continueAsNewInitialVersioningBehavior|CONTINUE_AS_NEW_VERSIONING_BEHAVIOR_UNSPECIFIED|
|continueAsNewInitialVersioningBehavior|CONTINUE_AS_NEW_VERSIONING_BEHAVIOR_AUTO_UPGRADE|
|continueAsNewInitialVersioningBehavior|CONTINUE_AS_NEW_VERSIONING_BEHAVIOR_USE_RAMPING_VERSION|

### Properties

|predicate|string|false|none|Activity predicate is a SQL-like string filter parameter.<br> It is used to match against workflow data.<br> The following activity attributes are supported as part of the predicate:<br> - ActivityType: An Activity Type is the mapping of a name to an Activity Definition..<br> - ActivityId: The ID of the activity.<br> - ActivityAttempt: The number attempts of the activity.<br> - BackoffInterval: The current amount of time between scheduled attempts of the activity.<br> - ActivityStatus: The status of the activity. Can be one of "Scheduled", "Started", "Paused".<br> - TaskQueue: The name of the task queue the workflow specified that the activity should run on.<br> Activity predicate support the following operators:<br>  * =, !=, >, >=, <, <=<br>  * AND, OR, ()<br>  * BETWEEN ... AND<br>    STARTS_WITH|

SDKs using flags must comply with the following behavior:<br><br> During replay:<br> * If a flag is not recognized (value is too high or not defined), it must fail the workflow<br>   task.<br> * If a flag is recognized, it is stored in a set of used flags for the run. Code checks for<br>   that flag during and after this WFT are allowed to assume that the flag is present.<br> * If a code check for a flag does not find the flag in the set of used flags, it must take<br>   the branch corresponding to the absence of that flag.<br><br> During non-replay execution of new WFTs:<br> * The SDK is free to use all flags it knows about. It must record any newly-used (IE: not<br>   previously recorded) flags when completing the WFT.<br><br> SDKs which are too old to even know about this field at all are considered to produce<br> undefined behavior if they replay workflows which used this mechanism.<br><br> (-- api-linter: core::0141::forbidden-types=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: These really shouldn't have negative values. --)|
|langUsedFlags|[integer(uint32)]|false|none|Flags used by the SDK lang. No attempt is made to distinguish between different SDK languages<br> here as processing a workflow with a different language than the one which authored it is<br> already undefined behavior. See `core_used_patches` for more.<br><br> (-- api-linter: core::0141::forbidden-types=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: These really shouldn't have negative values. --)|
|sdkName|string|false|none|Name of the SDK that processed the task. This is usually something like "temporal-go" and is<br> usually the same as client-name gRPC header. This should only be set if its value changed<br> since the last time recorded on the workflow (or be set on the first task).<br><br> (-- api-linter: core::0122::name-suffix=disabled<br>     aip.dev/not-precedent: We're ok with a name suffix here. --)|
|sdkVersion|string|false|none|Version of the SDK that processed the task. This is usually something like "1.20.0" and is<br> usually the same as client-version gRPC header. This should only be set if its value changed<br> since the last time recorded on the workflow (or be set on the first task).|

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|

|scheduledEventId|string|false|none|The id of the `WORKFLOW_TASK_SCHEDULED` event this task corresponds to|
|identity|string|false|none|Identity of the worker who picked up this task|
|requestId|string|false|none|This field is populated from the RecordWorkflowTaskStartedRequest. Matching service would<br> set the request_id on the RecordWorkflowTaskStartedRequest to a new UUID. This is useful<br> in case a RecordWorkflowTaskStarted call succeed but matching doesn't get that response,<br> so matching could retry and history service would return success if the request_id matches.<br> In that case, matching will continue to deliver the task to worker. Without this field, history<br> service would return AlreadyStarted error, and matching would drop the task.|
|suggestContinueAsNew|boolean|false|none|True if this workflow should continue-as-new soon. See `suggest_continue_as_new_reasons` for why.|
|suggestContinueAsNewReasons|[string(enum)]|false|none|The reason(s) that suggest_continue_as_new is true, if it is.<br> Unset if suggest_continue_as_new is false.|
|targetWorkerDeploymentVersionChanged|boolean|false|none|True if Workflow's Target Worker Deployment Version is different from its Pinned Version and<br> the workflow is Pinned.<br> Experimental.|
|historySizeBytes|string|false|none|Total history size in bytes, which the workflow might use to decide when to<br> continue-as-new regardless of the suggestion. Note that history event count is<br> just the event id of this event, so we don't include it explicitly here.|
|workerVersion|object|false|none|Version info of the worker to whom this task was dispatched.<br> Deprecated. This field should be cleaned up when versioning-2 API is removed. [cleanup-experimental-wv]|
|buildIdRedirectCounter|string|false|none|Used by server internally to properly reapply build ID redirects to an execution<br> when rebuilding it from events.<br> Deprecated. This field should be cleaned up when versioning-2 API is removed. [cleanup-experimental-wv]|
